monsters.name: Achaiyerai
monsters.attacks: 1 bite (1d10 piercing) and 2 claws (1d8 slashing), or just 2 claws (1d8 slashing)
monsters.description: Though not strictly demons, achaiyerai are native to the Abyss. They are about 16ft tall and look like giant flightless birds with short necks and four legs.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (35%): Any magic spell or effect has a 35% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect.
sections.Special Features: Height Advantage. Creatures less than 8ft tall that aren’t flying can only attack the achaiyerai‘s body with missile weapons, spears, or pole arms. With hand weapons they can only attack its legs. Special Body-Type. The achaiyerai’s relatively-unprotected body is AC 8[12] and has 10 hit dice. Its legs are AC -1[21]. If a leg suffers a total of 15 hit points of damage it is unusable, and the bird falls if two legs are unusable. Limited Reach. Because of its stilt legs, the achaiyerai can only use its bite attack (1d10 damage) against a target that’s more than 8ft tall or a target that’s flying.
sections.Special Attacks: Toxic Cloud. The achaiyerai can use this power once per day, and regains its use at dawn. The achaiyerai can emit an opaque, toxic cloud in a 20ft diameter sphere. Creatures within this cloud suffer no ill effects if they’re achaiyerai, if they’re immune to poison, or if they don’t need to breathe. Otherwise they take 2d6 hp of damage, and must attempt a saving throw vs poison. Creatures that fail this saving throw are feebleminded (as the 7th level druidic spell) for three hours. Unarmed Combat. Achaiyerai cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.
sections.Languages: Achaiyerai have their own tongue, and all speak Abyssal, the lingua franca of the Abyss. Some learn other languages.

monsters.name: Aerial servant
monsters.description: Aerial servants are creatures from the Elemental Plane of Air, sometimes met on the ethereal or astral planes (where they are visible), but more often met when conjured by the divine spell aerial servant. On the Prime Material Plane, aerial servants are invisible. These beings are very strong and can carry 1,000 lbs without being encumbered. If a summoned aerial servant can’t carry out its mission, it will go back to the cleric who summoned it and attack them.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: The Aerial servant surprises opponents on 1-4 on 1d6.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magical Phenomenon. The aerial servant doesn’t need to eat, drink, sleep, or breathe. Magic can’t put it to sleep. Gases can’t harm it, and it is immune to poison and disease. Immune to Mundane Weapons. The aerial servant is immune to piercing, blunt, or cutting damage, unless the weapon causing that damage is magical.
sections.Special Features: Compressible. The aerial servant can fit through a gap one inch wide. It can’t be restrained and isn’t affected by being prone. Invisible. While on the Prime Material Plane, the aerial servant is invisible. Unarmed Combat. Aerial servants cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.
sections.Languages: Aerial servants can’t talk and don’t speak languages, but the divine spell Aerial Servant enables the creature to understand its summoner’s commands.

monsters.name: Animated object, small object
monsters.armour_class: Depends on material but for example, 7 [13] if wood; 5 [15] if stone; 4 [16] if metal
monsters.description: In medieval Arabic literature, Al-Mi’raj (or just Mi’Raj) are yellow hares with black horns, like miniature unicorn horns. In OSRIC they are fey creatures that live in temperate and subtropical woodlands. Their horns are useful to alchemists, and some wizards use wands made of Al-Mi’raj horns.

sections.Languages: None. have to use their discretion for most of these; for example, some best treated as large creatures. Animated objects are temporary creatures created by the level 6 Cleric spell animate object. The animated object magically understands its creator’s spoken commands, no matter what language its creator is speaking. It doesn’t understand anyone else.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immunities. Animated objects are immune to blindness, psychic damage, charm, domination, sleep, gases, poison, and disease.
sections.Special Attacks: Unarmed Combat. Some animated objects might be able to choose to overbear or grapple instead of making a regular melee attack. Because they vary in shape and size, pre-calculated stats for unarmed attacks will vary.

monsters.name: Ankheg
monsters.description: 3 HD: 65 +2/hp 4 HD: 105 +3/hp 5 HD: 155 +4/hp 6 HD: 230 +6/hp 7 HD: 345 +8/hp 8 HD: 550 +10/hp Ankhegs are giant, burrowing arthropods with chitinous shells. These predators resemble a horrible mixture of grasshopper and lobster, but they are eight feet or more in length. To make matters worse, they can spit digestive acid. Ankhegs often lurk underground waiting to feel the vibrations of an approaching creature, then attack it by surprise.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. A burrowed-in ankheg surprises on a roll of 1-3 on a d6. This is not an original rule of the game, but matches the original text description.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Many-legged. An ankheg cannot be knocked prone, overborne, or grappled.
sections.Special Attacks: Spit Acid. The ankheg can spit its digestive acid at one target within 30ft of it. It must make an attack roll against that target. If it hits, the target takes 4d8 corrosion damage. Whether it hits or misses, the ankheg can’t use this attack again for 12 hours. Unarmed Combat. Ankhegs can choose to overbear instead of making a regular melee attack. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +5/NA. Grappling attacker/ defender modifier: NA/NA. They cannot be overborne or grappled.
sections.Languages: None.

monsters.name: Annis hag
monsters.senses: Infravision 60ft, Detect invisible 5%, and Illusion sense
monsters.description: When an evil fey abducts the infant daughter of giants or ogres, they can raise it as an annis hag. Annis hags have a variable creature type—some are giants, others fey. They are carnivorous and suffer from constant, gnawing hunger, which they can temporarily relieve by devouring a human, demi-human or humanoid.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Illusion Sense. Annis hags are never fooled by illusion magic.
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. Annis hags can cast each of the following spells, without material components: 3/day: Change self (Illusionist 1) 3/day: Fog cloud (Illusionist 2)
sections.Special Attacks: Melee Attack: Seize and Devour. Seizing: When both of an annis hag’s claw attacks hit the same target, and the target’s size is medium or smaller, the target is seized. The seize ends when the creature escapes, when either the annis or the seized creature is killed, or when something moves the seized creature such that it’s no longer within 5ft of the annis. • While it’s seized, the seized creature can’t attack, move, or use its arms and legs. When the annis moves, the seized creature moves with it. The annis’ movement speed is halved while it’s seized a creature. Each annis can only seize one creature at a time, and two or more annis can’t seize the same creature. • A creature that’s seized can try to escape on its i nitiative. It attempts a Major Test of Strength. If the creature passes, then it escapes the annis. It can then choose to move up to its speed away from the annis, but it can’t take any other action that round. If it fails, then it remains seized and can’t take any other action that round. • Other creatures can help the seized creature to escape by attempting a Major Test of Strength. If they pass, they wrestle the creature away from the annis, so the creature is no longer seized. They can’t take any other action that round. If they fail, then the seized creature remains seized and the other creature can’t take any other action that round. Devouring. If the annis has seized a creature, then on its initiative in the next round, instead of attacking, the annis can devour the creature it has seized. The creature takes 3d8+3 piercing damage (no saving throw). If this damage kills the creature, then the devoured creature is no longer seized but inside the annis’ belly. The annis digests the corpse 1d3 rounds later. A digested corpse can’t be raised. Unarmed Combat. Annis hags can choose to overbear instead of making a regular melee attack. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/- 10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2. They do not employ grappling tactics.
sections.Languages: Annis speak common, and the tongue of the fey that raised them. Most also speak various giantish tongues, which can include the languages of ogres, ettins, and/or trolls.

monsters.name: Ant, giant, worker
monsters.description: Giant ants are a dangerous threat to dungeon adventurers, but they can also be encountered above ground. The population of a giant ant colony is determined by rolling for the number of workers (1d100). There will also be one soldier for each five workers (round fractions up). The queen can’t move or fight, and lives at the heart of the colony. It takes twelve workers to carry her, moving at 30ft. If the queen’s chamber is invaded, twelve workers will try to carry her to safety while the rest of the colony (workers and soldiers alike) attacks the intruders. If the queen is killed, the entire colony will be confused (as the 7th level druidic spell) for 1d6 rounds. They will then leave the colony in search of a new one.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Many-legged. A giant ant cannot be knocked prone, overborne, or grappled.
sections.Special Features: Climber. Giant ants can move on walls and ceilings as if they were floors.
sections.Special Attacks: Melee Attack: Poison (Soldiers only). Anyone bitten by a soldier ant will take 3d4 hit points of damage from poison in addition to the piercing damage unless they succeed at a saving throw vs poison, in which case the poison damage is 1d4 hit points. Unarmed Combat. Giant ants cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.
sections.Languages: None.

monsters.name: Ape, gorilla
monsters.description: GORILLA Wild gorillas live in remote places and usually avoid conflict.

sections.Special Attacks: Mangle. When both of the gorilla’s fist attacks make a successful hit against the same target, the gorilla automatically inflicts an additional 1d6 points of blunt damage from mangling the target. The target is not held or immobilised by this, and can continue to act normally in combat. Ranged Attack. Gorillas can throw rocks for 1d6 blunt damage. The range increment is 20ft (-2 beyond 20ft, -4 beyond 40ft). Unarmed Combat. Gorillas can choose to overbear instead of making a regular melee attack. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. Mangle. When both of the carnivorous ape’s fist attacks make a successful hit against the same target, the carnivorous ape automatically inflicts an additional 1d8 points of blunt damage from mangling the target. The target is not held or immobilised by this, and can continue to act normally in combat. Ranged Attack. Carnivorous apes can throw rocks for 1d8 blunt damage. The range increment is 20ft (-2 beyond 20ft, -4 beyond 40ft). Unarmed Combat. Carnivorous apes can choose to overbear instead of making a regular melee attack. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +3/-3. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2. Trample. On its move, as a charge, or as part of a move into combat, the giant ape can tread on any creature smaller than size Huge. If the smaller creature can move and isn’t prone, then it can immediately (during the giant ape’s turn) choose to move to an unoccupied space within 5ft of it. This 5ft move doesn’t cost the smaller creature any of its movement. If the smaller creature is prone, can’t move for any other reason, or if there’s no unoccupied space within 5ft of it, then the smaller creature takes 3d6+12 blunt damage as the giant ape treads on it. This doesn’t count as one of the giant ape’s attacks; it is just part of movement. Melee Attack: Grasp and Squeeze. Grasp: When one of the giant ape’s fists attacks hits a target, and the giant ape’s attack roll is 4 or more higher than the minimum it would need to hit the creature, the target is grasped if its size is large or smaller. The grasp ends when the creature escapes, when either the giant ape or the grasped creature is killed, or when something moves the grasped creature such that it’s no longer within 5ft of the giant ape. • While it’s grasped, the seized creature can’t attack, move, or use its arms and legs. When the giant ape moves, the grasped creature moves with it. The giant ape’s movement speed isn’t affected by seizing creatures. Each giant ape can only grasp one creature in each fist at a time, and two or more giant apes can’t grasp the same creature. • A creature that’s grasped can try to escape on its i nitiative. It attempts a Major Test of Strength. If the creature passes, then it escapes the giant ape. It can then choose to move up to its speed away from the giant ape, but it can’t take any other action that round. If it fails, then it remains grasped and can’t take any other action that round. • Other creatures can help the grasped creature to escape by attempting a Major Test of Strength. If they pass, they wrestle the creature away from the giant ape, so the creature is no longer grasped. They can’t take any other action that round. If they fail, then the grasped creature remains grasped and the other creature can’t take any other action that round. Squeeze: If the giant ape has grasped a creature, then on its initiative, instead of one fist attack, the giant ape can squeeze the creature it’s grasped. The creature takes 3d6+12 points of blunt damage. The giant ape can then choose whether to keep the creature grasped, or to drop it, ending the grasp. A dropped creature takes 3d6 blunt damage from the fall. It must then attempt a saving throw vs death, and must add its Dexterity saving throw modifier to this saving throw. If it fails, it lands prone. Range Attack: Throw Tree. If the giant ape doesn’t have any creatures grasped, then instead of all its attacks, it can throw a nearby tree or boulder. It can uproot a tree or lift a boulder as part of this action. The giant ape then throws the tree or boulder at a point within 180ft of it that it can see. Each creature within 5ft of that point (either scale) must attempt a saving throw vs death and must add its Dexterity saving throw modifier to this saving throw. If it fails this saving throw, it takes 2d6+12 points of blunt damage. Stomp. Instead of using its bite attack in combat, the giant ape can choose to stomp. When it does so, it jumps with both feet, and lands, making the ground shake. Creatures within 10ft of the giant ape must attempt a saving throw vs death, and must add their Dexterity saving throw modifier to this saving throw. If they’re flying, they automatically pass this saving throw. If they fail, they fall prone (they don’t die; death is just the saving throw category used). Unarmed Combat. Giant apes cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.
sections.Languages: Usually none. In some campaigns there may exist colonies of Awakened Apes that speak either their own language or Common, wear simple clothes, and use simple tools and weapons. CARNIVOROUS APE OSRIC’s source literature has a tradition of aggressive ape-like creatures, such as the White Apes of Barsoom or Thak in Robert E. Howard’s Rogues in the House. In OSRIC, certain humanoids, and particularly hobgoblins, form alliances with carnivorous apes and share lairs with them. The carnivorous ape doesn’t speak any languages, but may understand a few simple words in a human or humanoid language. GIANT APE The giant ape is enormous: King Kong scale. The giant ape doesn’t speak any languages, but may understand a few simple words in a human or humanoid language.

When the giant ape moves, the grasped creature moves with it. The giant ape’s movement speed isn’t affected by seizing creatures. Each giant ape can only grasp one creature in each fist at a time, and two or more giant apes can’t grasp the same creature. • A creature that’s grasped can try to escape on its i nitiative. It attempts a Major Test of Strength. If the creature passes, then it escapes the giant ape. It can then choose to move up to its speed away from the giant ape, but it can’t take any other action that round. If it fails, then it remains grasped and can’t take any other action that round. • Other creatures can help the grasped creature to escape by attempting a Major Test of Strength. If they pass, they wrestle the creature away from the giant ape, so the creature is no longer grasped. They can’t take any other action that round. If they fail, then the grasped creature remains grasped and the other creature can’t take any other action that round. Squeeze: If the giant ape has grasped a creature, then on its initiative, instead of one fist attack, the giant ape can squeeze the creature it’s grasped. The creature takes 3d6+12 points of blunt damage. The giant ape can then choose whether to keep the creature grasped, or to drop it, ending the grasp. A dropped creature takes 3d6 blunt damage from the fall. It must then attempt a saving throw vs death, and must add its Dexterity saving throw modifier to this saving throw. If it fails, it lands prone. Range Attack: Throw Tree. If the giant ape doesn’t have any creatures grasped, then instead of all its attacks, it can throw a nearby tree or boulder. It can uproot a tree or lift a boulder as part of this action. The giant ape then throws the tree or boulder at a point within 180ft of it that it can see. Each creature within 5ft of that point (either scale) must attempt a saving throw vs death and must add its Dexterity saving throw modifier to this saving throw. If it fails this saving throw, it takes 2d6+12 points of blunt damage. Stomp. Instead of using its bite attack in combat, the giant ape can choose to stomp. When it does so, it jumps with both feet, and lands, making the ground shake. Creatures within 10ft of the giant ape must attempt a saving throw vs death, and must add their Dexterity saving throw modifier to this saving throw. If they’re flying, they automatically pass this saving throw. If they fail, they fall prone (they don’t die; death is just the saving throw category used). Unarmed Combat. Giant apes cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.
sections.Languages: Usually none. In some campaigns there may exist colonies of Awakened Apes that speak either their own language or Common, wear simple clothes, and use simple tools and weapons. CARNIVOROUS APE OSRIC’s source literature has a tradition of aggressive ape-like creatures, such as the White Apes of Barsoom or Thak in Robert E. Howard’s Rogues in the House. In OSRIC, certain humanoids, and particularly hobgoblins, form alliances with carnivorous apes and share lairs with them. The carnivorous ape doesn’t speak any languages, but may understand a few simple words in a human or humanoid language. GIANT APE The giant ape is enormous: King Kong scale. The giant ape doesn’t speak any languages, but may understand a few simple words in a human or humanoid language.

monsters.name: Aurumvorax
monsters.description: Also known as the “golden gorger” for its beautiful fur coat, the aurumvorax is a long-bodied, eight-legged carnivore. It lives in plains or woods. Though as small as a badger, the creature is very dense and heavy, and weighs as much as a bear.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune (gas and poison): The aurumvorax is immune to gases and poison. Resistant (blunt and fire): The creature takes only half damage from blunt weapons and fire damage (round down). Many-legged. This creature cannot be knocked prone, overborne, or grappled.
sections.Special Features: This small creature is very heavy (600 pounds).
sections.Special Attacks: Melee Attack: Jaw Lock and Rake. Jaw Lock: When the aurumvorax’s bite hits, it locks its jaws in the target’s flesh. (If you are using a grid, it is in the target’s square). If the target moves, it has to pull the aurumvorax with it, and since the aurumvorax weighs 600 pounds, this is unlikely. Until the jaw lock ends, the aurumvorax can’t bite or lock onto another target. On its initiative, the aurumvorax can choose to release its target (in a grid, it moves to an unoccupied space within 5ft) and can take another action. • A creature the aurumvorax is locked onto can try to escape on its i nitiative. It attempts a Major Test of Strength. If the creature succeeds at the test, it takes 2d4 piercing damage as it pulls the aurumvorax off itself. The jaw lock ends, and the creature can then choose to move up to its speed away from the aurumvorax, but it can’t take any other action that round. If it fails, then the aurumvorax remains locked on and its target can’t take any other action that round. • Other creatures can help the creature locked onto to escape by attempting a Major Test of Strength. If they pass, they wrestle the creature away from the aurumvorax, so the aurumvorax is no longer locked on. The creature rescuing can’t take any other action that round. If the creature rescuing fails, then the aurumvorax remains locked on and the creature rescuing can’t take any other action that round. Rake: If the aurumvorax is locked onto a creature, then instead of attacking, it can rake the creature it’s locked onto. When it does so, the aurumvorax’s target automatically takes 2d4 piercing damage from the aurumvorax’s jaws, and the aurumvorax rakes it, attacking with 2d4 of its claws. Each claw inflicts 1d6 slashing damage (a successful to-hit roll is required). Unarmed Combat. Aurumvoraxes cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.
sections.Languages: None.

monsters.name: Axe beak (phorusrhacid)
monsters.description: These ostrich-like birds run fast, and attack prey with their immensely strong beaks. They are usually found in Lost World types of settings, but some cultures or monsters may have learned how to domesticate them as mounts for battle. Unarmed Combat. Axe beaks do not initiate unarmed combat unless they are trained mounts, and cannot be grappled. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +2/- 2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -/-.

monsters.name: Azer
monsters.description: Azer are elementals from the elemental plane of fire. They look like dwarfs with flames for hair and brass-coloured skin. In that plane of existence, azers may be encountered in much larger numbers than shown here.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Fire. The azer ignores fire damage. Resistant to Poison. When the azer takes poison damage, this damage is halved. Round fractions down. Vulnerable to Cold. When the azer takes cold damage, this damage is doubled.
sections.Special Features: Burning. When you hit the azer with a melee attack while standing within 5ft of it, you take 1d3 fire damage. Glowing. The azer sheds light in a 40ft radius.
sections.Special Attacks: Melee Attack: Burning. When the azer hits you with a melee attack, you take an extra 1d3 fire damage. Ranged Attack. 1 spear (1d6+2 piercing); 30ft range increment (-2 beyond 30ft, -4 beyond 60ft). Unarmed Combat. Azers can choose to overbear or grapple instead of making a regular melee attack. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with an 18+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-14. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.
sections.Languages: Azer have their own language, and also speak Ignan, the lingua franca of the Elemental Plane of Fire.

monsters.name: Babbler
monsters.description: Babblers are intelligent, lizard-like creatures that resemble a small allosaurus with long arms. They are usually found in swamps, fens, and marshes. Babblers particularly like the taste of human flesh. Babblers share their habitat with lizardfolk and may be distantly related to them. Some sages think they’re former lizardfolk transformed by a curse. In any event, they are sometimes found accompanying lizardfolk raiding parties, and sometimes found eating lizardfolk. Since no one can understand the language of babblers, there’s no way of knowing the motivations involved.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Hold Breath. This creature can go for up to an hour between breaths.
sections.Special Features: Swamp Stealth. While motionless in marsh or swamp terrain, the babbler has a 30% chance to become completely invisible, as if hiding in shadows. Unarmed Combat. Babblers can choose to overbear instead of making a regular melee attack, but cannot grapple or be grappled. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/ DEF +2/-2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -/-.
sections.Languages: Babblers vocalise constantly, unless they’re asleep or hiding. They emit a constant stream of noises that sound like language, but magic doesn’t translate the sounds, and nobody has ever learned their tongue. They never speak intelligibly. Babblers can usually understand the languages of lizardfolk, although they can’t speak it.

monsters.name: Baboon
monsters.description: Baboons are communal, omnivorous creatures found in warmer climes. They live in troops. Baboons sometimes enter houses to steal food, or raid farms to take goats or swine. They tend to flee from serious resistance. Unarmed Combat. Baboons can choose to overbear instead of making a regular melee attack, and can be grappled. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2.

monsters.name: Badger, ordinary
monsters.description: Swift-moving burrowers, badgers will defend their territory to the death. They mate for life, and when more than one is indicated, the encounter will be with a family. Adult badger pelts will usually bring 1d3×10 gold each, and juvenile pelts are worth one-half normal. The giant badger is simply a larger version of the regular badger. They are very rare, even in badger-rich areas, but may be encountered in prehistoric “lost world” environments. Their pelts are worth 1d3 x20 gold each. Unarmed Combat. Badgers cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

sections.Language: Depending on the world setting, some unusual badgers (both ordinary and giant) may be related to the fey, in which case they can speak common and/or fey.

monsters.name: Badger, giant
monsters.description: Swift-moving burrowers, badgers will defend their territory to the death. They mate for life, and when more than one is indicated, the encounter will be with a family. Adult badger pelts will usually bring 1d3×10 gold each, and juvenile pelts are worth one-half normal. The giant badger is simply a larger version of the regular badger. They are very rare, even in badger-rich areas, but may be encountered in prehistoric “lost world” environments. Their pelts are worth 1d3 x20 gold each. Unarmed Combat. Badgers cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

sections.Language: Depending on the world setting, some unusual badgers (both ordinary and giant) may be related to the fey, in which case they can speak common and/or fey.

monsters.name: Banshee (groaning spirit)
monsters.description: The banshee is often said to be the ghost of an evil elven woman, although many have been encountered who don’t really appear to fit this description. These spirits are found in remote countryside and other lonely natural places. They are mostly incorporeal, and float just above the ground, but they cannot fly.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Turned as Undead. Banshees are turned as type 13 Undead. Magic Resistance (50%). Any magic spell or effect has a 50% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immune to Mundane Weapons. The banshee is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage, unless the weapon causing that damage is magical. Immunities. This creature is immune to mind control (including charm) and hold spells, sleep, gases, poison, disease, cold damage, electrical damage, temporary damage, and subdual damage. Vulnerability to Exorcism. An exorcism spell immediately kills the creature.
sections.Special Features: Fearful Appearance. The mere sight of a banshee will cause fear (as the level 3 illusionist spell) unless the viewer saves vs spells (one saving throw, not an ongoing series). Fighting the creature without looking at it incurs a to-hit penalty of -4.
sections.Special Attacks: Wail (1/day). The banshee can wail only when it is dark. All creatures within 30ft of the banshee when it wails must save versus spells or die. Unarmed Combat. Banshees cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Barracuda
monsters.description: 2HD: 30 +1/hp 3HD: 50 +2/hp The barracuda is a fearsome, very fast aquatic predator. The natural habitat of this fish is warm salt water. It prefers vulnerable or wounded prey, especially those smaller than itself.

monsters.name: Basilisk
monsters.description: The basilisk is an eight-legged, reptilian creature with baleful eyes and a deadly gaze.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Reflected Gaze. The basilisk is vulnerable to its own reflected gaze. If confronted with a reflective surface, it must make a saving throw vs petrifaction (with a bonus of +4) or be turned to stone.
sections.Special Features: Petrifying Gaze. Any creature meeting the gaze of a basilisk must successfully save vs petrifaction or instantly be turned to stone (save each time the gaze is met). The gaze effects of the basilisk extend into both the astral and ethereal planes. This applies to anyone who is generally in front of the basilisk, and not using an indirect method of sight such as a mirror. Attacking the creature by looking at a reflection incurs a to-hit penalty of -2. Attacking blindly incurs a to-hit penalty of -4. Unarmed Combat. Basilisks cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Bat, ordinary
monsters.description: ORDINARY BATS This listing includes all types of normal bats. They will only attack when trapped, seeking to escape. When startled, they will swarm, causing confusion, extinguishing torches, etc.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Echolocator. Sight isn’t this creature’s primary sense. Silence affects it in the same way that darkness affects sighted creatures. Invisible opponents are detected and may be attacked without any penalty. Echolocator. Sight isn’t this creature’s primary sense. Silence affects it in the same way that darkness affects sighted creatures. Invisible opponents are detected and may be attacked without any penalty.
sections.Special Attacks: Bat Swarm. If more than 5 bats are startled and swarm, they cause confusion, extinguish torches, and can interrupt spell casting. Every 5 bats in the swarm occupies an area of about 10x10ft. Any person in the area must make a saving throw vs. petrifaction or be affected in some way by the bats, in the following order: (1) an open flame carried by the character is extinguished, (2) if the character is not carrying an open flame but is casting a spell, the spell is lost, (3) if the character is neither carrying an open flame nor casting a spell, the character is confused and cannot take actions for 1d4 rounds. GIANT BATS These are giant versions of carnivorous ordinary bats. Their bodies grow up to 3ft long, and they can have wingspans of up to 6ft. Disease. There is a 1% chance that anyone bitten will contract rabies, or some similar blood-borne infection.
sections.Special Features: Highly Manoeuvrable. Users of missile weapons will suffer a -3 “to hit” penalty unless the attacker’s dexterity is 13 or higher. Giant bats must land on their intended victims to attack, losing this benefit when they do so.

monsters.name: Bat, mobat
monsters.description: 6HD: 300 +6/hp The very large mobat is found in warm regions where a plentiful supply of warm-blooded prey is available. These evil creatures may work with other evil species of any kind that can communicate with them.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise Attack. Mobats surprise opponents on a 1-3 (on 1d6).
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Echolocator. Sight isn’t this creature’s primary sense. Silence affects it in the same way that darkness affects sighted creatures.
sections.Special Features: Armour Class. When mobats are airborne their AC is 2 [18], but when grounded or attacking their AC is 10 [10].
sections.Special Attacks: Shriek. Mobats can emit a terrifying shriek. If a saving throw vs paralysis is failed, the victims (all within a 20ft radius) are forced to cover their ears, and are thus rendered defenceless. The mobat can do this in any round, but cannot shriek and attack in the same round.
sections.Language: Mobats do not have a language other than the neutral evil alignment speech. They can (and do) cooperate with other evil creatures—on a disorganised basis if there is no communication, or in more organised fashion if they can communicate by alignment tongue or by spells.

monsters.name: Batrachian
monsters.attacks: 1 spear (1d6 + poison) or 1 bite (1d4+1) and 2 claws (1d2)
monsters.loot: Individual 1, 2, 4 each; in lair, Cache 3 (x5) and 10% chance of any 2 magic items
monsters.description: points (1) Batrachians are humanoid frog-people of several different varieties. advanced batrachian species/cultures use javelins, spears (or harpoons) armour. There is a 25% chance that batrachians will have 2d4 giant frogs sonous giant frogs (25%) in their lair. Advanced batrachians with poisonous ant frogs available may (50% chance) have anointed their spears with poison. Batrachian tadpoles spend most of their time in water, and usually large, central pool, but they can emerge and fight if threatened. Rumours persist of batrachian ghouls, which may be under a tribal witch-crafter’s command. If 30 or more batrachians are encountered at once, there will be chian leaders with 2 HD. These larger batrachians have a strength +1 to damage. Batrachians can have witch-priests (maximum of 5th level) or witch-crafters (maximum of 5th/4th level).

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Hold Breath. This creature can go for up to an hour between breaths.
sections.Special Features: Ambush. Batrachians are well-camouflaged and can remain motionless for long periods. They are also cold-blooded and hence hard to see with infravision. As a result, they surprise opponents on a 1-3, and on a 1-5 if hopping. Clumsy. If not armed with a long weapon like a spear or harpoon, a batrachian will always lose 150ft initiative due to its clumsy movements on land.
sections.Special Attacks: Hop. A hop counts as a charge, with an additional +1 “to hit” bonus with a weapon. A batrachian making a hop attack with a spear or harpoon inflicts double damage. Ranged Attack. Adult batrachians can attack with javelins. 1 javelin (1d6 piercing). Range increment 20ft (-2 at 21+ft, -4 at 41+ft). Unarmed Combat. Batrachians can choose to overbear or grapple instead of making a regular melee attack. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20 (6+ if wearing armour). Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2. monsters.name: Bear, lesser, black
monsters.description: BLACK BEAR Of all bears, the black bear is the least aggressive. If attacked, they will defend themselves and their cubs. The black bear is omnivorous and possesses good hearing and smell, but has weak vision.

sections.Special Attacks: Melee Attack: Bear Hug. Any claw attack with a to-hit roll of 18 or more results in the target being hugged for an additional 2d4 hit points. Unarmed Combat. Black bears cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics. BROWN BEAR The brown bear, of which the grizzly is the most famous, is an aggressive strain of bear. Like black bears, they are omnivorous and possess good hearing and smell, but have weak vision. Melee Attack: Bear Hug. Any claw attack with a to-hit roll of 18 or more results in the target being hugged for an additional 2d6 hit points. Unarmed Combat. Brown bears may attempt to overbear a lone opponent, and can (technically) grapple and be grappled. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +5/-5. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Death Stamina. If reduced to zero hit points, the brown bear will continue to fight until either 1d4 rounds have elapsed or it is reduced to -9 hit points.

CAVE BEAR The cave bear, a giant relic of past ages, is particularly carnivorous, in contrast to its more omnivorous relatives.

monsters.name: Bee, giant (honeybee), worker
monsters.description: Giant honeybees live in hives. These lairs will contain non-combatant queens (10 HD but no effective attack) and 2d3 non-combatant drones (2 HD and no effective attack). Giant honeybees will flee from smoke or fire unless their lair is threatened. Giant bee hives will always contain honey worth 10d10 gold pieces. There is a 15% chance that a hive will contain royal jelly. If it does, the royal jelly can be fashioned into 2d3 potions of extra healing by a magic-user of 7th or higher level—or a magic-user of 12th level or higher may make it into an unguent which preserves the appearance of youth. Regular application of this unguent for 1 year makes the user appear 2d3 years younger. Such an unguent is typically worth 3d6x1,000 gp to wealthy nobles.

sections.Special Attacks: One Poison Sting. A giant bee can only sting once per encounter; it has a 25% chance of dying after stinging, otherwise the stinger will slowly regrow. The sting is poisonous; if it hits, the target must make a saving throw vs. poison or take additional points of poison damage. For worker bees the saving throw is made with no penalty and the additional damage is 2d4. For soldier bees, the saving throw is made at a -1 penalty and the additional damage is 5d4.

monsters.name: Bee, giant (honeybee), soldier
monsters.description: Giant honeybees live in hives. These lairs will contain non-combatant queens (10 HD but no effective attack) and 2d3 non-combatant drones (2 HD and no effective attack). Giant honeybees will flee from smoke or fire unless their lair is threatened. Giant bee hives will always contain honey worth 10d10 gold pieces. There is a 15% chance that a hive will contain royal jelly. If it does, the royal jelly can be fashioned into 2d3 potions of extra healing by a magic-user of 7th or higher level—or a magic-user of 12th level or higher may make it into an unguent which preserves the appearance of youth. Regular application of this unguent for 1 year makes the user appear 2d3 years younger. Such an unguent is typically worth 3d6x1,000 gp to wealthy nobles.

sections.Special Attacks: One Poison Sting. A giant bee can only sting once per encounter; it has a 25% chance of dying after stinging, otherwise the stinger will slowly regrow. The sting is poisonous; if it hits, the target must make a saving throw vs. poison or take additional points of poison damage. For worker bees the saving throw is made with no penalty and the additional damage is 2d4. For soldier bees, the saving throw is made at a -1 penalty and the additional damage is 5d4.

monsters.name: Bee, giant (bumblebee)
monsters.description: Giant bumblebees live in nests rather than hives. These lairs will contain combatant queens and 2d3 non-combatant drones (2 HD and no effective attack). Giant bumblebees will flee from smoke or fire unless their lair is threatened. Giant bumblebee nests will always contain honey worth 10d10 gold pieces. There is a 15% chance that a hive will contain royal jelly. If it does, the royal jelly can be fashioned into 2d3 potions of extra healing by a magic-user of 7th or higher level—or a magic-user of 12th level or higher may make it into an unguent which preserves the appearance of youth. Regular application of this unguent for 1 year makes the user appear 2d3 years younger. Such an unguent is typically worth 3d6x1,000 gp to wealthy nobles.

sections.Special Attacks: Bumblebee Sting. A giant bumblebee can only sting once per encounter; it has a 25% chance of dying after stinging, otherwise the stinger will slowly regrow. Queens do not die from stinging, but still lose the stinger. The sting is poisonous; if it hits, the target must make a saving throw vs. poison with a -1 penalty or take 5d4 additional points of poison damage.

monsters.name: Beetles, giant, fire beetle
monsters.description: SMALL Unarmed Combat. Giant beetles cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics. GIANT FIRE BEETLE With their glowing red glands, one above each eye and one on the back of the abdomen, these nocturnal beetles are much sought after by adventurers. Fire beetles can be found both above and below ground, feeding on decaying matter like all beetles. LARGE

sections.Special Features: The glands will continue to glow for 1d6 days after removal, illuminating a 10ft radius without fail. GIANT BOMBARDIER BEETLE Frequently found in forested regions, this beetle primarily scavenges for food above ground. It will collect decaying matter into a large heap and there lay its eggs. Hold Breath. This creature can go for up to an hour between breaths. Unusual Senses. Giant water beetles automatically detect invisible opponents because their primary senses are scent and vibration. GIANT BORING BEETLE Giant boring beetles may be found in enormous dead trees, but are usually encountered in tunnel complexes where there is sufficient rotting wood and moisture to support the fungal cultures they eat. There are rumours that some have developed a “hive-mind” similar to ants and when threatened they may display surprising group intelligence in the defence of their home. GIANT DEATH WATCH BEETLE Giant Death Watch beetles live in temperate areas and sometimes underground. They disguise themselves by sticking rubbish, branches and detritus to their carapaces with their saliva.
sections.Special Attacks: Noxious Gas. When attacked it has a 50% chance to release an 8ft cube of noxious gas. The gas will cause 3d4 hp of damage and the sound of its release will stun (20% chance) and deafen (20%) all within a cloud (5ft radius beginning directly in front of the beetle). The stun effect will prevent action for 2d4 rounds and the deafness will persist for 2d6 rounds. The beetle must “recharge” for 1 round before releasing gas again, and cannot release gas more than twice in 8 hours. GIANT WATER BEETLE Hunting by scent and vibration, and dwelling in fresh water at least 30ft deep, the water beetle is a powerful threat to the unwary adventurer. Omnivorous and insatiable, the water beetle will consume whatever it can get its powerful mandibles around. Death Vibration. These giant beetles are feared for making terrible, deadly bass vibrations by scraping their hind legs—when a beetle does this, all within 30ft of the creature must save vs death or die. Even those who pass their save take 4d6 hp damage. After using this special attack, the Death Watch beetle must wait at least 12 turns before using it again. GIANT RHINOCEROS BEETLE Usually encountered in the tropics, these massive creatures (roughly 12ft long, plus another 6ft of horn) live on the fruit and vegetation they crush as they roam about.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Many-legged. This creature cannot be knocked prone, overborne, or grappled. Many-legged. This creature cannot be knocked prone, overborne, or grappled. GIANT STAG BEETLE Giant stag beetles live in woodlands near farmland, preferring for food the young shoots of cultivated grains. For this reason, they can often plague regions and even cause famine should enough of them descend upon an area. They attack with a bite and with their two horns. Many-legged. This creature cannot be knocked prone, overborne, or grappled.

monsters.name: Behir
monsters.description: A behir is a particularly nasty subterranean beast with a crocodile-like head on a 40ft long, snake-like body with twelve sets of legs. Since behirs swallow prey whole, the beast’s stomach will contain 10d4 gems (60% chance), 1d8 jewellery (30% chance), and a misc. magic item that can survive its digestive juices (10% chance).

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immunities. The behir is immune to electricity damage and poison. Many-legged. This creature cannot be knocked prone, overborne, or grappled, and does not employ unarmed combat tactics.
sections.Special Features: Climber. This creature can move on walls and ceilings as if they were floors, but moves at half speed when doing so.
sections.Special Attacks: Lightning Breath. Every 10 rounds a behir can also breathe a 20ft lightning bolt that does 4d6+24 damage unless a save vs breath is made for half damage. Swallow Whole. On a bite attack that rolls a natural 20, the behir swallows the victim. If the victim is not rescued, they will die at the end of 6 rounds spent in the creature’s stomach. It is possible for the victim to cut their way out (the inside of the behir is armour class 10 [10]). For each round the victim is inside, subtract 1 from their damage that they inflict. This penalty is cumulative for each round, so after four rounds the damage inflicted is at -4. Bite and Claw. The behir’s first attack is a bite, but if it hits with this attack it can coil around the victim and bring its claws into play. On the second round after a successful bite, the behir can make an additional 6 claw attacks against the victim. The victim is held in place, but can continue to act (other than moving); the behir’s attacks do not shift to automatic damage; it must still make to-hit rolls to inflict damage, although it can now make a lot more attacks.
sections.Language: Behirs only speak the alignment tongue of neutral evil.

monsters.name: Bird of prey, normal
monsters.description: NORMAL BIRDS OF PREY Birds of prey are found across the known world in many shapes, forms and colours. They are distinguished from one another by plumage, size, beak shape, body length, wing size and talon type, as well as by dietary habits. Most are two or three feet long, weigh up to about three pounds and have a wingspan of around four or five feet. Eagles, hawks and falcons are all examples of birds of prey. Falcons are generally the smallest of the three, tending to be around a foot in length and having a wingspan of two to three feet. Hawks are usually somewhat larger, typically being around two feet long and having a wingspan of four to five feet. Eagles can be considerably larger, sometimes exceeding even three feet in length and having a wingspan of anywhere from five to eight feet. The largest types may weigh up to twelve pounds.

sections.Special Attacks: Diving Attack (Normal). A diving attack must be made from the air at a distance of 120ft or more. It acts as a charge, and grants a +2 “to-hit” bonus and double damage from their talons. GIANT BIRDS OF PREY There is a 50% chance that randomly-encountered giant birds of prey are of a highly-intelligent variety (such as Tolkien’s giant eagles). These are similar enough to their animal-type relatives to share the rest of the physical statistics, but have higher intelligence, possibly their own culture, and may be related to the fey. Otherwise, the giant bird of prey is just a giant version of a normal bird of prey. Diving Attack (Giant). A diving attack must be made from the air at a distance of 60ft or more. It acts as a charge, and grants a +4 “to-hit” bonus and double damage from their talons.
sections.Languages: Intelligent giant birds of prey are likely to understand the common tongue, and may be able to speak it.

monsters.name: Blindheim
monsters.description: Blindheims are yellowish, frog-like monsters found in subterranean environments. They are usually bipedal, but move on all fours in rough terrain.

sections.Special Attacks: Blinding Light. These yellowish, frog-like bipeds can project twin beams of incredibly bright light from their eyes. Anyone who comes within 30ft of the blindheim must save vs aimed magic items or be temporarily blinded (for 1d8+12 turns). The saving throw is at -3 if the approaching character has infravision. A character who is not blinded may attack the blindheim at a penalty of -2 “to hit” (if they are avoiding looking at the creature) or as normal (if they are for some reason immune to bright light). Unarmed Combat. Blindheims do not employ unarmed combat but can be grappled or overborne. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF -1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2.

monsters.name: Blink dog
monsters.description: Blink dogs are medium-sized dogs, dark brown with white highlights. They are intelligent, as smart as the average human. Blink dogs are so called because they can use a limited form of teleportation, called a “blink,” in a somewhat random fashion and at random intervals. Coupled with their pack hunting tactics, blink dogs are fearsome opponents. If the pack takes more than 25% losses all will simultaneously blink out and not return. There is a long-standing hatred between blink dogs and phase cats (coeurls) and the two will attack each other on sight. Blinking is a natural ability for these animals and they will never materialise in an occupied space or within a solid object. If a blink dog lair is found there is a 60% chance of 3d4 pups. These younglings fight as 1 HD monsters and inflict 1d2 points of damage per attack, though they are far more likely to flee using their teleportation ability. A captured pup will make a loyal companion to a good aligned human, or, it can be sold for 1,500 gp (± 100–600 gp).

sections.Special Attacks: Blink. In combat (and if needed, in other situations) blink dogs use a semi-random, short-range teleportation, called a “blink.” Each round, roll to see if the blink dog uses this ability: roll 1d20, and if the result is 12 or more, the blink dog teleports to attack. A second roll of the 1d20 reveals where the dog reappears: 01–15 = behind (rear attack at +2), 16–18 = non-shielded or right flank (defender cannot use shield in this round), 19 = shielded or left flank (no benefit), 20 = front (no benefit). The blink dog blinks and attacks in the same round, gaining any bonuses based on its position relative to the target. Unarmed Combat. Blink dogs cannot be grappled or overborne, but might overbear a lone opponent. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/na. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF na/na.
sections.Language: Blink dogs communicate amongst themselves via their highpitched barks and low growls. They do not speak or understand Common.

monsters.name: Boar, wild boar
monsters.description: WILD BOAR Boars are wild pigs with tusks. They are extremely aggressive and quite dangerous. The first two boars encountered will automatically be adults; each additional boar indicated has a 75% chance of being a sounder (boar piglet). Sounders will flee from attackers, and are non-combatants.

sections.Special Features: Die Hard. Adult boars will fight for 1d4+1 rounds after reaching 0 hit points, or until -7 hit points are accumulated. Unarmed Combat. Wild boar cannot be grappled or overborne, but might overbear a lone opponent. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/na. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF na/na. GIANT BOAR Ancient ancestor to the modern boar, the giant boar is even more aggressive. They have a smaller proportion of sounders in a group: additional boars after the first two (automatic adults) have only a 25% chance of being sounders (as opposed to 75% for normal boars). Also, giant boar sounders do not flee; they are treated as ordinary adult wild boars (without the die hard ability). Die Hard (Giant Boar). Adult giant boars will fight for 1d4 rounds after reaching 0 hit points, or until -11 hit points are accumulated. Unarmed Combat. Wild boar cannot be grappled or overborne, but might overbear a lone opponent. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +3/na. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF na/na.

monsters.name: Boar, warthog
monsters.description: Tropical relatives of the common boar, warthogs will only attack if threatened or cornered. If more than two are indicated, they will consist of a mated pair and young. Young warthogs have 2 hit dice rather than 3, but are otherwise the same as adults.

sections.Special Features: Die Hard. All warthogs will fight for 1–2 rounds below 0 hit points, or to -6 hp. Unarmed Combat. Warthogs cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Brownie
monsters.description: Found in sylvan woodland, often along with fauns, unicorns and similar creatures, brownies are shy and retiring. They can sometimes be persuaded to help good-aligned creatures. They are skilled craftsmen, adept at making and repairing ordinary things, and are highly magical.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Cannot be Surprised. Thanks to their excellent senses and habitual alertness, brownies cannot be surprised.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Improved Saving Throw. Brownies are inherently lucky and strongly defended against magic, which means they make all saving throws as follows: Aimed magic items 11, Breath weapons 13, Death/Paralysis/Poison 7, Petrifaction/Polymorph 10, Spells 12. As Familiar. If a brownie is a familiar, it confers a +2 bonus on all saving throws to its character ally.
sections.Special Features: Spell-like Abilities. Brownies can cast each of the following spells, without material components: At will: Brownies may become invisible at will, provided they remain still while doing so. 1/day: confusion, continual light, dancing lights, dimension door, mending, mirror image, protection from evil, and ventriloquism. Unarmed Combat. Brownies do not employ unarmed combat but can be grappled or overborne. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/- 8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2.
sections.Language: Brownies speak their own tongue, as well as elven and halfling. They also speak sylvan, the language of other fey creatures such as spites, nymphs and dryads.

monsters.name: Bugbear
monsters.description: Bugbears are related to goblins, although they are much larger and shaggier than true goblins, with large heads and a gift for stealthiness. They can live both above and below ground, and do not have penalties for fighting in sunlight. Bugbears use a variety of weapons usually gathered from fallen opponents. These include axes, morning stars, hammers, swords, spears and missile weapons. Bugbear hunting parties (12+ creatures) always have a leader who fights as a 4 Hit Dice creature. (AC 4 [16], 22–25 hp, and do 2d8+1 damage). Within the lair there will be a chieftain and sub-chief. The chief is also a 4 Hit Dice creature with the following stats: (AC 3 [17], 28–30 hp, 2d8+2 damage). The sub-chief has the same stats as a leader (see above).

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Bugbears surprise opponents on a 1–3 on 1d6.
sections.Special Attacks: Ranged Attack. Bugbears armed with ranged weapons may use them as humans do. Unarmed Combat. Bugbears can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 12+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-2. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2.
sections.Language: Bugbears speak hobgoblin and goblin as well as chaotic evil and their own form of speech.

monsters.name: Bulette
monsters.description: Bulettes are sometimes called “land sharks” because of their habit of burrowing while the crests of their backs break the surface. Like sharks, they are huge, vicious, and always hungry. They seem to be someone’s experiment gone wrong: a turtle crossed with an armadillo with just a touch of demon thrown in. Their favourite food is horse but they will eat just about anything that moves. The only kind of meat they don’t seem to like is dwarf or elf. They have been known to dig halflings right out of their holes. Being fearless, a bulette will attack anything that moves on sight. They have been known to attack an armed party to get at the horses. When they attack, they use their vicious bite and their two front claws. Their plates are highly prized by armourers. They can be fashioned into +1 or +2 shields.

sections.Special Features: Sectioned Armour Class. Bulettes are well armoured AC -2 [22], but they have a vulnerable spot. When fighting, the bulette raises one of its back plates as a warning crest (part of the reason it is often described as a “land shark”. The area underneath the crest is unprotected, AC 6 [14]. However, an attacker must be behind the bulette in order to attack the unarmoured spot.
sections.Special Attacks: 8ft jump. When cornered or seriously wounded, a bulette will attempt to leap 8ft vertically and land directly on top of their victim, clawing with all four feet. Unarmed Combat. Bulettes cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Camel
monsters.description: An ornery beast of burden, the camel comes in two types, both of which have the same stats in game terms. The dromedary has only one hump and prefers warm climates. The bactrian camel has two humps, is adaptable to a wider range of temperatures and environments, and moves 30ft more slowly. Regardless of the type, all camels can be domesticated, can carry immense loads (up to 6,000 gp). Between 4 and 6 thousand gp, speed is reduced to half.

sections.Special Attacks: Spit. Their usual attack is a bite, but they may also spit. Spitting requires no to-hit roll, and has a 25% chance to blind the opponent for 1d3 rounds (no saving throw).

monsters.name: Carbuncle
monsters.description: Carbuncles are adorable minor agents of Chaos. They seem to be curious little animals like armadillos, and they feed on leaves and small insects. Set in the carbuncle’s head above its eyes is a large ruby (randomly-determined value of at least 500 gp). If the beast dies, any ruby attached to it shatters and cannot be reconstituted—but it can voluntarily give up its gem, in which case the gem will re-grow over a period of several months (re-roll the gem’s value each time it re-grows). The carbuncle will not normally give up its gem unless charmed or otherwise enchanted.

sections.Language: Carbuncles are empathic and communicate via a minor form of telepathy. They will approach and seek to join a party of humans or demi-humans and then try to spread discord by means of lies, bearing false witness, or betraying the party’s presence to nearby monsters.

monsters.name: Carcass creeper
monsters.description: A fearsome creature that roams around in caves and dungeons, the carcass creeper has a body resembling a caterpillar, with an armoured head that sprouts 8 tentacles. It requires a steady supply of fresh corpses in which to lay its eggs. The armoured head belies a tender, vulnerable body so the creeper will rely on its speed and many paralysing tentacles to protect itself as it secures prey. Each of the tentacles has a 2ft reach, although larger specimens are not unknown. If a carcass creeper has paralysed all nearby enemies, it will begin biting them, inflicting 1d2 hit points of damage per round (the carcass creeper’s mouth is not usable for a bite in actual melee combat).

sections.Special Features: Sectioned Armour Class. The carcass creeper has a well-armoured head, which is AC 3 [17]. Attacks from the sides or rear may reach the softer, less-protected portion of the beast, which is only AC 7 [13].
sections.Special Attacks: Paralysing Tentacles. Anyone hit by a tentacle must make a saving throw vs. paralysis or be paralysed for 3d4 turns. Unarmed Combat. Carcass creepers cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Caryatid column
monsters.description: Caryatid columns share many similarities to stone golems, being created in much the same way. These constructs resemble intricately-carved columns in the shape of a person, usually in pairs. The most common type is maidens, however they can resemble practically anyone. In their dormant state they are almost indistinguishable from a normal statue. The only indication of their true nature is a faint outline of sword held in one hand. They are created as guardians and will animate only when triggered by a certain event. Their trigger must be something simple like someone entering a room, lifting a chest, or opening a door. Once animated they will do their utmost to prevent the trigger from continuing. When their task is complete they will return to their previous place and form. The caryatid column’s main purpose is not combat, but if pressed they will use their swords and attack.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Saving Throw Bonus. Caryatid columns make all saving throws with a +4 bonus. Immunities. Caryatid columns are immune to blindness (and invisibility), psychic damage, charm, domination, sleep, gases, poison, and disease. Resistances. Normal weapons do half damage and magical weapons score full damage, but without their additional magical effects.
sections.Special Features: Any weapon, including magic weapons, that hits a caryatid column has a 25% chance of breaking. For each plus that the weapon has reduces the chance of breaking by 5%; consider any magical weapons without any pluses as a +1. Unarmed Combat. Caryatid Columns cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Cat, domestic
monsters.description: Agile and proud, cats are found everywhere. Because of their size, domestic cats have very ineffective attacks. When a black cat is found as a magic-user’s familiar, the cat confers excellent hearing and night vision on its master or mistress. See also, Lynx, Giant.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Cats are only surprised on a 1 (of a d6), and they surprise opponents on a 1–3 (of a d6).
sections.Special Attacks: Rear Claws. A cat exceeding its needed “to hit” score by 4 or more can rake with its rear claws as well as its front, so roll the listed damage twice. Unarmed Combat. Cats cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Cat, wild
monsters.description: Agile and proud, cats are found everywhere. Because of their size, domestic cats have very ineffective attacks. When a black cat is found as a magic-user’s familiar, the cat confers excellent hearing and night vision on its master or mistress. See also, Lynx, Giant.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Cats are only surprised on a 1 (of a d6), and they surprise opponents on a 1–3 (of a d6).
sections.Special Attacks: Rear Claws. A cat exceeding its needed “to hit” score by 4 or more can rake with its rear claws as well as its front, so roll the listed damage twice. Unarmed Combat. Cats cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Caterwaul
monsters.description: A caterwaul is a bipedal feline predator that stalks darkened caves waiting for prey to walk past. These unusual creatures resemble black panthers walking upright. On their hind legs they move at 180ft, but they can drop to all fours and sprint very fast (240ft) for short distances. What makes these creatures unique is their unusually high dexterity. This will vary from individual to individual. Roll d100 and check the chart below. D100 AC BONUS ATTACKS/ROUND 01–30 0 [0] 1/1 31–60 -1 [+1] 3/2 61–90 -2 [+2] 3/2 91–93 -3 [+3] 2/1 94–97 -4 [+4] 2/1 98 -5 [+5] 2/1 99 -6 [+6] 5/2 00 -7 [+7] 5/2 The attacks per round works much the same way as for fighters, referring to a full attack routine (claw, claw, bite) rather than individual attacks.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Caterwauls can only be surprised (for one segment) on a roll of 1 on a d10.
sections.Special Features: Thief-Type Abilities. Climb 95%, Move quietly 75%, Hide 75%.
sections.Special Attacks: Screech. When a caterwaul attacks for the first time in a combat, it lets out a distinctive screech, which inflicts 1d8 hit points of damage to all within 60ft. This may also summon wandering monsters. Unarmed Combat. Caterwauls do not employ unarmed combat but can be grappled. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF na/na. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.

monsters.name: Cattle, bison (buffalo)
monsters.description: Unarmed Combat. Cattle cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics (they are folded into their trample or charge attacks). BUFFALO Native to tropical and subtropical plains, the buffalo will usually attack if approached within 60ft. Any attack by one may result in the whole herd charging. 50% of all buffalo species are non-aggressive and will flee from threats unless cornered.

sections.Special Features: Sectioned Armour Class. A bison’s head is AC 3 [17]. Only those to the side or rear can attack the body’s AC 7 [13].
sections.Special Attacks: When charging, the buffalo will do 3d6 impact damage plus 1d4 trampling damage. The charge must cover a minimum of 40ft. BULL This is an encounter with a wild bull, massive in size and very aggressive. If someone moves to within 80ft, it is likely to charge (75%), even without apparent provocation. The charge, if either horn hits, inflicts 4d4 points of blunt damage upon impact, in addition to any damage from the horns. Any creature smaller than huge is knocked prone. The charge must traverse a minimum of 30ft in order to be effective. CATTLE These are smaller bulls and cows, either encountered without a lead bull or as part of a lead bull’s herd. If there is any interaction with the herd, it has a 25% chance of stampeding, and a stampede has a 25% chance to head toward the characters, becoming a special attack. Stampedes will cause characters to be trampled by 2d4 animals, and take 1d4 damage per animal.

monsters.name: Centaur
monsters.loot: Individual 4 and Cache 3 each; Hoard 4, 9, and Cache 6 in lair
monsters.description: Centaurs have the body of a horse, but have the upper torso, arms and head of a human in place of the horse’s neck and head. Antipathetic toward humans, yet friendly toward elves and their kin, centaurs prefer unfrequented glades, pastures and woodlands. A centaur band is armed with: 50% hardwood clubs (2d4 damage), 25% composite and/or longbows with the remaining centaurs armed with lance and shield (thus, AC 4 [16])—this last group being the leaders. All centaurs are capable of attacking with melee weapons and two hoof attacks each melee round. If upon rare occasion encountered in their lair, there will be an additional 3d6 (total 7d6 encountered) fighting centaurs, with 5d6 young. Non-fighting (young) centaurs possess only 1d3 hit points.

monsters.name: Centipede, giant, big
monsters.description: Giant centipedes can be encountered in three sizes.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Many-legged. This creature cannot be knocked prone, overborne, or grappled.
sections.Special Attacks: Ranged Attack. Centaurs may use ranged weapons as humans can. Unarmed Combat. Centaurs cannot be overborne or grappled, but they may overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +5/na. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF na/na. Poison Bite (Big). Weak venom (save at +4) that only does 4d4 damage if the saving throw fails. Poison Bite (Bigger). Weak venom (save at +4), but the venom is lethal if the saving throw fails. Poison Bite (Biggest). Relatively powerful venom (no adjustment to saving throw). Death is the result of a failed save, but a successful save still results in 1d8 acid damage. Unarmed Combat. Giant centipedes cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.
sections.Special Features: Climber. This creature can move on walls and ceilings as if they were floors.

monsters.name: Centipede, giant, bigger
monsters.description: Giant centipedes can be encountered in three sizes.

monsters.name: Chimera
monsters.attacks: 2 lion claws (1d4), 2 goat horns (1d3), 1 lion bite (2d6), 1 dragon bite (3d4)
monsters.description: CHIMERA A chimera has the hind quarters of a goat, the forequarters of a lion, the wings of a dragon and 3 heads, one each of the aforementioned creatures. The creature may make up to 6 natural attacks per round, two with clawed lion paws, one with each of the goat head’s 2 horns, the mighty bite of the lion’s maw and another powerful bite by the dragon.

sections.Special Attacks: Breath Weapon. The chimera’s dragon head is capable of breathing fire to a 60ft distance, inflicting 3d8 points of damage. Normal saving throws vs breath weapon apply (save for half damage). GORGIMERA The gorgimera looks much like a chimera, but it has gorgon’s head rather than a goat’s head beside the lion and dragon heads. Breath Weapons. The gorgon head breathes a cloud of petrifying gas in a cone 30ft long and 10ft radius at the base (save or be turned to stone). The dragon head is capable of breathing fire to a 60ft distance, inflicting 3d8 points of damage (save for half damage). Unarmed Combat. Chimeras and gorgimeras cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.
sections.Language: Chimeric is an imperfect form of the red dragon tongue, and is spoken by both chimeras and gorgimeras. It is also often used as a code by those familiar with the language.

monsters.name: Chimera, gorgimera
monsters.attacks: 2 lion claws (1d4), 1 gorgon-gore (2d4), 1 lion bite (2d6), 1 dragon bite (3d4)
monsters.description: CHIMERA A chimera has the hind quarters of a goat, the forequarters of a lion, the wings of a dragon and 3 heads, one each of the aforementioned creatures. monsters.name: Cockatrice
monsters.description: These creatures have the head, legs and wings of a rooster, while the body is that of a serpent. Its wings are functional and allow it to fly. The creature is believed to be from a rooster’s egg hatched by a serpent. Although the beast is capable of inflicting light wounds with its beak, the mere touch of the cockatrice is capable of turning any creature to stone.

sections.Special Attacks: Petrifaction. If the cockatrice hits with beak or claws, the touched creature must roll a successful saving throw vs petrifaction or be instantly turned to stone. The power of this touch is capable of affecting astral and ethereal beings. Unarmed Combat. Cockatrices cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Coffer corpse
monsters.description: A coffer corpse resembles a zombie, seeming nothing more than a rotting, fetid corpse. They are the bodies of the dead who are left behind, never given a proper burial, their souls never finding rest.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Turned as Undead. Coffer corpses are turned as type 7 Undead. Immune to Mundane Weapons. The coffer corpse is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage, unless the weapon causing that damage is magical. Immunities. This creature is immune to mind control (including charm) and hold spells, sleep, gases, poison, disease, cold damage, temporary damage, and subdual damage.
sections.Special Features: If a coffer corpse is hit for 6 or more points in a single round of combat by a normal weapon (to which they are immune) they will fall down, only to rise up the next round. All who witness this horror must save vs fear. Those who fail the saving throw will panic and run away for 2 rounds, with a 60% chance (reduced by 5% per level) to drop all items they are holding.
sections.Special Attacks: Strangle. A coffer corpse has a 75% chance to attack with its bare hands to strangle rather than attacking with a weapon. If they hit, they have grabbed their target by the throat, causing 1d6 damage. Each successive round thereafter they cause an additional 1d6 damage as they are strangling their victim, with no additional roll needed. They will continue choking until they are destroyed or their victim is dead. Unarmed Combat. Coffer corpses cannot be overborne or grappled (it is theoretically possible, but they are immune to temporary damage), and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Couatl
monsters.description: Couatl are a species of brightly feathered serpents with wings. They are extremely intelligent spellcasters. Couatl are rarely encountered, usually in remote tropical environments. They are often treated as gods by lesser beings nearby.

sections.Special Features: Spellcasting. Roll 1d100 to determine the couatl’s spell-casting type. 01-45: 5th level magic-user, 46-80: 7th level cleric, 81-00: 5th level magic-user and 7th level cleric. Ethereality. Couatl can shift into the ethereal plane once per day. In this form they become invisible even while attacking, and can only be damaged by magic weapons (and spells). However, they cannot make physical attacks while in ethereal form. This is usually used to escape through walls rather than as a combat tactic.
sections.Special Attacks: Poison Bite. If the couatl’s bite hits, the victim must save vs poison or die. Constrict. A couatl can also constrict with its body. A successful attack means the couatl has grabbed its victim, causing 2d4 damage, with an additional 2d4 damage each round until one or the other is dead. Unarmed Combat. Couatls cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Crabman
monsters.description: Crabmen are amphibious humanoids. Each has a tough reddish-brown exoskeleton and pincers in place of hands. They have smaller, rudimentary “arms” that can work together to manipulate very light tools. Crabmen lair in caves along the seashore and are generally peaceful creatures, though they are often forced to defend themselves from raids by sahuagin and other marine predators. These creatures prize silver very highly and will attack, on sight, anyone openly carrying silver objects or items which appear to be made of silver. Another oddity of the species is that they occasionally undergo some sort of group frenzy, forming a band of 1d10+30 individuals to march inland, raiding any settlements they find. Unarmed Combat. Crabmen can be overborne or grappled, and they may overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF na/-2.

sections.Language: Crabmen speak their own language, which appears to be an ancient offshoot of the Neutral alignment tongue.

monsters.name: Crocodile, normal
monsters.description: Crocodiles may be found in shallow fresh or salt water. They lie in ambush along river banks, leaping up from concealment to eat just about anything that comes in reach. Cold is their enemy, cutting their movement speed in half. Giant Crocodiles are normally restricted to prehistoric or salt water environments.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Crocodiles of both varieties surprise opponents on a roll of 1–3 on a d6. Unarmed Combat. Crocodiles of either type cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Crocodile, giant
monsters.description: Crocodiles may be found in shallow fresh or salt water. They lie in ambush along river banks, leaping up from concealment to eat just about anything that comes in reach. Cold is their enemy, cutting their movement speed in half. Giant Crocodiles are normally restricted to prehistoric or salt water environments.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Crocodiles of both varieties surprise opponents on a roll of 1–3 on a d6. Unarmed Combat. Crocodiles of either type cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Crustacean, giant, giant crab
monsters.description: Unarmed Combat. Giant crustaceans cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics. GIANT CRAB These creatures are only found near water (fresh or salt). They will typically rush their prey from a place of concealment, having “scouted” the area with their eyes (which are on stalks).

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Giant crabs achieve surprise on 1–4 of 1d6. Giant crayfish achieve surprise on 1–3 of 1d6.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Many-legged. This creature cannot be knocked prone. GIANT CRAYFISH Giant crayfish are only encountered near fresh water. They will typically rush their prey from a place of concealment, but they do not have the advantage of the giant crab’s eyestalks. Many-legged. This creature cannot be knocked prone.

monsters.name: Crustacean, giant, giant crayfish
monsters.description: Unarmed Combat. Giant crustaceans cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics. GIANT CRAB These creatures are only found near water (fresh or salt). They will typically rush their prey from a place of concealment, having “scouted” the area with their eyes (which are on stalks).
