They will typically rush their prey from a place of concealment, but they do not have the advantage of the giant crab’s eyestalks. Many-legged. This creature cannot be knocked prone.

monsters.name: Crypt thing
monsters.description: A crypt thing appears as a cloaked skeleton, but contrary to appearances, is not undead and cannot be turned. They reside in their lairs and never venture forth. A crypt thing will never attack first, they will always let the party attack before they do. If they are not molested they will leave the adventurers alone. If they are attacked then they will respond by activating their teleport ability. A crypt thing can also defend itself with its clawlike hands.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Cannot be Turned (Not Undead). Despite appearances, crypt things are not undead and thus cannot be turned. Immune to Mundane Weapons. The crypt thing is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage, unless the weapon causing that damage is magical.
sections.Special Features: Teleport Enemies. Anyone attempting to attack a crypt thing must (for the first attack only) make a saving throw vs spells or instantly be teleported in a random direction. Each individual who fails must roll d100. Those who roll 01–20 are teleported from 100 to 1,000ft north. Those who roll 21–40 are teleported 100–1,000ft south. Those who roll 41–60 are teleported 100– 1,000ft east. Those who roll 61–80 are teleported 100–1,000ft west. Those who roll 81–90 are teleported one dungeon level up. Those who roll 91–00 are teleported one dungeon level down. Those who make the saving throw can continue with their attack. This is an advanced form of teleportation. Individuals will arrive safely, not in solid areas like floors or walls. Unarmed Combat. Crypt things can be overborne or grappled, although they do not use these tactics themselves. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF na/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF na/+0.
sections.Language: Crypt things speak common. If questioned about the disappearance of any comrades, they will say they were disintegrated.

monsters.name: Cyclops
monsters.description: Cyclopes are extremely tall, ugly humanoids, each with a single eye centred under its slightly drooping brow. These oafish, antisocial creatures prefer to inhabit lonesome environs, such as out–of–the–way, otherwise deserted islands. In addition to their single club attack, cyclopes may attack by hurling large boulders up to a distance of 60ft.

sections.Special Attacks: Ranged Attack. A cyclops can throw rocks like other giants, for 4d10 blunt damage, with a range increment of 20ft (-2 at 40ft, -4 at 60ft). Unarmed Combat. A cyclops can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2.

monsters.name: Dakon
monsters.description: Dakons are intelligent apes resembling gorillas. They are peaceful, fighting only in defence or to regain treasure stolen from them. These apes are likely to be settle anywhere, but avoid large expanses of water. They are on good terms with lawful humans and demi-humans and are able to speak the common tongue, but they have a deep mistrust of humanoids and shun them.

sections.Special Attacks: To-Hit Bonus: Dakons attack with a +2 to-hit bonus due to their incredible strength and the knife-edged sharpness of their claws. Unarmed Combat. Dakons can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.
sections.Language: Dakons speak the common tongue.

monsters.name: Dark creeper
monsters.description: Dark creepers are short, spindly humanoids with pale skin who like to wrap themselves in loose, dark clothing, leaving little exposed save their eyes and hands. These beings are in some way a manifestation of the eldritch powers of darkness, although they are not individually powerful. Dark creepers detest sunlight and avoid any light as best they can, dwelling alone in dungeons or profane villages even deeper underground. These villages are always governed by a dark stalker. Solitary dark creepers tend to carry their treasure with them, concealed within the many loose folds of their dark clothing. There is a 20% chance a dark creeper will carry a magic dagger, 15% chance of a magic ring, and 10% chance of either 1d4 gems of random value or 1d3 items of random jewellery. Lair treasure probabilities for a lone dark creeper are 50% for a magic dagger, 10% for a magic ring, 30% for gems or jewellery. To generate treasure for a dark creeper village, multiply individual treasure chances by the number of creepers, adding 5d20 pp and 5d12 gp.

sections.Special Features: Thief Abilities. Dark creepers have all the skills of a 4th level thief. Spell-Like Abilities. 3/day: Detect magic and create darkness. In both cases, duration is 1 hour, and the effect is in a 50ft radius around the target point. Any magical sources of light have a 20% chance to avoid the effects of darkness upon that item only. If an item is affected, it will resume normal function after 1 hour. Death Fire. When a creeper dies, its body magically immolates in a fiercely hot blaze of disgusting purple and green flames. Metal items, including magical items of metal, carried as part of the creeper’s treasure hoard have an 80% of surviving this magical fire undamaged. Any magic item damaged by the creeper’s death fire will lose its enchantment. Deadly in Darkness: In darkness, the dark creeper’s armour class is 0 [20]. In light, the armour class is 8 [12].
sections.Special Attacks: Ranged Attack. Dark creepers can attack with ranged weapons as humans can. Unarmed Combat. Dark creepers do not make grappling or overbearing attacks, but can be attacked in this way. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2.

monsters.name: Dark stalker
monsters.description: Dark stalkers are the leaders of the dark creepers, though it is not known whether they are dark creepers altered through some means either genetic or magical, or if they are a breed apart. What is known for certain is the dark stalker is much taller than its dark creeper followers and one will be found as the leader of any dark creeper village. In an area settled by at least 25 solitary dark creepers there is a 90% chance there will be a dark stalker in the area, increased by 2% for every 5 additional creepers. A dark stalker is rarely encountered away from their clan, but if such an encounter occurs the stalker is probably on some mysterious personal mission and will not engage in combat unless forced to do so. Dark stalkers carry their treasure in their robes like dark creepers: 30% chance of magic short sword, 10% of magical rings (worn if possible), 10% chance of either 2d4 gems or 1d2 items of jewellery to be determined randomly by GM.

sections.Special Features: Thief Abilities. Dark stalkers have all the skills of a 4th level thief. Spell-Like Abilities. 3/day: Detect magic and create darkness. In both cases, duration is 1 hour, and the effect is in a 50ft radius around the target point. Any magical sources of light have a 20% chance to avoid the effects of darkness upon that item only. If an item is affected, it will resume normal function after 1 hour. 2/day: wall of fog Death Fire. When a dark stalker dies, it explodes in a sickly blue 3d8 fireball blast with a radius of 10ft. Magic items carried by the stalker have a 75% chance of surviving the blast in usable condition. Deadly in Darkness: In darkness, the dark stalker’s armour class is 0 [20]. In light, the armour class is 8 [12].
sections.Special Attacks: Ranged Attack. Dark stalkers can attack with ranged weapons as humans can. Unarmed Combat. Dark stalkers can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0. DEMONS Demonologists have identified several classes of demon. Each class of demon possesses a variety of powerful, supernatural abilities. Those abilities common to all demons are noted below. For further information on both the classified and unclassified demons, see the individual demon listings. Note that most demons do not actually fall into the six listed categories. Many demons possess the following magical abilities: infravision (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), teleport (with no chance of error) (as the 5th level magic-user spell), darkness and gate (as the 9th level magic-user spell). See individual listings for details. Demons can freely travel between their own home planes and Tartarus, Pandemonium and Hades. They may also travel the Astral Plane at will. However, they are only able to enter the Prime Material Plane if summoned with a spell (conjuration, gate, wish, etc.) or certain magical items. Demons are all extremely and decidedly chaotic evil (see “Alignment”). Demonic society is highly competitive and always favours the strong over the weak. In combat, demons are fearless and the less intelligent among them will attack mindlessly until slain. They are immune to subdual attacks and may simultaneously attack as many opponents as their abilities allow. Being supremely chaotic, demons will never willingly serve another. If compelled into service through magical or other means, they will always seek a way to either kill or enslave their master, or at the very least, subvert the terms of their summoning. While demons may be summoned by higher-level PCs, they will prove highly difficult to control. Thaumaturgic circles are proof against demons, but require increasingly complex preparation and materials for the more powerful sorts. Often summoning will entail either a threat of punishment or a reward. These should be considered carefully by the GM during play and should always carry an element of risk for the summoner. Demons are repulsed by good artifacts or other powerful holy items. On the Prime Material Plane, demons may be turned by clerics of levels 8+ and paladins of levels 11+. Summary of Resistances: ATTACK FORM DAMAGE ROLLED Acid Full damage Cold Half damage Electricity (lightning bolt) Half damage Fire (dragon breath, fireball) Half damage Gas, poisonous (cloudkill) Half damage Iron Weapons Full damage

monsters.name: Class a demon (vrock)
monsters.description: Vrock, considered one of the weakest of demonkind, look like a hideous cross between a vulture and a humanoid. Unlike stronger demons, they are vulnerable to non-magical weapons. Vrock are particularly stupid, and cannot normally be bargained with. They love the sight of precious gems and jewellery, however, and also enjoy feasting on the flesh of humans.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (50%). Any magic spell or effect has a 50% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Electricity, Fire, Poison (including gases).
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: Darkness, 5ft radius, detect invisibility (objects only, otherwise as per the 2nd level magic-user spell), gate in another vrock (10% chance of success), or telekinesis (as the 5th level magic-user spell, up to 200 lbs). Unarmed Combat. Vrock demons can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +3/-3. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +3/-3.

monsters.name: Class b demon (hezrou)
monsters.description: Slightly shorter than the vrock, the hezrou resemble loathsome toads with humanoid arms. They are vulnerable to normal melee and missile weapons. Hezrou and vrock will gladly fight each other without hesitation, and they both share a love of human flesh.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (55%). Any magic spell or effect has a 55% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Electricity, Fire, Poison (including gases).
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: Darkness, 15ft radius, cause fear (as the 4th level magic-user spell), levitate (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), detect invisibility (objects only, otherwise as per the 2nd level magic-user spell), telekinesis (as per the 5th level magic-user spell, up to 300 lbs), or gate (as the 9th level magic-user spell) another hezrou (20% chance of success). Unarmed Combat. Hezrou-type demons can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2.

monsters.name: Class c demon (glabrezu)
monsters.attacks: 2 pincers (2d6 piercing), 2 claws (1d3 slashing), and 1 bite (1d4+1 piercing)
monsters.description: These muscular demons have a head like a horned dog, and four smaller arms that sprout from the creature’s chest: two of these end in sharp pincers, and two end in clawed hands. Glabrezu are vulnerable to normal melee weapons and missiles.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (60%). Any magic spell or effect has a 60% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Electricity, Fire, Poison (including gases).
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: Darkness, 10ft radius, cause fear (as the 4th level magic-user spell), cause fear (as the 4th level magic-user spell), levitate (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), pyrotechnics (as the 2nd level magic-user spell ), polymorph self (as the 4th level magic-user spell), telekinesis (as the 5th level magic-user spell, up to 400 lbs), gate (as the 9th level magic-user spell) another Class A to C demon (30% chance of success). Unarmed Combat. Glabrezu demons can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +3/-3.

monsters.name: Class d demon (nalfeshnee and others)
monsters.description: Particularly malevolent demons, the class D have the upper body of an ape and the cloven-hoofed lower body (and head) of a boar. They have rather small, feathered wings as well, which seem undersized compared to their corpulent bodies. Certain class D demons have their own secret names, which makes it 90% certain they will answer a summons if it is spoken. Conjurers should be prepared to make impressive promises of treasure, magical items or living sacrifices when summoning a class D demon, especially by name. It should also be remembered that these demons particularly enjoy feasting on human blood and meat.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (65%). Any magic spell or effect has a 65% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immune to Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Electricity, Fire, Poison (including gases).
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: Darkness, 10ft radius, improved phantasmal force (as the 2nd level illusionist spell), fear (as the 4th level magic-user spell), levitate (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), detect magic (as the 1st level magic-user spell), comprehend languages (as the 1st level magic-user spell), dispel magic (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), polymorph self (as the 4th level magic-user spell), telekinesis (as the 5th level magic-user spell, up to 500 lbs), project image (as the 6th level magic-user spell), use a symbol of fear or discord (as the 8th level magic-user spell), and gate (as the 9th level magic-user spell) another class A to D demon (random class, 60% chance of success).
sections.Special Attacks: Strength Bonus. These demons have a +2 bonus on to-hit rolls. Unarmed Combat. Nalfeshnee demons can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +5/-5. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2.

monsters.name: Class e demon (marilith and others)
monsters.description: Infamous even among demonkind for their cruel and ill-tempered nature, the marilith are invariably female. From the waist up they appear to be a human female with six arms and skin tones ranging from deep violet to a putrescent green. Below the waist however, they have the coiling body of a large serpent. In melee they prefer to wield a variety of barbed and hooked swords and battle axes or simply constrict their prey with their powerful serpentine tail. All class E demons have personal and secret names which may be used to summon and bargain with them, much like class D demons.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (80%). Any magic spell or effect has an 80% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immune to Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Electricity, Fire, Poison (including gases).
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: Darkness, 5ft radius, charm person (as the 1st level magic-user spell), levitate (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), comprehend languages (as the 1st level magic-user spell), detect invisibility (objects only, otherwise as the 2nd level magic-user spell), pyrotechnics (as the 2nd level magic-user spell ), polymorph self (as the 4th level magic-user spell), project image (as the 6th level magic-user spell), or gate (as the 9th level magic-user spell) another demon (50% chance of success). Use the following table to determine which class of demon is summoned: D100 DEMON CLASS 1–30 Class A 31–55 Class B 56–70 Class C 71–85 Class D 86–00 Class F Unarmed Combat. Marilith demons can make grappling or overbearing attacks, but cannot be overborne. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/ DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +3/na. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-6.

monsters.name: Class f demon (balor and others)
monsters.description: Reportedly only six of this class of demon exist, each with its own secret name. In combat they wield massive +1 swords and a cat-o-nine-tails whip which they employ to drag their victims into the flames that they continually immolate themselves in. Summoning class F demons requires significant offerings or future promises of service or sacrifice. If negotiation is successful, they might be persuaded to aid the summoner or associated group for a while. In any case, these demons will always try to bully and intimidate their masters in an effort to usurp leadership, which they crave. Many other chaotic evil monsters and demons are attracted to the aura of charismatic evil that surrounds class F demons, so they are often found in the forefront of evil hordes.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (75%). Any magic spell or effect has a 75% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immune to Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Electricity, Fire, Poison (including gases).
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: Darkness, 10ft radius, fear (as the 4th level magic-user spell), detect magic (as the 1st level magic-user spell), read magic (as the 1st level magic-user spell), comprehend languages (as the 1st level magic-user spell), detect invisibility (objects only, otherwise as the 2nd level magic-user spell), pyrotechnics (as the 2nd level magic-user spell ), dispel magic (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), suggestion (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), telekinesis (as the 5th level magic-user spell, up to 600 lbs), use a symbol of fear, discord, sleep, or stunning (as the 8th level magic-user spell), and gate (as the 9th level magic-user spell) another demon of class C (80% chance) or class D (20% chance) with a 70% chance of success.
sections.Special Attacks: Whip. Each round, there is a 4 in 6 chance the Balor will use its fiery whip. Victims who are hit and fail a saving throw vs spells are burnt by the flames and suffer 4d6 additional points of damage. Unarmed Combat. Balor demons can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +3/-3. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2.

monsters.name: Aluu-demon (half-demon)
monsters.attacks: 1 weapon (weapon + strength bonus) or draining touch
monsters.description: Aluu-demons are one of several types of “tieflings,” a common term for those with fiends of the lower planes in their ancestry. The two tiefling monster types represented in this book (aluu-demons and caumbions) are too powerful to be used as a character ancestry. Most aluu-demons are the result of union between a succubus or incubus with a human. Their individual appearances vary, but their vestigial horns and small leathery bat-like wings denote their demonic heritage. Most favour their demonic parent and revel in chaotic evil. A minority (20%) harbour less demoniacal inclinations. Nevertheless, they may never be lawful or good. Aluu-demons have a natural base armour class of 5 [15]. Wearing armour gives them no additional benefit, although rings, magic items and spells can improve their AC. Fully 25% of all aluu-demons have genius level intelligence (17- 18). These aluu-demons are able to memorise and cast spells as a 1st to 12th level magic-user (1d12 to determine level). Spell casting abilities are in addition to their other innate abilities noted above, and the aluu-demon has none of the armour/weapon restrictions of the magic-user class.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (30%). Any magic spell or effect has a 30% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immune to Non-Iron Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons that are not made of iron, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more. Most metal weapons are made from iron (steel).
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. 1/day: dimension door (as the 4th level magic-user spell) 3/day (as Level 12 Caster): charm person (as the 1st level magic-user spell), ESP (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), polymorph self (humanoid shapes only, otherwise as the 4th level magic-user spell), and suggestion (as the 3rd level magic-user spell).
sections.Special Attacks: Energy Drain. Much like succubi/incubi, aluu-demons are able to drain a victim’s life energy with a touch (a “to hit” roll is required in combat). Each touch drains 1d8 hit points from the victim and adds 1d4 hit points to the aluu-demon. Unarmed Combat. Aluu-demons can make grappling or overbearing attacks, but usually don’t. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/- 8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

monsters.name: Babau
monsters.attacks: 2 claws (1d4+1) and 1 bite (2d4) or 1 weapon (+7 damage)
monsters.description: Babau are also known by demonologists as horned demons or bone demons. They are around 7ft tall and look like skeletons covered in a leathery black skin. The babau’s feet, taloned hands and head are grossly oversized, nearly the same as a hill giant’s. From the base of its skull protrudes a hooked horn. These demons are known for their cunning intelligence and strength (19). In combat, they prefer to use any sort of weaponry if it is to their advantage. Babau are despised by class A, B and C demons. Class D demons especially hate bands of babau, and hunt them for food.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (50%). Any magic spell or effect has a 50% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immune to Mundane Weapons. The babau is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage, unless the weapon causing that damage is magical. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Electricity, Fire, Poison (including gases). Ichor Reduces Weapon Damage by Half. In the heat of battle, babau demons secrete a slimy rust coloured ichor that reduces damage from melee weapons, as blows slide off their bodies. Any damage from a melee weapon inflicts only half the damage indicated. Vulnerability to Iron. Iron weapons inflict +2 additional damage on babau demons (although the weapon must be magical to hit).
sections.Special Features: Thief Abilities. Babau have the thieving abilities of a 9th level Thief.
sections.Spell-Like Abilities: At Will: Darkness, 5ft radius 1/day (as 14th level caster): fear (touch only, otherwise as the 4th level magic-user spell), levitate (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), fly (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), dispel magic (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), polymorph self (as the 4th level magic-user spell), heat metal (as the 2nd level druid spell), and gate (as the 9th level magic-user spell) in another babau (25% chance of success). Enfeebling Gaze. Anyone up to 20ft away gazing into the eyes of a babau must save vs spells or suffer the effects of a ray of enfeeblement (as the 2nd level magic-user spell). This applies to anyone who is generally in front of the demon and looking at it without using an indirect method of sight such as a mirror. Attacking the creature by looking at a reflection incurs a to-hit penalty of -2. Attacking blindly incurs a to-hit penalty of -4. Unarmed Combat. Babau demons can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1.

monsters.name: Caumbion, minor
monsters.description: Caumbions are the offspring of a major demon and a human (cf. aluu-demon). As such, each is slightly different depending upon parentage. Generally, caumbions are strong and heavily– built. They will usually have several other demonic characteristics as well, such as vestigial horns, barbs, or scaled skin. Caumbions may become clerics, attaining a maximum level equal to their hit dice, magic-users (maximum of 5th level), or thieves or assassins (up to a maximum of their hit dice in ability level). The caumbion has the abilities of the class, none of the armour/weapon restrictions, but does not gain extra hit points from the class. If the caumbion has the abilities of a character class, add an extra 15 points of XP per hit point to the monster’s experience point value. MINOR CAUMBIONS Minor Caumbions have a natural base armour class of 6 [14]. Wearing mundane armours cannot improve this. Magical armours or other protections add only their bonus, unless the armour is superior to AC 6 [14], in which case the full benefit is accrued (the caumbion’s base AC is ignored, and the AC of the armour is used instead). The GM may choose to add class abilities or special abilities to a minor caumbion to generate an interesting foe if the caumbion is the main villain and has minions; caumbions are highly individual. In higher level adventures where the caumbion is just one of many enemies, this usually isn’t worth the extra complexity.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance: Minor caumbions have 5%–20% magic resistance depending on their hit dice. 5HD=5%, 6HD=10%, 7HD=15%, and 8HD=20%. Unarmed Combat. Minor Caumbions can make grappling or overbearing attacks, but only overbearing is commonly used against sole opponents. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. NOBLE CAUMBIONS Noble Caumbions are the children of very powerful demons, such as demon princes and the like (“nobility” refers to their power, for their behaviour is usually anything but noble). They are likely to be the main villain in an adventure, so the GM will probably choose to add abilities from one of the four possible classes (see above). Magic Resistance: Noble caumbions have 25%–40% magic resistance depending on their hit dice. 9-10HD=25%, 11-12HD=30%, 13-14HD=35%, 15-16HD=40%. Unarmed Combat. Noble Caumbions can make grappling or overbearing attacks, but only overbearing is commonly used against sole opponents. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

monsters.name: Caumbion, noble
monsters.description: Caumbions are the offspring of a major demon and a human (cf. aluu-demon). As such, each is slightly different depending upon parentage. Generally, caumbions are strong and heavily– built. They will usually have several other demonic characteristics as well, such as vestigial horns, barbs, or scaled skin. Caumbions may become clerics, attaining a maximum level equal to their hit dice, magic-users (maximum of 5th level), or thieves or assassins (up to a maximum of their hit dice in ability level). The GM may choose to add class abilities or special abilities to a minor caumbion to generate an interesting foe if the caumbion is the main villain and has minions; caumbions are highly individual. In higher level adventures where the caumbion is just one of many enemies, this usually isn’t worth the extra complexity.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance: Minor caumbions have 5%–20% magic resistance depending on their hit dice. 5HD=5%, 6HD=10%, 7HD=15%, and 8HD=20%. Unarmed Combat. Minor Caumbions can make grappling or overbearing attacks, but only overbearing is commonly used against sole opponents. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. NOBLE CAUMBIONS Noble Caumbions are the children of very powerful demons, such as demon princes and the like (“nobility” refers to their power, for their behaviour is usually anything but noble). They are likely to be the main villain in an adventure, so the GM will probably choose to add abilities from one of the four possible classes (see above). Magic Resistance: Noble caumbions have 25%–40% magic resistance depending on their hit dice. 9-10HD=25%, 11-12HD=30%, 13-14HD=35%, 15-16HD=40%. Unarmed Combat. Noble Caumbions can make grappling or overbearing attacks, but only overbearing is commonly used against sole opponents. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

monsters.name: Dretch
monsters.description: Dretch are the weakest of native demonkind (manes, as condemned souls, are weaker). Their appearance is almost comical: a plump body with thin, gangly arms and legs. Their squat heads are bald and they have a slobbering, stupid visage. Dretch usually attack in hordes, using tooth and claw in blind abandon, although if they consider themselves threatened they will first try to open a gate for reinforcements.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (30%). Any magic spell or effect has a 30% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Electricity, Fire, Poison (including gases).
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: Darkness, 5ft radius, scare (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), telekinesis (as the 5th level magic-user spell, up to 50 lbs) or attempt to gate (as the 9th level magic-user spell) a class A demon (15% chance of success). 1/day: stinking cloud (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), and teleport without fail (as the 5th level magic-user spell, but with no chance of error). Unarmed Combat. Dretch demons can make grappling or overbearing attacks, but ordinarily don’t. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF -1/+1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2.

monsters.name: Ekivu (fly demon) (khasme)
monsters.description: Ekivu resemble a hideous crossbreed between a giant fly and a human. Their hind legs are insect-like and their fore-limbs resemble human arms, but with bony, sharp claws. Like flies, their bodies are covered in blueish-black chitin with bristling hair. Their heads are vaguely human, but with bulbous, faceted eyes like those of a fly. Their mouths are ringed with sharp teeth and their long noses are actually a sharp proboscis for drawing blood from their victims. Ekivu have a long standing hatred of most other classes of demons, especially classes A and B. Ekivu have managed to enslave a number of shub, which they use for their own nefarious ends.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (40%). Any magic spell or effect has a 40% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Poison Immunity. These demons are immune to poison and poison damage (including gases). Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Electricity, Fire.
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: Darkness, 5ft radius, detect good (as the 1st level cleric spell), detect invisibility (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), telekinesis (as the 5th level magic-user spell, up to 150 lbs), fear (touch only, otherwise as the 4th level magic-user spell) or gate (as the 9th level magic-user spell) another ekivu (15% chance of success).
sections.Special Attacks: Drone. When not using one of their other special abilities, ekivu constantly make an insidious buzzing drone which has the power to lull listeners into a comatose state. The ekivu can drone while engaged in melee combat. If a save vs spells (unlisted categories) is not made, the victim will sleep for 2d4 hours or until the demon has drawn 1d4 hp of their blood. Unarmed Combat. Ekivu demons cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Manis
monsters.description: A manis (plural: manes) is the form of a soul condemned to the abyss. They are considered demons, but do not have all the powers associated with demonkind. They are rare in the material planes. Manes will attack anything that is not a demon. The form of a manis is bipedal and humanoid, but manes have vacant eyes, sharp teeth and claws, and tails.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Mundane Weapons. A manis is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage, unless the weapon causing that damage is magical. Immunities. This creature is immune to mind control (including charm) and hold spells, sleep, gases, poison, disease, cold damage, temporary damage, and subdual damage. Cannot Be Killed. A manis that is killed re-forms after one day. They are only truly destroyed when a demon lord chooses to feed on them. Unarmed Combat. Manes can make grappling or overbearing attacks, but ordinarily don’t. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2.

monsters.name: Quasit
monsters.description: Quasits are larval fiends that have been shaped by demon lords for service as familiars to chaotic evil magic-users and occasionally as servants to other powerful chaotic evil individuals. When serving as a familiar, quasits endow the magic-user with several abilities. If the magic-user is within a mile of their quasit familiar, a constant full-sensory telepathic communication operates through the quasit. The master also gains 1 level of ability as a magic-user within this radius. If the quasit is within 25ft of its master, it imparts its 25% magic resistance and also its regeneration abilities. If either master or quasit moves out of range, the special abilities are lost. In addition to these abilities, once per week a quasit is able to contact the Abyss in order to help gain some necessary advice or information. This operates as the 5th level cleric spell commune, and up to 6 questions are permitted. Despite their rather low intelligence, quasits are quite crafty and cunning creatures. They are also used as tools by demon lords, who might communicate through them. Quasits are generally tasked with helping their masters to spread evil and chaos. In particular, they are often used to pervert lawful evil souls to chaos, which earns them rewards on their home plane of the Abyss. Ultimately, when its master dies, the quasit is charged with bringing the soul back to the Abyss. If the quasit has served well, it may be rewarded by being changed into a class A or class B demon. If not, they will be punished through becoming a soul worm, or even a quasit again. If the quasit dies, the master immediately loses 4 levels (duration 1 month).

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (25%). Any magic spell or effect has a 25% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immune to Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more. Immunities. Quasits are immune to cold, fire, and electrical damage. Saving Throw (Spells). Quasits make saving throws against spells with a target number of 13.
sections.Special Features: Regeneration. Quasits regenerate damage at a rate of 1 hp per round. Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: detect good (as the 1st level cleric spell), detect magic (as the 1st level cleric spell), invisibility (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), polymorph self (each quasit has 2 forms into which it can polymorph, chosen by the GM from frog, bat, giant centipede, or wolf. 1/day: cause fear (as the 4th level magic-user spell) in a 30ft radius.
sections.Special Attacks: In its natural form, a quasit attacks with its teeth and claws, which inflict a burning irritation that subtracts 1 from the victim’s dexterity unless a save vs poison is made. This penalty is cumulative. The irritation remains for 2d6 melee rounds. Unarmed Combat. Quasits can make grappling or overbearing attacks, but ordinarily don’t. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/- 10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF -4/+4. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -4/+4.

monsters.name: Shub (rutterkith)
monsters.loot: Individual 3 and 4 each; Cache 1 and 3 in lair
monsters.description: Shub resemble humanoids, but with hunched backs, twisted arms and legs, and a strange, loping gait. Their pointed skulls are bald and misshapen. While physically among the weakest of demonkind, the shub are a vile, vengeful sort. They are the continual target of abuse by other classes of demon, and the shub are quick to respond in kind if given the opportunity. Shub particularly enjoy bullying the dretch, whom they despise as lumbering and stupid. In combat, shub prefer to wield a variety of strange, wicked-looking pole arms, saw-toothed swords, and bizarre atlatls and throwing knives.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (40%). Any magic spell or effect has a 40% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Electricity, Fire, Poison (including gases).
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: darkness (5ft radius), fear (touch only, otherwise as the 4th level magic-user spell), fly (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), telekinesis (as the 5th level magic-user spell, up to 100 lbs), attempt to gate in an ekivu (15% chance of success). 1/day: teleport (without fail, otherwise as the 5th level magic-user spell). Unarmed Combat. Shub demons can make grappling or overbearing attacks, but ordinarily don’t. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.

monsters.name: Succubus/incubus
monsters.description: These solitary demons are called a succubus (if female) and an incubus (if male). In their true forms they resemble stunningly attractive human beings, with leathery bat wings sprouting from their backs. If they take a liking to a particular victim, a succubus/incubus may mate with a human, producing an aluu-demon (see listing for further details). In the Abyss, the succubi and incubi reign over lesser demons through intimidation and trickery. They also prize treasure, especially gems and jewellery.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more. Magic Resistance (70%). Any magic spell or effect has a 70% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Electricity, Fire, Poison (including gases).
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: darkness (5ft radius), become ethereal (as per the magic item oil of etherealness), charm person (as the 1st level magic-user spell), ESP (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), clairaudience (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), suggestion (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), polymorph self (humanoid shapes only, otherwise as the 4th level magic-user spell), or gate (as the 9th level magic-user spell) a class D demon (70%) or a class E demon (30%) with a 40% chance of success. 1/day: teleport (without fail, otherwise as the 5th level magic-user spell).
sections.Special Attacks: Energy-Draining Kiss. A succubus or incubus feeds by draining energy from charmed or unconscious victims by a kiss. Each kiss, to a maximum of one per day, drains one level from the victim. Captives of a succubus or incubus do not survive for long. Unarmed Combat. Succubi and incubi can make grappling or overbearing attacks, and often do (their AC makes it difficult to fend them off). If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.

monsters.name: Uduk (bar-igura)
monsters.description: The uduk, or the “jumping demon”, looks much like an orang– utan with a horribly twisted face. Its hands and feet are taloned and have 6 digits each. The uduk can move on foot along the ground, but they excel at swinging through areas of dense foliage. They can also jump up to 40 feet in a single bound. They have a natural ability to change their colouration to match their surroundings, which takes one melee round. Uduk do not like the company of other demons, and generally are found only with others of their ilk. If other kinds of demons are present, uduk will bully weaker demons in order to undermine their superiors.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (45%). Any magic spell or effect has a 45% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Electricity, Fire, Poison (including gases).
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: darkness (10ft radius), fear (as the 4th level magic-user spell), create water (as the 1st level cleric spell), detect illusion (as the 1st level Illusionist spell), detect invisibility (objects only, otherwise as the 2nd level magic-user spell), dispel magic (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), entangle (as the 1st level druid spell), plant growth (as the 3rd level druid spell), telekinesis (as the 5th level magic-user spell, up to 250 lbs), or gate in another uduk (25% chance of success). 2/day: change self (as the 1st level illusionist spell), invisibility (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), and spectral force (as the 3rd level Illusionist spell). Unarmed Combat. Bar-Igura demons can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0. DEVILS The primary inhabitants of the planes of Hell are the devils. They are the champions of lawful evil, and are the implacable foes of chaotic demonkind and all servants of good. Devil society is organised into a strict hierarchy, which is never compromised for fear of retribution from the archdevils, who rule the planes of Hell. Nevertheless, squabbling and rivalries are common amongst devils. Amongst the archdevils themselves there also exists a hierarchy of barons, dukes, marquises, and princes—cause for considerable rivalry and jealousy. All devils can move between the various planes of Hell, although this usually requires permission from the archdevil who rules the particular plane. Devils may also move at will to Gehenna, Hades, and Acheron. Similarly, they can also travel to the Astral Plane, but this is rare. Devils are not allowed to enter the other planes (e.g. the Prime Material) without a proper summoning, a gate spell, or the invocation of their secret name (if they have one). All devils of a certain rank possess special, magical abilities which may vary according to individual type. They can use these abilities at will one at a time. These abilities are: animate dead (as the 5th level magic-user spell), charm person (as the 1st level magic-user spell), fear (effect varies, as the 4th level magic-user spell), know alignment (as the 2nd level cleric spell), spectral force (as the 3rd level illusionist spell), suggestion (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), teleport (no chance of error, otherwise as the 5th level magic-user spell), and summoning other devils (varies, as the 3rd level magic-user spell monster summoning I. All devils have infravision and may understand and communicate in any language. Only the material form of a devil may be killed. To actually slay a devil one must do so in the planes of Hell or a neighbouring lower plane. If its material form is slain, a devil must return to its home plane in Hell for nine decades of servitude as a lemure before it will resume its former status. Once combat is joined with devils, they can never be subdued. In dire circumstances the major devils and archdevils may be willing to negotiate. Lesser devils will madly fight to the death. If it is to their advantage, devils can split their attacks among 2 or more targets. Devils are exceptionally conscious of any kind of laws or contracts binding them to certain behaviour, and are profoundly adept at exploiting hidden loopholes. Negotiating with them can be quite tedious as every minute detail and exigency must be properly accounted for. Just as when summoning a demon, proper inscription of a magical circle of protection is necessary for the conjurer’s safety when attempting to summon a devil. These circles are type-specific, with more powerful devils requiring proportionately more complex and expensive circles. Devils are also repulsed by good artifacts. Devils are susceptible to attack as noted in the table below; ATTACK FORM DAMAGE ROLLED Acid Full damage Cold Half damage Electricity (lightning bolt) Full damage Fire (dragon breath, fireball) None Gas, poisonous (cloudkill) Half damage Iron weapons No additional damage Magic missile Full damage Poison Full damage Full damage (according to Silver normal weapon type)

monsters.name: Assagim (nipheribu, nuperibbo)
monsters.description: These are the lowest of all the devils, and they are found in the millions throughout every plane of Hell. Assagim are the unfortunate souls of those not evil enough to be incarnated as lemures. They are totally senseless—having neither eyes, ears, or mouth. Assagim resemble bony, featureless humanoids with two crude arms ending in claws. In combat, they attack with their two sharp claws. If organised by an archdevil into an army, they are sometimes armed with crude clubs or maces which they use to blindly batter their opponents en masse. If slain in the service of evil, assagim will usually (99%) reincarnate within one day as another assagim. A small percentage (1%) become lemures; and within another 10 millennia, they might again be reincarnated as one of the lesser devils.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immunities. This creature is immune to fire damage and immune to any condition that assumes the presence of senses such as hearing or sight. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Poison (including gases).
sections.Special Features: Regeneration (Native Plane Only). These creatures regenerate at a rate of 1hp/round if they are in Hell or one of the other lower planes of existence. This ability is lost in the material planes. Unarmed Combat. Assagim can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.
sections.Language: Assagim (Nipheribu) are telepathically sensitive to other devils, and can receive commands from most other types of devil except lemures.

monsters.name: Barbed devil
monsters.description: These devils are quite common on the 3rd and 4th planes of Hell. They are typically used as guards and sentries, a task at which they excel. Any trespassers will be quickly imprisoned in one of their many iron cells to await torture. Barbed devils do not need any hand-held weapons. They are quite proficient at using their hard, sharply-barbed claws and tail to beat their victims into submission.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (35%). Any magic spell or effect has a 35% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immunities. This creature is immune to fire damage. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Poison (including gases).
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: animate dead (as the 5th level magic-user spell), charm person (as the 1st level magic-user spell), fear (effect varies, as the 4th level magic-user spell), know alignment (as the 2nd level cleric spell), spectral force (as the 3rd level illusionist spell), suggestion (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), teleport (no chance of error, otherwise as the 5th level magic-user spell), pyrotechnics (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), produce flame (as the 2nd level druid spell), hold person (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), or summon an additional barbed devil to their aid (30% chance of success).
sections.Special Attacks: Fear. Whenever a barbed devil hits an opponent, they cause fear (as the 4th level magic-user spell) if the victim fails a saving throw against spells. Unarmed Combat. Barbed devils can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.

monsters.name: Bearded devil
monsters.attacks: 1 glaive (1d3 + entangle) or 2 claws (1d2) and 1 beardburn (1d8)
monsters.description: Bearded devils make their home on the 3rd plane of Hell. They are renowned for both their bloodthirstiness and their malicious cruelty. For this reason, they are often seen serving as shock troops in the legions of Hell. Bearded devils do not value treasure, although they may be influenced by offers of warm meat.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (45%). Any magic spell or effect has a 45% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immunities. This creature is immune to fire damage. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Poison (including gases).
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: animate dead (as the 5th level magic-user spell), charm person (as the 1st level magic-user spell), fear (effect varies, as the 4th level magic-user spell), know alignment (as the 2nd level cleric spell), spectral force (as the 3rd level illusionist spell), suggestion (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), teleport (no chance of error, otherwise as the 5th level magic-user spell), affect normal fires (as the 1st level magic-user spell), command (as the 1st level cleric spell), fear (touch only, otherwise as the 4th level magic-user spell), produce flame (as the 2nd level druid spell), or summon another bearded devil (35% chance of success).
sections.Special Attacks: Glaive. In combat, bearded devils prefer to use a wickedly barbed and hooked glaive, which can entangle an opponent intent on escape (1d3 damage plus the victim is immobilised and cannot attack. A successful Minor Test of Strength check is required to escape from the glaive. Beards. If unarmed, these devils will grab victims in their claws and use their bristly beards to scrape and burn. If they manage to hit with both claws, they will also score maximum damage with their beards (8 hp). Any victim struck for maximum damage from these “beard-burns” must make a save vs poison or be afflicted with a painful, itching rash (-1 dexterity every 4 rounds; duration 3d8 turns). Unarmed Combat. Bearded devils can make grappling or overbearing attacks, although they usually don’t. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/ DEF +10/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.

monsters.name: Bone devil
monsters.description: Bone devils make their lair on the 5th plane of Hell. They are cruel, and enjoy torturing those weaker than themselves. They resemble large skeletons, covered in leathery white flesh, with a segmented tail like a scorpion. Unlike most devils, bone devils prefer the frigid climate of their home plane. Bone devils carry no treasure. They cannot be bribed with coins or gems, but they consider frozen humanoid flesh a delicacy.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (20%). Any magic spell or effect has a 20% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immunities. This creature is immune to fire damage. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Poison (including gases).
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: animate dead (as the 5th level magic-user spell), charm person (as the 1st level magic-user spell), fear (effect varies, as the 4th level magic-user spell), know alignment (as the 2nd level cleric spell), spectral force (as the 3rd level illusionist spell), suggestion (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), teleport (no chance of error, otherwise as the 5th level magic-user spell), fear (5ft radius, otherwise as the 4th level magic-user spell), phantasmal force (as the 1st level illusionist spell), fly (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), invisibility (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), detect invisibility (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), or summon another bone devil (40% chance of success). 1/day: wall of ice (as the 4th level magic-user spell).
sections.Special Attacks: Hook. Bone devils wield a large bone hook to snag their opponents. If they score a hit, there is a 50% chance the victim will be immobilised and cannot attack. A successful Minor Test of Strength check is required to escape from the hook. Tail Sting. If a victim is caught in the devil’s hook, the bone devil can then sting with their scorpion-like tails (2d4 damage, save vs poison or lose 1d4 strength for 10 rounds). Unarmed Combat. Bone devils can make grappling or overbearing attacks, although they usually don’t. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +3/-3.

monsters.name: Erinyes
monsters.description: These winged humanoids usually appear female, although a few (10%) are male. Erinyes dwell on the 2nd Plane of Hell, and are tasked with retrieving evil souls from the Prime Material Plane for their diabolical masters. Erinyes are unrelenting pursuers and prefer to capture their victims alive and return them to Hell for punishment. On occasion, erinyes may be willing to bargain, but they are quite crafty and will always try to tempt the bargainer into committing a great sin.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (30%). Any magic spell or effect has a 30% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immunities. This creature is immune to fire damage. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Poison (including gases).
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: animate dead (as the 5th level magic-user spell), charm person (as the 1st level magic-user spell), fear (effect varies, as the 4th level magic-user spell), know alignment (as the 2nd level cleric spell), spectral force (as the 3rd level illusionist spell), suggestion (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), teleport (no chance of error, otherwise as the 5th level magic-user spell), fear (gaze, otherwise as the 4th level magic-user spell), detect invisibility (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), locate object (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), invisibility (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), polymorph self (as the 4th level magic-user spell), produce flame (as the 2nd level druid spell), or summon another erinyes to their aid (25% chance of success).
sections.Special Attacks: Poison Dagger. In melee, erinyes use a magical dagger which is poisonous and causes horribly painful wounds (save vs poison or pass out for 1d6 rounds). Ropes of Entanglement. These devils also carry ropes of entanglement, which they use to bind their prisoners. Unarmed Combat. Erinyes devils can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, although they don’t use these tactics. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.

monsters.name: Hellcat (devilcat)
monsters.description: Hellcats are a minor type of devil, often seen serving their infernal masters in the nine planes of Hell. Rarely, hellcats also travel to the Prime Material Plane to serve as a familiar for an important evil spell caster. Hellcats encountered on the Prime Material Plane who are not already serving as a familiar may attach themselves to a suitable lawful evil character. They prefer to serve clerics, but will also attach themselves to a magic-user or illusionist. If a stronger lawful evil character is present, hellcats will willingly switch to the new master, even betraying or attacking their former master in the process. In any case, a hellcat is only allowed to remain on the Prime Material Plane for a year and day. At the end of this period they must return to Hell. Sometimes they may later travel to the Prime Material Plane again, but will not necessarily seek out their old master.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (20%). Any magic spell or effect has a 20% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immune to Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more. Other Immunities. Hellcats are immune to the effects of all charm, sleep, hold and suggestion spells.
sections.Special Features: Invisible in Light. In normal lighting, hellcats are invisible. In total darkness however, they can be dimly seen as a glowing reddish aura resembling a large feline. Unarmed Combat. Hellcats cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Horned devil
monsters.attacks: 2 claws (1d4) and 1 bite (1d4+1) and 1 tail (1d3) or 1 weapon and 1 tail (1d3)
monsters.description: Horned devils are inhabitants of the 6th and 7th planes of Hell. Although considered to be greater devils, they are weaker than either ice devils or pit fiends, whom they despise. Horned devils have their own personal names which can be used to summon and control them.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (50%). Any magic spell or effect has a 50% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immune to Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more. Immunities. This creature is immune to fire damage. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Poison (including gases).
sections.Special Features: Fear Aura. Horned devils constantly emanate fear (as the 4th level magic-user spell) in a 5ft radius. Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: animate dead (as the 5th level magic-user spell), charm person (as the 1st level magic-user spell), fear (effect varies, as the 4th level magic-user spell), know alignment (as the 2nd level cleric spell), spectral force (as the 3rd level illusionist spell), suggestion (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), teleport (no chance of error, otherwise as the 5th level magic-user spell), ESP (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), detect magic (as the 1st level magic-user spell), phantasmal force (as the 1st level illusionist spell), pyrotechnics (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), produce flame (as the 2nd level druid spell) or summon another horned devil (50% chance of success). 1/day: wall of fire that inflicts 3d8 hit points of fire damage.
sections.Special Attacks: Melee Weapons. In combat, horned devils typically use either a barbed fork (75%) for 2d6 damage or a jagged whip (25%) that inflicts 1d4 damage plus the victim is stunned 1d4 rounds— save vs spells for unlisted categories to avoid). Wounding Tail. As part of their normal attack, these devils can attack with their sharply-tipped tails, which cause weeping wounds (1d3 damage plus 1 hp of damage per turn until the wound is bound or cured). Unarmed Combat. Horned devils can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, although they usually do not engage in grappling. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +3/-3. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +3/-3.

monsters.name: Ice devil (greater devil)
monsters.attacks: 2 claws (1d4) and 1 mandible (2d4) and 1 tail (3d4) or spear (2d6+4 plus freezing)
monsters.description: Ice devils resemble upright remorhaz with humanoid arms and legs, and knotted, barbed tails. They dominate the 8th plane of Hell, which serves as their frozen home. They are also very strong (18.76 strength) and enjoy torturing their victims before killing them. Ice devils also have secret personal names which can be used to summon them, if the name is somehow known to the conjurer.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (55%). Any magic spell or effect has a 55% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immune to Mundane and +1 Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +2 or more. Immunities. This creature is immune to fire damage. Damage Resistances (all half damage): Cold, Poison (including gases).
sections.Special Features: Regeneration. If injured, the ice devil regenerates 1 hp per round. Fear Aura. Ice devils exude fear (as the 4th level magic-user spell) in a 10ft radius. Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: animate dead (as the 5th level magic-user spell), charm person (as the 1st level magic-user spell), fear (effect varies, as the 4th level magic-user spell), know alignment (as the 2nd level cleric spell), spectral force (as the 3rd level illusionist spell), suggestion (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), teleport (no chance of error, otherwise as the 5th level magic-user spell), detect invisibility (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), detect magic (as the 1st level magic-user spell), fly (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), polymorph self (as the 4th level magic-user spell), wall of ice (as the 4th level magic-user spell), or summon 2 bone devils (70%) or another ice devil (30%) with a 60% chance of success in either case. 1/day: ice storm (as the 4th level magic-user spell).
sections.Special Attacks: Magic Spear. Some ice devils (25% chance) wield long, magical spears which they can use to impale and freeze their victims. The spear inflicts 2d6 piercing damage, and if a victim is hit they must make a saving throw vs. paralysation or be reduced to half their normal move (duration 3d6 rounds). The effect can only reduce a victim to one-quarter move, after which additional attacks have no further effect. Unarmed Combat. Ice devils can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, although they usually do not engage in grappling. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2.

monsters.name: Imp (lesser devil)
monsters.description: Imps are formed from soul worms, created by archdevils to spread evil through service to a lawful evil priest or sorcerer. They are very rarely encountered on the Prime Material Plane, but are commonly seen in the lower planes. They have only average intelligence, but in their role as familiars they are able to rely on the knowledge of their archdevil master. When serving as a familiar to an evil magic-user or cleric, the Imp imparts the following benefits to its master: Constant full-sensory telepathic contact between the Imp and the master up to 1 mile in range. If the master is within 25ft of the imp, the former gains the Imp’s 25% magic resistance and its regeneration ability (1 hp/round). If the master is within 1 mile of the Imp, the former gains an additional level of ability. However, if the imp is killed, the master immediately loses four ability levels.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (25%). Any magic spell or effect has a 25% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immune to Mundane Non-Silver Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more, or is a silver weapon. Other Immunities. Imps are also immune to cold, fire, and electrical damage.
sections.Special Features: Polymorph. Imps are created with the innate ability to polymorph self. The GM should choose two of the following forms (giant rat, goat, large spider, raven). In their polymorphed form, imps are limited to that animal’s natural attacks. Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: detect good (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), detect magic (as the 1st level magic-user spell), and invisibility (as the 2nd level magic-user spell). 1/day: Once per day, an imp can cast a suggestion (as the 3rd level magic-user spell). 1/Week: Once per week it can commune with the lower planes (6 questions maximum, otherwise as the 5th level cleric spell).
sections.Special Attacks: Poison Sting. In their natural form, imps attack with their poison–tipped tail stingers. Any victim struck must save vs poison or die. Unarmed Combat. Imps can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, although they do not use these tactics. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF -4/+4. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -3/+3.

monsters.name: Manalishi (lesser devil; scaly devil, abyssai), black
monsters.description: The manalishi, also known as “scaly devils” and “abyssai,” are quite common on the upper planes of Hell. Most manalishi serve the five-headed dragon queen of Hell. Manalishi are humanoid-shaped with horns, bat-like wings, a long spiked tail, and vaguely draconic features. Certain lemures (5%) are chosen by archdevils to form wraiths, spectres, and other ethereal undead. Lemures cannot normally be destroyed, except by blessed or holy items or weapons.

monsters.name: Shaitan (greater devil; styx fiend)
monsters.description: These devils resemble humanoids with large, bulbous heads and small, evil features. Their wings are black with silver tips. Shaitan dwell on the 5th plane of Hell, where they serve the archdevil, Geryon. Their primary task is to acquire souls for their master. Occasionally, they will travel to the Prime Material plane on a mission of murder and mayhem.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (50%). Any magic spell or effect has a 50% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immune to Non-Silver Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more, or is a silver weapon.
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: animate dead (as the 5th level magic-user spell), charm person (as the 1st level magic-user spell), fear (effect varies, as the 4th level magic-user spell), know alignment (as the 2nd level cleric spell), spectral force (as the 3rd level illusionist spell), suggestion (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), teleport (no chance of error, otherwise as the 5th level magic-user spell). Dispelling. Dispelling a shaitan on the Prime Material plane requires pronouncement of a holy word (the 7th level cleric spell).
sections.Special Attacks: Imprisonment. In combat, these devils will attempt to touch their victim (2d4 damage) and thereby cast an imprisonment spell (as the 9th level magic-user spell). Unarmed Combat. Shaitan devils can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, although they do not use these tactics. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.

monsters.name: Spiked devil (least devil; spined fiend)
monsters.description: Spiked devils are small and weak compared to the other devils, but are amongst the most commonly seen types. They have scaly reddish skin and bat-like wings. A row of dark spines runs from their forehead to the base of their tail. Both their hands and feet have sharp claws. In melee, they usually attack with a trident, fork, or similar pole arm. When flying and attacking a target on the ground, they can also attack with their clawed feet. Spiked devils are typically used for herding assagim or lemures, or serving as a messenger for more powerful devils. These devils rarely have any sort of treasure or possessions beyond their weapon. Only when serving as a messenger are they likely to possess something of value. In these cases, the GM should decide what, if anything, the spiked devil is carrying.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (25%). Any magic spell or effect has a 25% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect.
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: affect normal fires (as the 1st level magic-user spell), change self (as the 1st level illusionist spell), command (as the 1st level cleric spell), produce flame (as the 2nd level druid spell), and scare (as the 2nd level magic-user spell). 1/day: Attempt to summon a barbed devil (5% chance of success).
sections.Special Attacks: Flying Attack. When flying, if attacking a target on the ground, these devils can also attack with their clawed feet. Ranged Attack: Spines. The spiked devil’s spines burst into flame when plucked from the devil’s back. If attacking from above, these devils can also shoot up to 12 of their spines (1d4 damage, like a dart). In melee, should they choose to grapple, 1d4 of the spines will damage the opponent in addition to any grappling damage. Unarmed Combat. Spiked devils can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, although they do not use these tactics. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2.

monsters.name: Pit fiend (greater devil)
monsters.attacks: 1 scimitar (1d8+6) and 1 spiked club (1d6+7) and tail (2d4 constriction)
monsters.description: Pit fiends are native to the 9th Plane of Hell, and are the personal servants of Asmodeus, the Lord of Hell. They are both incredibly strong and diabolically evil. All pit fiends have secret personal names which can be used to summon them.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (65%). Any magic spell or effect has a 65% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immune to Mundane and +1 Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +2 or more.
sections.Special Features: Fear Aura. Pit fiends exude fear (as the 4th level magic-user spell) in a 20ft radius. Regeneration. Pit fiends regenerate 2 hp per combat round until they are killed, at which point the regeneration stops. Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: animate dead (as the 5th level magic-user spell), charm person (as the 1st level magic-user spell), fear (effect varies, as the 4th level magic-user spell), know alignment (as the 2nd level cleric spell), spectral force (as the 3rd level illusionist spell), suggestion (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), teleport (no chance of error, otherwise as the 5th level magic-user spell), detect invisibility (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), detect magic (as the 1st level magic-user spell), hold person (as the 3rd level magic-user spell), polymorph self (as the 4th level magic-user spell), produce flame (as the 2nd level druid spell), pyrotechnics (as the 2nd level magic-user spell), wall of fire (as the 4th level magic-user spell), or summon 1d3 barbed devils (60%) or another pit fiend (70%). 1/day: Once per day, a pit fiend can use a symbol of pain (as the 7th level cleric spell).
sections.Special Attacks: Tail Constriction. In addition to their weapons, pit fiends can also strike with their serpentine tail. A hit causes 2d4 points of constriction damage per round (automatically after a hit) and can only be escaped if the victim makes a successful Open Doors roll as an action. Unarmed Combat. Pit fiends can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and under some circumstances they may use these tactics. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +3/-3. DINOSAURS In OSRIC the “dinosaur” category also includes other creatures contemporaneous with or predating the dinosaurs. This means that for the purposes of the OSRIC core rules, prehistoric creatures such as dimetrodon or plesiosaurus are included with “dinosaurs”, even though palaeontologists classify them separately. These rules do include an indication of the rough period in which the dinosaur lived, but dinosaur-infested areas often resemble Sir Arthur Conan Doyle’s The Lost World in that a mishmash of dinosaurs from different times co-exist. Dinosaur areas are only really suitable for relatively high-level play. Portals to such areas can sometimes be found in the nethermost depths of large dungeons. Unarmed Combat. Dinosaurs cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Tyrannosaurids and allosaurids, albertosaurus
monsters.description: Tyrannosaurids and allosaurids are not related families, but they occupy the same ecological niche: large bipedal carnivores. Allosaurus and saurophaganax are allosaurids, the others are tyrannosaurids. The “Number Encountered” listing allows for two interpretations—they could be solitary predators or pack hunters. Tyrannosaurus: Cretaceous carnivore, long thought to be the largest land carnivore of the dinosaur age. Gorgosaurus: Cretaceous carnivore, smaller than tyrannosaurus. Tarbosaurus: Cretaceous carnivore, closely related to tyrannosaurus. Albertosaurus: Much smaller Cretaceous carnivore. Allosaurus: Jurassic carnivore. Saurophaganax: Jurassic carnivore, may be just a very large allosaurus.

monsters.name: Sauropods, apatosaurus
monsters.description: Edmontosaurus: Cretaceous herbivore, formerly “anatosaurus”. Charonosaurus: Cretaceous herbivore. Shantungosaurus: Cretaceous herbivore. Saurolophus: Cretaceous herbivore. Hypacrosaurus: Cretaceous herbivore. Telmatosaurus: Smaller Cretaceous herbivore. Large quadrupedal herbivores with elephantine bodies and extremely longnecks and tails, the sauropods are herd animals. They can bite, but are only really dangerous when they trample. Trampling automatically kills any creature weighing less than a ton in their path—saving throw vs death to avoid. A whole herd stampeding is an impressive sight, best viewed from a safe distance. In fantasy gaming environments sauropods might make good meat animals or beasts of burden. Apatosaurus: Jurassic herbivore, once called brontosaurus. Diplodocus: Jurassic herbivore, famously long. Brachiosaurus: Jurassic herbivore; long thought to be the largest land dinosaur.

monsters.name: Hadrosaurids, charonosaurus
monsters.description: Herbivores who foraged on all fours and ran on hind legs, there are two main families of the duck–billed dinosaurs known as hadrosaurids: hadrosaurines and lambeosaurines. In game terms there is no difference. Some could be interpreted as Semi-amphibious swamp or wetland dwellers, in which case they should have a swimming move, but many, perhaps all, are fully terrestrial. Trachodon and Anatosaurs are now–superseded names for kinds of hadrosaurid.
