monsters.name: Ceratopsians, centrosaurus
monsters.description: Ceratopsians are quadrupedal beasts with horns and bony head armour. They fill the rhinoceros’ ecological niche. Ceratopsians are bad-tempered and prone to charge, making them among the most dangerous of the dinosaur herbivorous species. They were extremely common during the late cretaceous period. The best known and most common of these creatures, triceratops, was probably about twice as heavy as an elephant. Pentaceratops: Cretaceous herbivore, resembling a triceratops with a longer neck-frill and two extra horns protruding from under its eyes. Triceratops: Cretaceous herbivore. Unlike most other ceratopsians it does not seem to have lived in herds. Diceratops: Cretaceous herbivore; extremely rare compared to triceratops. Styracosaurus: Cretaceous herbivore with a distinctive spiky neck-frill; about half the size of triceratops. Monoclonius: Cretaceous herbivore with only one horn. Centrosaurus: Cretaceous herbivore that seems to have lived in very large herds. Argentinosaurus: Cretaceous herbivore, relatively recently discovered, twice as massive as brachiosaurus. Camarasaurus: Very common Jurassic herbivore. Cetiosaurus: Jurassic herbivore, earlier relative of the other types.

sections.Special Attacks: Trample. Any sauropod listed here can trample as well as bite if the dinosaur can move across the victim’s location. Trampling requires no to-hit roll and requires the target (if the target is smaller than size Huge) to make a saving throw vs. death or be crushed to death under the sauropod’s feet. Stomp. If a ceratopsian attacks (other than with a charge) and exceeds its required “to hit” roll by 4 or more, it has knocked down its target and will stomp on it for an additional 1d10 points of damage. Charge. If a ceratopsian charges and hits, it inflicts triple damage.
sections.Special Features: Segmented Armour Class. Ceratopsians have two AC scores: one for their armoured heads, the other for their bodies.

monsters.name: Other dinosaurs i, anklyosaurus
monsters.description: A miscellany of other kinds of dinosaur, including some (anklyosaurus and stegosaurus) with bony, armoured backs. Both these creatures have an effective attack by clubbing with their tails. GMs who are fans of Jurassic Park may wish to increase the velociraptor’s intelligence score to “semi-” or even “low”. Anklyosaurus: Huge Cretaceous herbivore. Ceratosaurus: Large Jurassic carnivore. Plateosaurus: Large Triassic herbivore. Iguanodon: Large Cretaceous herbivore. Stegosaurus: Huge Jurassic herbivore. Velociraptor: Large Cretaceous carnivore.

sections.Special Attacks: Velociraptor Rake. If a velociraptor hits with its bite, it can bring its rear claws into action as well as its foreclaws. It gains an immediate follow-up attack with the 2 rear claws (2d4), and can continue to attack with the rear claws for as long as it continues to attack the target it bit (as well as normal biting and foreclaws). Dimetrodon is technically a synapsid, and is anachronistic here by quite a large number of millions of years, being more separated from Tyrannosaurus in time than 21st century humans are. It had a huge “sail” on its back that may have helped it regulate its temperature. GMs who are fans of Jurassic Park should note the dilophosaurus presented there was a result of quite a lot of artistic license. Compsognathus: Small Jurassic carnivore. Both these creatures have an effective attack by clubbing with their tails. GMs who are fans of Jurassic Park may wish to increase the velociraptor’s intelligence score to “semi-” or even “low”. Anklyosaurus: Huge Cretaceous herbivore. Ceratosaurus: Large Jurassic carnivore. Plateosaurus: Large Triassic herbivore. Iguanodon: Large Cretaceous herbivore. Stegosaurus: Huge Jurassic herbivore. sections.Special Attacks: Velociraptor Rake. If a velociraptor hits with its bite, it can bring its rear claws into action as well as its foreclaws. It gains an immediate follow-up attack with the 2 rear claws (2d4), and can continue to attack with the rear claws for as long as it continues to attack the target it bit (as well as normal biting and foreclaws). Dimetrodon is technically a synapsid, and is anachronistic here by quite a large number of millions of years, being more separated from Tyrannosaurus in time than 21st century humans are. monsters.name: Marine dinosaurs, archelon
monsters.description: None of these creatures are technically dinosaurs, though all are found in “Lost World” areas. Dunkleosteus can swallow prey whole on a roll of “20” “to hit” and actually preceded the dinosaurs by many millions of years. Elasmosaurus can also swallow whole, needing only 18–20 on its “to hit” roll to do so but otherwise as dunkleosteus. Mosasaurus filled the same ecological niche as sharks. Plesiosaurs may have preferred smaller prey than a man but would still be dangerous. Nothosaurs were amphibious, like huge seals. Archelon was a kind of gigantic turtle. Dunkleosteus: Formerly known as dinichthys; Huge Devonian carnivore. Elasmosaurus: Huge Cretaceous carnivore. Mosasaurus: Huge Cretaceous carnivore. Plesiosaurus: Huge Jurassic carnivore. Nothosaurus: Large Triassic carnivore. Archelon: Huge Cretaceous carnivore.

sections.Special Attacks: Dunkleosteus can swallow prey whole on a to-hit roll of 20. Elasmosaurus can also swallow whole, needing only 18–20 on its “to hit” roll. Swallow Whole. On a bite attack that rolls a natural 20, the dinosaur swallows the victim. If the victim is not rescued, they will die at the end of 6 rounds spent in the creature’s stomach. It is possible for the victim to cut their way out (the inside is armour class 10 [10]). For each round the victim is inside, subtract 1 from their damage that they inflict. This penalty is cumulative for each round, so after four rounds the damage inflicted is at -4.

monsters.name: Disenchanter
monsters.description: The disenchanter resembles a rather bizarre cross between a dromedary camel and a cow, with a muscular prehensile snout stuck on for good measure. Colouration is a shimmery electric blue, and the entire creature appears to be somewhat translucent and difficult for the eye to focus upon. The disenchanter is a thaumivore, feeding on magical power. It sucks the dweomer from enchanted objects by attaching its snout to them with a successful “to hit” roll. The disenchanter can only be hit by magic weapons but doing so will not affect the dweomer of the weapon; only the snout has the ability to disenchant items. Even the wisest and most learned of sages know nothing about the ecology of the disenchanter or why it seems to be able to sustain itself only with magic items.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more.
sections.Special Attacks: Disenchant Item. One touch (a normal to-hit roll) is all it takes for the disenchanter’s snout to render any magic item (except major artifacts) completely inert. The creature has no other attacks and causes no physical damage of any kind. The muscular snout can be extended as much as 5ft and the disenchanter is capable of detecting relative strengths of magic enchantment, knowing, for instance, that plate mail +5 will be a tastier morsel than a mere +1 ring of protection. Unarmed Combat. Disenchanters cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Djinn (genie), djinni
monsters.description: Djinn (singular “djinni”) come from the Elemental Plane of Air and are quite magical. They can travel the elemental planes and the Astral Plane, as well as the Prime Material. If subdued, they can be enslaved for 1,001 days. Once their service has expired, they are free and may not become enslaved again by the same creature. A djinni can carry up to 600 lbs without tiring, either flying or walking. A djinni is able to carry double the weight on foot but only for about thirty minutes. A djinni will require an hour’s rest for every 30 minutes of carrying.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: If any attack is made on the djinni by an airborne attacker, the attack will be at -1 “to hit” and -1 to damage.
sections.Special Features: Spell-like Abilities. At Will: Djinns can become invisible or enter gaseous form at will. In gaseous form, the creature takes on a translucent, gaseous consistency and floats at 30ft per round. This speed can be different depending on natural wind speed in the environment or due to the effects of wind–altering spells. While in gaseous form, the creature can flow below doors and other small spaces not sealed airtight. Although magical lightning and fire do the gaseous form full damage, the creature is impervious to all other attacks. 1/day: Djinn can perform any of the following abilities once per day: create food for up to 12 people; create water or wine for up to 12 people; create up to 16 cubicft of cloth, 9 cubicft of wood, or 100 pounds of metal (the metal is not permanent and will disappear within a day); create an illusion with both sight and sound that will act on its own without being controlled. The illusion will last until it is dispelled or touched. Three Wishes (Noble Djinn only). If subdued, a noble djinni need only grant three wishes to be released from service. The djinni can effectively cast three wish spells per day, but if the djinni is angry at the person asking for the wishes the wording of the request should be very specific, because the djinni will comply with the least beneficial interpretation possible.
sections.Special Attacks: Once per day, djinn can assume the form of a whirlwind 7ft tall, 3ft across at the top, and 1ft across at the bottom. This lasts for an entire round and does 2d6 hit points of damage to all creatures caught in its path (3d6 for a noble djinn). Any creature with less than 2 hit dice are killed instantly. The djinni can move 30ft in one round while in whirlwind form, but can turn while moving, to hit a large number of opponents. Unarmed Combat. Djinn can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and under some circumstances they may use these tactics. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2.
sections.Language: Djinn speak the language of the elemental plane of air, but they also have a limited form of telepathy that enables them to communicate with any intelligent creature.

monsters.name: Dog, war dog (mastiff)
monsters.description: War Dogs are usually large mastiffs or pit bulls, trained to fight or guard a location. They are typically armoured in leather. They do not check morale and are trained not to accept food from strangers. Most dogs are in the “Ordinary or Wild” category, including most guard dogs. All dogs have a 25% chance to detect the presence of an invisible person by smell. How the dog reacts to it depends on training. A war dog will usually be trained to attempt an attack (still with a -4 to hit), a guard dog may be trained to bark at anything suspicious, and a relatively untrained dog may just follow the invisible person’s scent until something causes it to react differently. Unarmed Combat. Dogs cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, but war dogs may be trained to overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF na/na.

monsters.name: Doppelgänger
monsters.description: Doppelgängers are strange beings that are able to take on the forms of those they encounter, including the appearance of equipment and any clothing the victim is wearing. In its natural form, a doppelgänger is a 5ft to 6ft tall humanoid, slender with gangly limbs and half-formed features. Its flesh is pale and hairless, and its large, bulging eyes are yellow with slitted pupils. The creature will assume its natural form upon death. Doppelgängers make excellent use of their natural mimicry to stage ambushes, bait traps, and infiltrate society. Their classic tactic in a dungeon is to take the form of a member of an adventuring party, dispatch them, and take their place amongst the group until a good time presents itself to kill them or rob them. Initiative and Surprise Stealth. Doppelgangers surprise with a roll of 1–4 on 1d6.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immunities. Doppelgangers are immune to the effects of charm and sleep spells. Improved Saving Throw. Doppelgängers make saving throws as a 10HD monster.
sections.Special Features: ESP. Doppelgangers can use ESP (as per the spell) at will. Natural Disguise. A doppelgänger can assume any humanoid form between 4ft to 8ft tall, but the creature must first see the victim to be copied. Any doppelgänger’s attempt at physical disguise is only faulty 10% of the time, and its knowledge of the victim is facilitated by the doppelgänger’s innate ESP ability. Unarmed Combat. Doppelgangers can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and under some circumstances they may use these tactics. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

monsters.name: Dracolisk
monsters.description: Dracolisks are surmised to be the result of the mating of a black dragon and a basilisk, though rumours persist of the existence of other sorts. These fearsome creatures most resemble their draconic sires, being armoured with thick black scales and having the horns and sharp toothed maws of their forebears; they also have six powerful clawed limbs and two large wings. Although capable of flight, dracolisks are limited to only short durations, ten or twenty minutes at the most, before they have to rest, so they principally use this form of movement to swoop down upon or escape from foes.

sections.Special Features: Additionally, anybody unfortunate enough to be within 30ft of a dracolisk and meet its gaze must make a saving throw vs petrifaction or be turned to stone. As with its basilisk parent, the gaze attack of the dracolisk extends into the astral and ethereal planes and those who seek to avoid looking directly at the beast attack with a -4 penalty.
sections.Special Attacks: Breath Weapon (3/day). Up to thrice a day, a dracolisk is capable of shooting an acid stream out of its mouth up to 30ft and with a width of 5ft; this causes 4d6 damage to anybody caught in its path, though a successful saving throw vs breath weapons reduces this by half. Unarmed Combat. Dracolisks cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.
sections.Language: If a dracolisk speaks a language at all, it is usually draconic, though it may be that some can understand other languages. DRAGONS Dragons are, in many ways, the archetypal adversaries in OS- RIC-compatible games. Some dragons are weak enough that even a relatively low level party can have a chance to fight a dragon— while others are powerful enough to pose a challenge even to a high-level party. Even parties of very high average level may well struggle to defeat a mated pair, or family group, of elder dragons! Dragons come in various colours. In many campaigns, these colours are literal—fire-breathing dragons really do always have red scales—but in others, they may be metaphorical, allowing (for example) a green or brown “red” dragon. Some campaigns also allow the possibility of dragons with more than 8 hp per die and dragons with d10, d12 or even larger Hit Dice are possible. There are some traits that are generally common to all dragons, no matter the colour or alignment. First, if issued with a formal challenge, a dragon will sometimes agree to fight until subdued HIT AGE CATEGORY AGE PER 1 Hatchling, Younger than 6 years. 1 2 Young dragon, 6 years to 15 years 2 3 Adolescent dragon, 16 years to 25 years 3 4 Young adult dragon, 26 to 50 years 4 5 Adult dragon, 51 to 100 years 5 6 Old dragon, 101 to 200 years 6 7 Very old dragon, 201 to 400 years 7 8 Ancient, 401 years and older 8 rather than to the death. The GM should rule about the likelihood of the dragon’s acceptance and the conditions that apply, since these will depend on the nature of the challenge and the alignment of the dragon. Second, dragons grow more powerful as they age (see Age Categories, below). Dragons do not roll dice for their hit points or breath weapons; these are determined by age category, which also influences a saving throw bonus and the ability to perceive invisible opponents. Third, dragons radiate an aura of fear (as the 4th level magic-user spell) affecting creatures of less than 5th level unless they save vs magic. Unarmed Combat. Dragons cannot be overborne or grappled. A dragon might choose to overbear. Stats for unarmed combat vary by size, so the GM will have to calculate those. (Although the to-hit number will be 2+). Size and Hit Dice Most dragon types have 3 possibilities for their hit dice (Example: Black dragons have 6 to 8 HD). Roll a d8 to determine a dragon’s hit dice, with 1-2 indicating the smallest (a black dragon with 6 hit dice), 3-7 indicating the middle number (a black dragon with 7 hit dice), and an 8 indicating the highest number (a black dragon with 8 hit dice). For a dragon with the smallest HD number (our 6HD black dragon), the dragon’s size will be approximately 4ft of body length (not including the neck or tail) per age category (see below). The middle HD number will have a body length of 5ft per age category, and the highest HD number will have a body length of 6ft per age category. The tails and necks of dragons vary, but a dragon’s full length is usually about 3-4 times its body length. Any dragon with a body length of 9ft or less is considered Medium, a body length of 10-20ft is Large, and a body length larger than 20ft is Huge. Age Categories Roll 1d8 to determine the age category of a randomly-encountered dragon. Dragon hit points and breath weapon damage are determined by the dragon’s age category, and older dragons have a bonus to all saving throws. monsters.name: Dragon, black
monsters.senses: Infravision 60ft, Detect invisibility by age category
monsters.experience: Varies by hit dice and age
monsters.description: Viking champions such as Ragnar Lodbrok and Sigurd the Volsung fought fearsome dragons that spewed a corrosive venom, deadly to the touch. These dragons are the deadly black dragons. Black dragons are found mostly in swamps, marshes and deep, dark caves.

sections.Special Features: Sleeping Dragon. A black dragon encountered in its lair has a 50% chance to be sleeping when the adventurers approach. If the dragon is asleep, there is a 1 in 6 chance that it will awaken from the mere presence of adventurers. Dragons also sometimes feign sleep. Spellcasting Dragon. Only 10% of black dragons are spellcasters. If it can cast spells, it does so as a magic-user, half the dragon’s age category in level (1-2=1, 3-4=2, etc.).
sections.Special Attacks: Breath Weapon. Black dragon breath is a stream of corrosive, acidic venom, 50ft long×5ft wide. It does corrosion damage equal to the dragon’s (uninjured) hit points to everyone in the area of effect, but a saving throw vs dragon breath reduces this amount to half damage. The dragon may use this breath weapon up to three times per day.
sections.Language: All dragons speak the draconic tongue, and there is a 30% chance that a black dragon will also be able to speak common.

monsters.name: Dragon, blue
monsters.senses: Infravision 60ft, Detect invisibility by age category
monsters.experience: Varies by hit dice and age
monsters.description: Deserts and dry wastes are home to the deadly blue dragons. These creatures usually dwell in vast caves or deserted towers in arid lands.

sections.Special Features: Sleeping Dragon. A blue dragon encountered in its lair has a 30% chance to be sleeping when the adventurers approach. If the dragon is asleep, there is a 1 in 6 chance that it will awaken from the mere presence of adventurers. Dragons also sometimes feign sleep. Spellcasting Dragon. Roughly 30% of blue dragons are spellcasters. If it can cast spells, it does so as a magic-user with a level equal to the dragon’s age category.
sections.Special Attacks: Breath Weapon. Blue dragon breath is a bolt of lightning, 100ft long×5ft wide. It does electrical damage equal to the dragon’s (uninjured) hit points to everyone in the area of effect, but a saving throw vs dragon breath reduces this amount to half damage. The dragon may use this breath weapon up to three times per day.
sections.Language: All dragons speak the draconic tongue, and there is a 60% chance that a blue dragon will also be able to speak common.

monsters.name: Dragon, brass
monsters.senses: Infravision 60ft, Detect invisibility by age category
monsters.experience: Varies by hit dice and age
monsters.description: The blue dragons of the desert must contend with their deadly rivals, the brass dragons, who love the same arid caves. The brass dragons are not the vicious killers that the blue dragons are, although their good nature is sometimes overcome with doses of greed and self-interest.

sections.Special Features: Sleeping Dragon. A brass dragon encountered in its lair has a 50% chance to be sleeping when the adventurers approach. If the dragon is asleep, there is a 1 in 6 chance that it will awaken from the mere presence of adventurers. Dragons also sometimes feign sleep. Spellcasting Dragon. Roughly 30% of brass dragons are spellcasters. If it can cast spells, it does so as a magic-user, half the dragon’s age category in level (1-2=1, 3-4=2, etc.).
sections.Special Attacks: Breath Weapon. Brass dragon breath is either a cone of sleep-inducing gas (70ft×20ft), or a cloud of fear gas (40ft×50ft,×20ft), at the dragon’s choice of how to breathe. The dragon may use either breath weapon up to a total of three times per day. A saving throw vs. dragon breath negates the effect of the breath. Saves against a 6HD dragon’s breath are at a +2, but they are made at -2 against that of an 8HD dragon. The duration of the effect is 10 rounds.
sections.Language: All dragons speak the draconic tongue, and there is a 30% chance that a brass dragon will also be able to speak common.

monsters.name: Dragon, bronze
monsters.senses: Infravision 60ft, Detect invisibility by age category
monsters.experience: Varies by hit dice and age
monsters.description: The reclusive bronze dragons live in caverns in temperate climates. They are interested in the ways of humanity and often use shape-changing powers to watch, observe and help people. They prefer to have their lairs in places isolated from prying eyes, however, and thus often place their entrances in lakes or ponds. They have found that their treasure hordes are tempting targets for evil or even neutral adventurers.

sections.Special Features: Sleeping Dragon. A bronze dragon encountered in its lair has a 25% chance to be sleeping when the adventurers approach. If the dragon is asleep, there is a 1 in 6 chance that it will awaken from the mere presence of adventurers. Dragons also sometimes feign sleep. Spellcasting Dragon. Roughly 60% of bronze dragons are spellcasters. If it can cast spells, it does so as a magic-user with a level equal to the dragon’s age category.
sections.Special Attacks: Breath Weapon. Bronze dragon breath is (at the dragon’s choice) one of two types. The first is a bolt of lightning, 100ft long and 5ft wide. It does damage equal to the dragon’s hit points (but a save vs dragon breath halves this amount). The other option is to breathe a cloud of repulsion gas (20ft×30ft×30ft) which requires all subjects to save vs dragon breath or be repulsed for 6 minutes (as per the level 6 magic-user spell). The dragon may use breath weapons up to three times per day.
sections.Language: All dragons speak the draconic tongue, and there is a 60% chance that a bronze dragon will also be able to speak common.

monsters.name: Dragon, copper
monsters.senses: Infravision 60ft, Detect invisibility by age category
monsters.experience: Varies by hit dice and age
monsters.description: Copper dragons live in wild and rugged places. They do not seek out the company of humans and are quite reclusive. However, they have a strong sense of morality, and will occasionally assist humans in need. When they do, they are happy to accept any reward offered, for they are as greedy as most other dragon types.

sections.Special Features: Sleeping Dragon. A copper dragon encountered in its lair has a 40% chance to be sleeping when the adventurers approach. If the dragon is asleep, there is a 1 in 6 chance that it will awaken from the mere presence of adventurers. Dragons also sometimes feign sleep. Spellcasting Dragon. Roughly 40% of bronze dragons are spellcasters. If it can cast spells, it does so as a magic-user with a level equal to the dragon’s age category.
sections.Special Attacks: Breath Weapon. Copper dragon breath is a blast of acid, like a black dragon’s breath, that does damage equal to the dragon’s hit points (but a save vs dragon breath halves this amount); or it may breathe a cloud of slowing gas (20ft×30ft×30ft) which requires all subjects to save vs breath weapon or be slowed (as the spell) for 6 minutes. The dragon may use breath weapons up to three times per day.
sections.Language: All dragons speak the draconic tongue, and there is a 45% chance that a copper dragon will also be able to speak common.

monsters.name: Dragon, gold
monsters.senses: Infravision 60ft, Detect invisibility by age category
monsters.experience: Varies by hit dice and age
monsters.description: Often shaped like the sinuous dragons of Asian myth, gold dragons epitomise law and goodness, and are typically just and kindly. They are interested in the ways of man and often use shape-changing powers to watch, observe and help people. They prefer to have their lairs in places isolated from prying eyes, however, and thus often place their entrances in lakes or ponds. They have found that their treasure hordes are tempting targets for evil or even neutral adventurers.

sections.Special Features: Sleeping Dragon. A gold dragon encountered in its lair has a 10% chance to be sleeping when the adventurers approach. If the dragon is asleep, there is a 1 in 6 chance that it will awaken from the mere presence of adventurers. Dragons also sometimes feign sleep. Spellcasting Dragon. Roughly 90% of gold dragons are spellcasters. If it can cast spells, it does so as a magic-user with a level equal to the dragon’s age category. Polymorph. A gold dragon can cast polymorph self as an innate ability three times per day.
sections.Special Attacks: Breath Weapon. Gold dragon breath is a blast of fire (like that of a red dragon) or a cloud of poison gas (like a green dragon), at the dragon’s option. The dragon may use breath weapons up to three times per day.
sections.Language: All dragons speak the draconic tongue, and there is a 90% chance that a gold dragon will also be able to speak common.

monsters.name: Dragon, green
monsters.senses: Infravision 60ft, Detect invisibility by age category
monsters.experience: Varies by hit dice and age
monsters.description: Particularly renowned for their foul temper, which is said to be even more venomous than their breath, green dragons prefer to live in caverns or ruins in or near forests.

sections.Special Features: Sleeping Dragon. A green dragon encountered in its lair has a 40% chance to be sleeping when the adventurers approach. If the dragon is asleep, there is a 1 in 6 chance that it will awaken from the mere presence of adventurers. Dragons also sometimes feign sleep. Spellcasting Dragon. Roughly 20% of green dragons are spellcasters. If it can cast spells, it does so as a magic-user with a level equal to the dragon’s age category.
sections.Special Attacks: Breath Weapon. Green dragon breath is a cloud of toxic gas, 50ft long, 40ft wide, and 30ft high. It does poison damage equal to the dragon’s (uninjured) hit points to everyone in the area of effect, but a saving throw vs dragon breath reduces this amount to half damage. The dragon may use this breath weapon up to three times per day.
sections.Language: All dragons speak the draconic tongue, and there is a 45% chance that a green dragon will also be able to speak common.

monsters.name: Dragon, red
monsters.senses: Infravision 60ft, Detect invisibility by age category
monsters.experience: Varies by hit dice and age
monsters.description: The archetypal red dragon is Smaug from The Hobbit.

sections.Special Features: Sleeping Dragon. A red dragon encountered in its lair has a 20% chance to be sleeping when the adventurers approach. If the dragon is asleep, there is a 1 in 6 chance that it will awaken from the mere presence of adventurers. Dragons also sometimes feign sleep. Spellcasting Dragon. Roughly 40% of red dragons are spellcasters. If it can cast spells, it does so as a magic-user with a level equal to the dragon’s age category.
sections.Special Attacks: Breath Weapon. Red dragon breath is a cone of flame, 90ft long and 15ft radius at the base, emanating from the mouth of the creature. It does fire damage equal to the dragon’s (uninjured) hit points to everyone in the area of effect, but a saving throw vs dragon breath reduces this amount to half damage. The dragon may use this breath weapon up to three times per day.
sections.Language: All dragons speak the draconic tongue, and there is an 80% chance that a red dragon will also be able to speak common.

monsters.name: Dragon, silver
monsters.senses: Infravision 60ft, Detect invisibility by age category
monsters.experience: Varies by hit dice and age
monsters.description: Dwelling in high places such as mountaintops or among the clouds, like gold dragons, silver dragons epitomise law and goodness. They are interested in the ways of humankind and often use shape-changing powers to watch, observe and help people. They prefer to have their lairs in places isolated from prying eyes, however, and thus often place their entrances in lakes or ponds. They have found that their treasure hordes are tempting targets for evil or even neutral adventurers.

sections.Special Features: Polymorph. A silver dragon can cast polymorph self as an innate ability three times per day. Sleeping Dragon. A silver dragon encountered in its lair has a 15% chance to be sleeping when the adventurers approach. If the dragon is asleep, there is a 1 in 6 chance that it will awaken from the mere presence of adventurers. Dragons also sometimes feign sleep. Spellcasting Dragon. Roughly 75% of silver dragons who can speak are spellcasters. If it can cast spells, it does so as a magic-user with a level equal to the dragon’s age category.
sections.Special Attacks: Breath Weapon. Silver dragon breath is a blast of frost (like that of a white dragon) or a cloud of paralysing gas (like a green dragon except those who fail their saves are paralysed for 3d4 turns), at the dragon’s option. The dragon may use breath weapons up to three times per day.
sections.Language: All dragons speak the draconic tongue, and there is a 75% chance that a silver dragon will also be able to speak common.

monsters.name: Dragon, white
monsters.senses: Infravision 60ft, Detect invisibility by age category
monsters.experience: Varies by hit dice and age
monsters.description: Almost the antithesis of the fiery red dragon is the frost-rimed white dragon of the frigid north. Although lesser than their red cousins in size, power and intelligence, they are at least as evil.

sections.Special Features: Sleeping Dragon. A white dragon encountered in its lair has a 60% chance to be sleeping when the adventurers approach. If the dragon is asleep, there is a 1 in 6 chance that it will awaken from the mere presence of adventurers. Dragons also sometimes feign sleep. Spellcasting Dragon. Only 5% of white dragons are spellcasters. If it can cast spells, it does so as a magic-user, half the dragon’s age category in level (age category 1-2= level 1, category 3-4= level 2, etc.).
sections.Special Attacks: Breath Weapon. White dragon breath is a cone of deadly frost, 50ft long and 25ft diameter at the base. It does damage equal to the dragon’s (uninjured) hit points to all in the area of effect, but a save vs breath weapons reduces the damage to half. The dragon may use this breath weapon up to three times per day.
sections.Language: All dragons speak the draconic tongue, and there is a 20% chance that a white dragon will also be able to speak common.

monsters.name: Dragon turtle
monsters.senses: Standard, Detect invisible 25%, 35%, 45% or 55% by HD
monsters.description: 15HD: 4600 +19/HP Dragon turtles are not true dragons, but they are clearly related, looking much like a dragon with a turtle shell.

sections.Special Attacks: Breath Weapon. Dragon turtles can breathe a cone of steam, 60ft long and 40ft wide at the base. It does damage equal to the dragon turtle’s (uninjured) hit points to all in the area of effect, but a save vs breath weapons reduces the damage to half. The dragon turtle may use this breath weapon up to three times per day. Unarmed Combat. Dragon turtles cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.
sections.Language: Dragon turtles speak their own language and that of the Neutral alignment. There is a 20% chance that a dragon turtle will also be able to speak common.

monsters.name: Dryad
monsters.description: Dryads are tree sprites who dwell in the most remote locations. Dryads are female, although male “hamadryads” are encountered just as often. Dryads all have a home tree that houses their spirits (if this tree is killed, the dryad dies). They are never far (400 yards, or thereabouts) from this spirit-tree. Dryads are non-violent and will never attack unless they have no other choice. Dryads and hamadryads, as fey creatures, have a tendency to kidnap humans using their charm ability. If successful, there is a 50% chance the victim will never be seen again. If they do return to civilisation, it will be at least 1d4 years later.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (50%). Any magic spell or effect has a 50% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect.
sections.Spell-Like Abilities: At Will: Dryads can dimension door by stepping into any nearby tree, returning to their own spirit-tree. 3/day: A dryad can cast a charm person spell thrice per day. Unarmed Combat. Dryads and hamadryads can make grappling or overbearing attacks, but ordinarily don’t. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/ DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.
sections.Language: Dryads have their own language as well as elven, pixie, sprite, and they can also speak with animals.

monsters.name: Dwarf
monsters.loot: Individual 4 (x5); in lair Hoard 7, Cache 3 (x20) and 4
monsters.description: Dwarfs are sturdy demi-humans who live in extended clans. They typically make their homes in rocky hills. Dwarfs are led by higher level leader types (additional to the number encountered die roll) as follows: • For every 40 dwarfs: 2nd to 6th level fighter (1d6, 1 = 2nd level, 2–6 = level indicated by die roll). • If over 160 dwarfs: 1 6th level fighter (chief) & 1 4th level fighter (lieutenant). • If over 200 dwarfs: 1 fighter/cleric (of 3rd to 6th level as fighter and 4th to 7th level as cleric). • If over 320 dwarfs: 1 8th level fighter, 1 7th level fighter, 1 6th level fighter/ 7th level cleric. • If encountered in their lair: 2d6 fighters (2nd to 5th level), 2d4 fighter/clerics (2nd to 4th level), plus 1d100 noncombatant dwarfs. Higher level fighters and fighter/clerics have a 10% chance (per level) of having magic armour or weapons. Dwarfs are typically armoured in chain mail and carry shields. Axes and hammers are their weapons of choice. Dwarfs receive a +1 on “to hit” rolls vs goblins, orcs, and hobgoblins due to their intense hatred of these ancestries. When in melee with giants, trolls, and ogres, these opponents must fight at -4 due to their size and the skill of dwarfs in fighting such opponents. Description: Dwarfs grow long beards, and usually favour dark, sombre colours for their clothing, with flashes of bright colours. They are short but have stocky builds and are known for their great strength. In some campaign worlds, they may wear kilts. Mountain Dwarfs: These dwarfs are similar to their cousins, the hill dwarfs (described above), except they have 1d8+1 hit dice and they are slightly taller (4.5ft tall).

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Saving Throw Bonus (Poison and Magic). Dwarfs are a hardy people, and save vs poison and magic as if they were 4 levels (or hit dice) higher than their actual level.
sections.Special Features: Ancestral Features. Dwarfs have the same ancestral features as dwarven player characters. Unarmed Combat. For a dwarf wearing chainmail: If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 14+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-0. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2.
sections.Language: Dwarfs speak common, goblin, gnome, kobold, and orc in addition to their own tongue.

monsters.name: Eel, giant, moray
monsters.description: GIANT MORAY EELS Giant morays are saltwater dwellers with a nasty temper and a mouth full of teeth. Though they will generally keep to themselves if not molested, giant moray eels are often found in the service of locathah (q.v.) as both battle mounts and guards. Giant morays encountered in those circumstances are extremely aggressive. On rare occasions, a giant moray eel will be found in fresh water. GIANT ELECTRIC EELS Electric eels are non-aggressive freshwater dwellers, preferring warm water. Rumours persist of a saltwater electric eel which is double the size and delivers a jolt twice as powerful.

sections.Special Attacks: Electric Jolt. If an electric eel feels threatened or is attacked it will discharge a jolt of electricity. This electrical charge causes any creature within 5ft of the eel to take 3d8 points of damage, all creatures within a 5ft to 10ft range will take 2d8 points of damage, and all creatures within 10ft to 15ft take 1d8 hp damage. No saving throw is allowed, though certain magic items and spells may grant immunity or reduced damage from the electrical attack. WEED EELS Weed eels are found in both salt and fresh water, preferring depths of around 30ft. Weed eels are so-called because of their brownish green colouration, and because they tend to anchor themselves in the rocks and dirt of the sea or lake bed, looking for all the world like a bed of seaweed. A weed eel lair consists of many small tunnels of about 6 inches diameter which eventually join into a series of 6ft tunnels, which in turn lead to a large cave which is the actual lair. The cave is usually about 600 square ft and the eels pave the bottom of it with any suitable material they find: small stones, gems, coins, and similar-sized shiny objects. Any attempt by anyone or anything other than a weed eel to enter any hole leading to the lair will provoke an immediate attack by every eel in the colony. Poison Bite. Weed eels have a single biting attack which injects a powerful poison into the wound: the victim must save or die.

monsters.name: Efreet
monsters.description: Efreet are creatures from the Elemental Plane of Fire, and can travel the elemental planes (although they usually avoid the Elemental Plane of Water), the ethereal or astral planes, and the Prime Material Plane. They hate djinn and attack them on sight. They are lawful and follow agreements and contracts to the letter, if not necessarily the original intention. An agreement or contract to serve, if you can persuade or threaten the efreet into consenting to one, binds the efreet to obedience for 1,001 days or until it has granted three wishes, whichever is earlier. Once the Efreet’s service is complete, it is freed, and cannot be subdued by the same person again. Efreet are strong and can carry 750 lbs without being encumbered.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to fire. Efreet ignore fire damage and fire-related effects.
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. Efreet can cast the following spells, without material components: At Will: detect magic, enlarge (only on the efreet itself), invisibility (only on the efreet itself), polymorph self, wall of fire, Improved phantasmal force. Gaseous Form. Efreet can turn themselves to a cloud of luminous, burning flame. While in this form, the Efreet can fit through a gap one inch wide, can’t be restrained, and isn’t affected by being prone. Three Wishes. Many efreet can cast the wish spell, but only to grant another’s wish—they can’t grant wishes for themselves or for other efreet. They can use this power to grant up to three wishes, and regain spent uses at dawn. Some efreet don’t have this power.
sections.Special Attacks: Ranged Attack (Hurl Flame). Efreet can attack with 1 hurled flame (3d6 fire damage) with a range of 90ft (not modified by range increments). Unarmed Combat. Efreet can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and under some circumstances they may use these tactics. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2.
sections.Languages: Efreet have limited telepathy. Any creature that understands at least one language, understands the efreet; and the efreet can understand it. In addition, efreet have their own language, and all speak Ignan, the lingua franca of the Elemental Plane of Fire. Almost all efreet met on the Prime Material Plane also speak Common and many speak other languages as well.

monsters.name: Elemental, air
monsters.description: 16 HD: 3,650 +20/hp 16 HD: 3,650 Elementals are formless (but material) manifestations of a spirit from one of the elemental planes of existence, which takes shape as a pure and animate form of the element. They are usually summoned by a spell, but can also form in places of high magic or with a close connection to the elemental plane. Unarmed Combat. Elementals cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not usually employ these tactics other than occasionally overbearing.

monsters.name: Elephant, african
monsters.description: Elephants are large mammals found in subtropical climates, where they roam wide open plains and grasslands in small herds or families. They have a tough hoary grey hide, four sturdy legs, two large tusks, a great trunk that they use to manipulate their surroundings and two very large ears. African elephants are typically larger than their Asian cousins and have proportionally larger ears, but both are relatively intelligent animals that can be trained to work as beasts of burden and obey simple commands and are occasionally even used for warfare. Mammoths and mastodons are thought to be the ancestors of the common elephant, the principal difference being their great woolly coats, which make them better suited to subarctic environments. In general, elephants are relatively peaceful creatures, but when roused they can be devastating. Treasure: Ivory is worth 1d6×100 gp per tusk. An elephant tusk is hugely encumbering (due to the size as much as the weight).

sections.Special Attacks: Limitation on Multiple Attacks. No single opponent may be subject to more than two of an elephant’s attacks at one time, though elephants can simultaneously combat as many enemies as it has attacks. Unarmed Combat. Elephants cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Elf
monsters.description: Sometimes elves live in a complex civilisation, other times they are found living in wild bands. While there are several different types of elves, most do share the following traits: Elves live in a rather loose society where independent clans pledge their support to a central ruler. They will likely place their homes in a secluded thicket or meadow. When encountered in groups of 20 or more there will likely be a fighter of 2nd level or better. If there are 40 or more then there will probably be a 2nd level fighter / 2nd level magic-user or better in the group. If there are 100 or more elves then the leader is likely to be a 4th level fighter / 8th level magic-user with 2 additional 4th level fighters / 5th level magic-users, and a 4th level fighter / 4th level magic-user / 4th level cleric. Typically elves will wear scale, ring, or chain armour and shield. They will be usually armed with spears, swords, and bows. Higher level fighter / magic-users and fighter / magic-user / clerics have a 10% chance per level per class to possess some sort of usable magic item.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Elves have the ability to move quietly when in natural surroundings, and are able to surprise on a roll of 1–4 on a d6 in a normal, unexpected encounter. Undetectable in Certain Surroundings. Elves are able to blend into foliage and become virtually invisible, so long as they do not attack. In forested terrain, this allows for undetectable ambushes with one round of automatic surprise.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Resistance to Sleep and Charm. Elves have a 90% resistance to sleep and charm effects.
sections.Special Features: Ancestral Features. Elves have the same ancestral features as a player character elf.
sections.Special Attacks: Melee Attack. Elves attack with a +1 “to hit” with longswords. Ranged Attack. When using any pulled bow elves receive a +1 to their attack roll. Unarmed Combat. For an elf wearing chainmail: If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 14+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/ DEF +6/-4. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.
sections.Language: Elves have their own language, and can also speak common, goblin, orc, hobgoblin, gnoll, halfling, and gnome.

monsters.name: Ettercap
monsters.description: Ettercaps appear to be humanoid arachnids. An ettercap will use its silk to prepare traps around its lair, such as webs and tripwires, and may use a silk-based weapon such as a lasso or garrotte. Ettercaps can communicate with spiders of all types, and they are often found working together with giant spiders.

sections.Special Features: Webs. Ettercaps can spin silk from their short, stubby tails like a giant spider does. These are used to create traps around the lair, or to snare passers-by in ambushes.
sections.Special Attacks: Poison Bite. The ettercap’s bite is venomous. Anyone bitten must make a saving throw vs. poison or die. Unarmed Combat. Ettercaps can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, although they don’t use these tactics. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

monsters.name: Ettin
monsters.loot: Cache 1 each; Hoard 3 and Cache 11 in lair
monsters.description: Ettins are two-headed giants, nocturnal creatures that live below ground. Each of an ettin’s heads controls one arm. The right side is slightly dominant, and can cause 3d6 damage whereas the left can inflict 2d8. Ettins are seldom surprised because one head or the other is usually keeping watch.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Ettins are only surprised on a 1 in 6. Unarmed Combat. Ettins can attack and be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2.
sections.Language: Ettins speak giantish, and each head has a 20% chance to speak common.

monsters.name: Executioner’s hood
monsters.description: A small, weird monster that may be related to the lurker above, the executioner’s hood often dwells underground or in ruins. The creature drops from above to cover a victim’s head and suffocate them. Because the executioner’s hood actually surrounds its victim’s head, any attack affecting the creature will also affect its victim. The only known ways to remove an executioner’s hood are to kill it or to bathe it in alcohol, which will intoxicate it until it becomes flaccid and helpless.

sections.Special Attacks: Strangle. The executioner’s hood drops from niches, cracks or anchor-points on the ceiling onto its victim’s head and begins to strangle. If its first attack is successful, the creature will hit automatically each round thereafter, inflicting rolled damage (1d4 hp). Unarmed Combat. Executioner’s hoods cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Eye of the deep
monsters.description: The eye of the deep is a fish, globular in shape (about 4ft in diameter) with a massive central eye. Two further eyes on stalks sprout from the top of the monster, two huge lobster-like pincers emerge from the side, and it has a gaping maw below.

sections.Special Attacks: Each eye has a unique power. Central Eye. The central eye can fire a cone 30ft long and 20ft in diameter at the base that stuns all within the area of effect for 2d4 rounds (save vs aimed magic items to avoid the effect) Eyestalks. The left and right eyestalks can cast hold monster and hold person respectively, once each per round, at will. The two eyestalks together can cast phantasmal force once per round, at will, if not used to cast hold spells.

monsters.name: Fish, giant, giant gar
monsters.description: GIANT GAR Giant gar live in deep rivers and lakes.

sections.Special Attacks: Swallow Whole. Giant gar can swallow prey whole on an attack roll 20, including creatures up to Medium size. A swallowed person a cumulative 5% chance per segment of drowning, but if they have bladed weapon they can try to cut their way out of the fish. To do 25% of the giant gar’s total hp must be inflicted. Any piercing attack against a giant gar has a 20% chance of causing equal damage swallowed creature. GIANT PIKE Giant pike are aggressive predators found in larger and deeper lakes. They often guard nixie lairs. Capsize Ships. Leviathans can overturn small vessels 90% of the time, oceangoing ships 50% of the time, and huge vessels 10% of the time. Swallow Whole. A successful “to hit” roll inflicts the damage shown and any creature attacked must save vs death or be swallowed whole (see “giant gar” for the effects of this).
sections.Surprise and Initiative: Due to their great speed and acuity of vision, giant pike will surprise their prey on a 1–4 on 1d6. LEVIATHANS Leviathans are huge fish that may originate from the deepest oceans or the Elemental Plane of Water.

monsters.name: Fly, giant, giant blow fly
monsters.description: of has Giant flies are more massive than the normal variety of a flying insects and thus are Aerial Agility: Level III, though so, they can hover. They do retain a normal fly’s ability to react quickly and thus they can jump away from an atto a tack in only 1 segment. This jumping defensive move is a backward springing leap which carries the giant fly 30ft away and does not count as a retreat for purposes of a free attack. Giant flies cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics. GIANT BLOW FLY Giant blow flies have a shiny metallic green or blue body covered with coarse black hair. Their large eyes are a dark orange colour. These flies will rarely attack living prey unless someone is covered with blood or has open wounds. They are also attracted to sweet food and drink; an abundance of these might garner the attention of this monster. Giant flies are more often encountered wherever there is an abundance of their preferred diet: carrion, rotting food, and malodorous refuse.

sections.Special Attacks: The bite of a giant blow fly has a 10% chance of infecting the victim with disease. GIANT HORSEFLY This giant insect is even larger than the giant blow fly and far more aggressive. The giant horsefly dines on fresh blood and it will land on any warm-blooded creature is encounters, attempting to draw blood from the target with its bite. Giant horseflies are flat tan and brown in colour, with shiny brown eyes. Suck Blood. After a successful bite, the horsefly continues to automatically inflict damage as it draws blood from the bite wound. This process can only be halted by killing the giant horsefly.
