monsters.name: Frog, giant
monsters.description: 3 HD: 50 +15/hp Giant frogs can be 2, 4, or 6ft in length. They are found anywhere their normal-size cousins are. A 2ft frog weighs 50 lbs and can jump 180ft, a 4ft frog weighs 150 lbs and can jump 140ft, and a 6ft frog weighs 250 lbs and can jump 100ft.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Giant frogs have natural camouflage and surprise on a roll of 1–4 on 1d6.
sections.Special Attacks: Tongue Pull. The frog can shoot its tongue up to three times its body length, and has +4 to hit with this attack. The tongue does no damage: it only sticks to the victim. Any creature hit with the tongue can attempt to free itself by striking the tongue. If the victim manages to strike the tongue, the frog will retract it and attack a different target next round. If the victim is not freed and weighs less than the frog, the frog will pull the victim into its mouth, inflicting maximum damage automatically each round thereafter. If the victim weighs more than the giant frog it will take 2 rounds to drag the victim into its mouth. If the victim is more than double the frog’s weight, the frog will not be able to move the victim (on the 3rd round the frog will release its tongue). Swallow Whole. If the frog scores a natural 20 on an attack, it has swallowed its prey (unless the target is a larger size than the frog). A giant frog can swallow whole anything elf-sized or smaller. If swallowed, there is a chance for the victim to cut their way out. They must have in hand a sharp edged weapon and score an 18 or better. Prey get three attempts to escape. Any hit to the giant frog, that has swallowed its victim, has a 33% chance of doing damage to the victim as well. Unarmed Combat. Giant frogs cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Fungi, violet
monsters.description: Violet fungi look like shriekers and in fact the two are often found growing together. The plants are usually 4ft to 7ft tall, and each plant has 1d4 branches growing out of it. At 4ft tall, the fungi will have 1ft branches. For every foot taller the fungi grows, the branches grow a foot longer.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Plant Immunities. This creature doesn’t need to eat, drink, sleep, or breathe as an animal would. Magic can’t put it to sleep. Gases can’t harm it, and it is immune to poison and disease. It does not rely upon sight, so it automatically detects invisible opponents.
sections.Special Attacks: Spores. When the fungi detects movement nearby it will wave its branches around, releasing its spores. Anyone within 4ft must save vs poison or their exposed flesh will begin to rot within 1 round. Anyone who fails their save will die in 1d4+4 rounds unless the rotting is stopped by a cure disease spell.

monsters.name: Gargoyle
monsters.description: Gargoyles are cruel creatures, 90% likely to attack any living creature they encounter. They resemble statues of winged humanoids, and are almost indistinguishable from carved stone until they move. They are usually encountered in ruins and underground caverns.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more. Unarmed Combat. Gargoyles can attack and be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/- 6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

monsters.name: Gelatinous cube
monsters.description: Gelatinous cubes are dungeon scavengers. They move slowly through corridors and rooms, absorbing carrion, fungi, algae and other nutrients from the surfaces they touch. Gelatinous cubes can only digest organic material, and they will sometimes sweep up inorganic substances (including metal items such as coins, glass or ceramic items such as potion bottles, etc.). These incidental items are sometimes kept in the body of the ‘cube for many days before being ejected. Such items form the creature’s treasure.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Being silent and virtually transparent, gelatinous cubes have a higher-than-usual chance to surprise (1–3 on 1d6).
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Ooze. This creature cannot be knocked prone, and is not affected by lack of light, invisible opponents, gases, or other circumstances that would not affect an ooze. Immunities. Gelatinous cubes are immune to electricity, fear, sleep, hold, paralysis, and polymorph. Reaction to Cold. Cold-based attacks slow a gelatinous cube (as the spell) but only inflict a maximum of 1d4 damage, unless they make a saving throw, in which case the cold-based attack will have no effect at all (including the slowing effect).
sections.Special Attacks: Paralysing Touch. The touch of a gelatinous cube causes paralysis for 3d6+2 rounds (a saving throw vs paralysation is permitted to avoid this effect). Unarmed Combat. It should go without saying that gelatinous cubes cannot and should not be overborne or grappled. They do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Ghast
monsters.description: These terrible undead creatures are more powerful versions of ghouls, and are indistinguishable from them save their terrible stench, released when engaged in melee. Ghasts, when acting as a pack, can travel the dream-realms and can also enter the lower planes. However, this takes too long for it to be a factor in combat situations. Certain entities of the higher hells use ghasts as slaves.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Turned as Undead. Ghasts are turned as type 6 Undead. Undeath. This creature is immune to all mind control (including charm) and hold spells. It cannot be affected by sleep, gases, poison, or disease. Immune to Protection from Evil. Ghasts are not affected by protection from evil spells (or effects, such as a paladin’s ability).
sections.Special Features: Stench. When ghasts are in melee combat, they release a stench of death so strong that anyone within 10ft must make a saving throw vs poison. Anyone affected by the stench begins retching, suffering -2 to all actions, including to-hit rolls and damage.
sections.Special Attacks: Paralysation. If a ghast hits with its claws or bite, the victim must make a saving throw vs. paralysation or be paralysed for 3d4 full turns. Unarmed Combat. Ghasts can attack and be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks although they seldom use this tactic. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

monsters.name: Ghost
monsters.description: Ghosts are the spiritual remains of extremely evil humans who have been denied the ordinarily inexorable movement of their souls to the outer planes of existence after discarding their mortal shell. This sundering of their metaphysical essence creates a foul thing, roaming dark and desolate places, existing in both the ethereal plane and the prime material, seeking to slake a thirst that can never be sated. This exigent need for living essences is what drives these spirits into contact with mortals. The ghost has different attributes when non-manifest (ethereal) and after it has manifested. A ghost’s first attack, before it manifests itself, is an attempt at a magic jar. Any creature within 180ft is threatened by the being’s magic jar ability, as per the spell. The ghost cannot be attacked while it is still unmanifested (unless the attacker is also ethereal). If the magic jar fails, then the ghost will manifest itself, taking on an ectoplasmic quality. Specially forged “pure” metals, especially silver, can cause half-damage to a ghost while it is manifested in this fashion, and magic weapons can affect it normally.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Turned as Undead. Ghosts are turned as type 11 Undead. Undeath. This creature is immune to all mind control (including charm) and hold spells. It cannot be affected by sleep, gases, poison, or disease. Ethereal Form. Until the ghost manifests itself physically, it is immune to all attacks, spell or no, unless the attacker has a method to become ethereal. Even if the spell caster is in this state, ghosts are still immune to many forms of spells, though no sage has recorded what those magics might be. Magical weapons used in an ethereal state against a ghost typically have to strike against AC 7 [13] or 8 [12]. Immune to Non-Silver Mundane Weapons. Once manifested, the ghost is still immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more, or is silver (which only inflicts half damage unless also magical).
sections.Special Features: Deadly to Look Upon. Merely beholding the awfulness of the ghost requires a saving throw vs magic (bonus described below). Failure causes the viewer to flee in panic (for 2d8 turns) and initiates a weaker form of the ghost’s wither attack—which ages the victim 3d6 years as the ghost feasts on the life of the victim. Clerics level 7 or greater can ignore this effect, as they have a better understanding of how to ward off such metaphysical forces, while other creatures with 9 or more hit dice or levels gain a +3 to their saves.
sections.Special Attacks: Magic Jar. A ghost’s first attack, before it manifests itself, is an attempt at a magic jar. Any creature within 180ft is threatened by the being’s magic jar ability, as per the spell. Wither. The manifest state allows the ghost to strike victims physically, with the full power of their withering attack—causing the victim to age 7d6 years per successful attack, no save possible. Victims who exceed their allotted lifespan are forever dead, with only a wish capable of reversing this end. Optional Rule: As an abstract way of handling aging, for every 10 years of aging, the victim is treated as having a -1 to all saving throws (until the aging is reversed). If the victim has been aged 60 years (120 years in the case of demi-humans), this indicates death from old age. Demi-humans generally have a longer lifespan than 120 years, but it’s easy to consider that ghostly aging is also quite traumatic. Unarmed Combat. Ghosts cannot be overborne or grappled, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Ghoul
monsters.description: Ghouls are undead creatures, possibly once human. Loping through the darkness with their vague canine cast and long, black, marrow-licking tongues, they haunt graves and ruins, seeking the flesh of the dead and the living. Though their minds are warped by the transformation, and their general intellect stunted, they still retain a terrible cunning, and they attack in fearless packs to good effect, bringing down the living to feast on their remains. Any person killed by ghouls will eventually rise as a ghoul unless the body is blessed. Such casualties can be raised from the dead normally, as well, as long as it is done before the ghoul transformation sets in. Protection from evil will keep these things at bay. Ghouls are also said to be able travel the lands of dreams, using them as conduit to enter the waking world of men at various graveyards, and escaping without a trace. Marine ghouls are called “lacedons” and are sometimes found on ghost ships or dwelling in wrecks on the sea bed.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Turned as Undead. Ghouls are turned as type 3 Undead. Undeath. This creature is immune to all mind control (including charm) and hold spells. It cannot be affected by sleep, gases, poison, or disease.
sections.Special Attacks: Paralysation. Any human or demi-human (except elves) hit by a ghoul must make a saving throw vs. paralysis or be paralysed for 3d4 turns. Unarmed Combat. Ghouls can attack and be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks although they seldom use this tactic. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/ DEF +0/+0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.
sections.Language: Ghouls, unlike most undead, have their own language which they share with ghasts. Their voices are weird and eldritch, sometimes described as “meeping” and “glibbering”. GIANTS Far from being mere brutes, giants’ cunning makes up for their sometimes low intelligence. Giants can sometimes be persuaded, so long it is within their interests, to cooperate with other beings of like alignment. Despite the diversity of giant types, these monsters share some common characteristics. Giants are able to lift and throw large rocks like a catapult, even at close range, with their immense strength of 19–25. Immature giants function at a percentage of that of adults. Giants’ great love of gold nearly matches their strength, and they commonly carry 1,000–6,000 coins, usually gold, with them when away from their cave dens. As if in defence of this treasure, they also commonly carry one or two rocks to use as convenient weapons. Giants speak one language unique to their type, as well as their alignment language.

monsters.name: Giant, cloud
monsters.description: Cloud giants usually live in giant castles at high elevations. When not high up in the mountains, their castles are on clouds given substance by magic. The majority (90%) of these giants have average intelligence; the remainder are very intelligent and most often live in castles in the sky. Cloud giants often dress in flowing clothing and fancy jewellery. They have bronze to white hair, with skin in tones of blue ranging from nearly white to cold, light blue. When multiple giants are found in a castle, there is a 75% chance that it is a family consisting of two adults, with any remaining giants being children (treat as ogres). The other 25% of the time, all of the giants are adults. Evil cloud giants have a 50% chance to be keeping 1d3 human slaves, and also have a 50% chance to own 1d4 prehistoric lions.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Sense of Smell. Cloud giants are rarely (1 on 1d6) surprised due to their impressive olfactory abilities.
sections.Special Features: Levitation. The “very intelligent” class of cloud giants have the ability to levitate the equivalent of 20,000 gp, plus their body weight, twice a day.
sections.Special Attacks: Ranged Attack (Thrown Rock). All cloud giants can throw rocks to inflict 2d12 blunt damage from 10 to 240ft distance from a target, and can catch thrown rocks 60% of the time. Unarmed Combat. Cloud giants cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use this tactic.

monsters.name: Giant, fire
monsters.description: Fire giants’ hair is the red and orange colour of flames, and their skin is soot black. Their teeth are flame orange, and their eyes red. The commonly wear armour on their broad, 6ft wide shoulders. This armour is sometimes made from the skin of dragons. Like cloud giants, fire giants often live in castles (50%), but are just as likely to frequent caves. It is not uncommon for many adult fire giants to live together. When more than six fire giants are encountered, the additional individuals will be immature and will only have a percentage of adult capabilities (as hill giants or ogres). Fire giants sometimes share their lairs with 1d4 hell hounds (25% chance).

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Fire. As their name suggests, all fire giants are unharmed by fire. This extends to the flame breath produced by red dragons.
sections.Special Attacks: Like most giants, fire giants delight in throwing rocks at enemies. They can hit a target from a distance of 10ft to 200ft (2d10 hit points of blunt damage), and can similarly catch (50% chance) thrown rocks. Unarmed Combat. Fire giants cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. They will occasionally make an overbearing attack. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 16+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +4/na. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF na/na.

monsters.name: Giant, frost
monsters.description: Frost giants have the overall appearance of giant, muscled barbarians. They have light yellow or blue eyes, with white hair that can likewise be tinged with yellow or blue. These giants get their name from their love of the cold. They often live within frosty caverns, but also have a propensity to take up residence in castles, as do some of their other giant kin. Winter wolves often share residence with frost giants (50% chance, 1d12 in number). When encountering more than 4 frost giants, the first six giants are adults, and additional individuals will be immature (treat as hill giants or ogres).

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Cold. Frost giants are completely immune to ill effects from cold, including the bone–chilling breath of white dragons.
sections.Special Attacks: Ranged Attack (Thrown Rocks). Frost giants can cause 2d10 hit points in damage by throwing large rocks from between 10ft to 200ft. Likewise, they can catch rocks tossed at them with a 40% probability. Unarmed Combat. Frost giants cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use such tactics.

monsters.name: Giant, hill
monsters.description: In many ways hill giants resemble large ogres, and they will often wield some type of bludgeoning weapon. They dress in animal skins and live in mostly inhospitable locations. Half of the time hill giants have other animals or beings guarding their homes. When guards are present, there is a 30% probability they are 1 to 3 giant lizards, 20% probability they are 2d4 ogres, and 50% probability they are 2d4 dire wolves. When encountering more than 4 hill giants, the first seven are adults and additional individuals are young (treat as ogres).

sections.Special Attacks: Ranged Attack (Thrown Rocks). Hill giants can cause 2d8 hit points in damage by throwing large rocks from between 10ft to 200ft. Likewise, they can catch rocks tossed at them with a 30% probability. Unarmed Combat. Hill giants cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. They will occasionally make an overbearing attack. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +4/na. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF na/na.

monsters.name: Giant, stone
monsters.description: Stone giants are partially named for their stone-like complexions and iron coloured eyes. Their hair is also dark-stone coloured, sometimes with hints of blue. Whereas hill giants often use wooden clubs, stone giants prefer stone and wear skins the colour of stone. These giants live in mountainous locations exclusively, in caverns or otherwise in the earth. They are most active at night. Three-quarters of the time stone giants have 1d4 cave bears guarding their homes. When encountering more than 4 stone giants, the first six adults. Additional giants are young (treat as hill giants or ogres). Stone giants sometimes share their lairs with cave bears (50% chance of 1d4).

sections.Special Attacks: Ranged Attack (Thrown Rocks). Stone giants can cause 3d10 hit points in damage by throwing large rocks from between 10 to 300ft. Likewise, they can catch rocks tossed at them with a 90% probability. Unarmed Combat. Stone giants cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use such tactics.

monsters.name: Giant, storm
monsters.description: There are two typical appearances of storm giants, related to their preference for environment. Those who choose to live underwater are often of green hair, eyes and skin, while those who reside on land have purple skin, eyes either purple or cloudy grey, and blue–tinted black hair. Storm giants are the most formidable of giants in many campaigns. They live in remote locations; about 60% of the time they live on clouds like their cloud giant cousins, and 30% of the time in the mountains like their stone giant relatives. Somewhat more rarely (10% of the time) storm giants choose to live underwater. In all cases, they live in immense, luxurious castles. Like other giants, storm giants have a fondness for pets and if living above water will have 1d4 griffons 30% of the time and 1 or 2 rocs 70% of the time. However, storm giants who have their castle abodes under water will instead have 2d4 sea lions.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Electricity. Storm giants are immune to all damage by electricity, including the fearsome electrical bolt breathed by the dreaded blue dragon.
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. 1/day: lightning bolt (8d8 damage), call lightning (10 to 15d6 damage, 3 bolts), control winds, predict weather, and weather summoning. 2/day: levitate their own weight plus an additional weight equal to 30,000 gold pieces two times per day. Underwater Abilities. Storm giants can breathe and otherwise function underwater unimpeded. Unarmed Combat. Storm giants cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use such tactics. GNOLL-KIN

monsters.name: Flind
monsters.description: Flinds are close relatives of, and to a degree resemble, gnolls. Flinds stand 6.5ft tall, with powerful limbs and a leonine head. Both flinds and gnolls regard flinds as a majestic, superior form of gnoll. Groups of gnolls are often led by one or more flinds, and the gnolls will obey any order given by a flind without question. A gnoll defending its flind leader will not check for morale unless the flind is killed. If 20 or more flinds are encountered, there will be a leader type with 3+3 hit dice, a strength of 18 (+1 “to hit” and +2 damage). Leader type flinds always wield a disarming weapon in combat. Regarding Player Character Use of Flindish Disarming Bars: The wielder must be medium-sized or larger, and possess minimum ability scores of 13 in both strength and dexterity. The disarm function can only be used by PCs who select the flindbar as a weapon of proficiency.

sections.Special Attacks: Strength. Flinds attack with a +1 to-hit bonus due to strength. Disarm. There is a 25% chance that any particular flind wields a disarming weapon, a pair of iron bars linked by a short piece of chain. A flind wielding one of these weapons can make two attacks per round for 1d4 hp bludgeoning damage. For every hit, the victim must save vs aimed magic items or be disarmed. Unarmed Combat. Flinds can attack and be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks although they seldom use this tactic. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 12+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-4. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/ DEF +2/-2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2.
sections.Language: Flinds share a common language with gnolls and can also speak bugbear, hobgoblin, ogrish, and orcish. They are generally on friendly terms with these humanoid ancestries and will work with them as need arises. For unknown reasons, flinds do not like, and will not cooperate with, trolls.

monsters.name: Gnoll
monsters.loot: Individual 3, 4 each; in lair Hoard 4, Cache 3 (x5), and Cache 5
monsters.description: Gnolls resemble tall humans, but they have the head of a hyena and are covered in yellowish-grey hair. They live and travel in small, roving bands. There are rumours of a gnoll overlord, though if one exists its power and reach are limited. In general, these creatures are scavengers, raiders, and thieves, their behaviour analogous to hyena packs. Raiding parties of gnolls are led by a leader with 16 hp, fighting as a 3 HD monster. Gnoll bands (when encountered in a lair) are led by a chieftain (AC 3 [17], 22 hp, attacking as a 4 HD monster, and inflicting 2d4+2 damage), and 2d6 guards (AC 4 [16], 20 hp, attacking as a 3 HD monster, inflicting 2d4+1 damage). Gnolls have been known to ally with orcs, hobgoblins, bugbears, and even trolls. Unarmed Combat. Gnolls can attack and be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks although they seldom use this tactic. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 12+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-2. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/ DEF +2/-2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2.

sections.Language: Gnolls speak troll, their own barked tongue which they share with flinds, the chaotic evil alignment tongue, and occasionally orcish and hobgoblin.

monsters.name: Gnome
monsters.loot: Individual 4 (x3) each; in lair Hoard 3, Cache 3 (x20)
monsters.description: Gnomes live underground in hills that they have burrowed into, seeking gems and precious metals. They are divided into clans which are rather competitive with each other, but are never outright hostile. They are a distant relative to dwarfs. For every 40 gnomes encountered there usually is a fighter of 2nd level or higher levels acting as leader. When the groups are of 200 or more there are clerics as well, usually 4th level or higher. Most of the time the gnomes will have badgers, or other burrowing animals, that they have trained to act as sentries. Typically when gnomes are encountered they will be wearing studded leather armour or ring armour and a shield. Gnomes are usually armed with a club and spear, sometimes with a short sword and spear.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Saving Throw. Due to their natural resilience to both magic and poison, gnomes save against these effects at four levels higher than they actually are. Nimbleness. When gnomes battle gnolls, bugbears, ogres, trolls, or giants these creatures receive a -4 to their attack rolls due to the gnomes’ smaller size and nimbleness.
sections.Special Features: Gnomes are excellent miners, possessing the abilities to detect whether a passage slopes upward or downward or if a corridor, walls, floors or ceiling is safe or not. They can even estimate depth and direction underground.
sections.Special Attacks: Kobolds and Goblins. When gnomes fight kobolds and goblins they gain an additional +1 to hit. Unarmed Combat. Gnomes can attack and be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. For a gnome wearing chain mail - if not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 12+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +4/+0. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2.
sections.Language: In addition to their own language, gnomes can also speak kobold, goblin, halfling, dwarfish, and can also speak a language commonly known to all burrowing animals.

monsters.name: Goblin
monsters.description: Goblins are small evil creatures with a yellow-to-red or a greenish-coloured skin tone. They typically wear leather armour, and have an average lifespan of 50 years. They are subterranean, and are only found on the surface when raiding or in the very darkest of forests. Goblins have a deep hatred of gnomes and dwarfs and will attack them on sight. Goblins are organised into war-bands, with the strongest ruling the war-band. The bands all owe fealty to the goblin king. A goblin raiding party will be led by a captain and 4 sergeants, each with 7 hp and who will fight as orcs (1 HD monsters). A goblin war party will be led by a sub-chief and personal guards (2d4). They will fight as hobgoblins (each with 8 hp, AC 5 [15], and doing 1d8 damage). There is a 1 in 4 chance that any war party will be mounted on worgs. A goblin lair will be led by a chief and personal guards (2d4). They will fight as gnolls (each with 12 hp, AC 4 [15], doing 2d4 damage). Worgs are often used as guards of goblin lairs, and sometimes a small band of bugbears will be found there as well. Goblins are good cavers and have a chance (25%) to note new or unusual construction.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Vulnerability to Light. Goblins are subterranean creatures that detest direct sunlight, and will fight at -1 if exposed to it.

monsters.name: Golem, clay golem
monsters.description: CLAY GOLEM A clay golem is a construct created through the following procedure: a lawful good cleric of at least 17th level (or a lower level cleric of same alignment using a magical tome written for such a process) creates a man–shaped figure out of clay and then undertakes an uninterrupted ritual involving material components worth no less than 20,000 gp, vestments and ritual items worth another 30,000 gp and the spells resurrection, animate object, commune, prayer and bless. Unarmed Combat. Goblins can attack and be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks although they seldom use this tactic. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 10+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-2. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/ DEF -2/+2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2.

sections.Language: Goblins speak kobold, orcish, hobgoblin, lawful evil, and their own language. GOLEM A golem is a magically created monster. Of the four basic types, three are created with earthen materials, while the flesh golem is created from human body parts. The creation process requires powerful spells, rare components, and eldritch forces. The golems listed below are typically humanoid in shape. A golem has hit dice equal to its hit points divided by 4.5 rounded up; thus, for example, a stone golem has 14 hit dice (60 hp/4.5). Magical creatures may strike a golem with effect if the creature’s hit dice equal or exceed that of the golem. Unarmed Combat. Golems cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use such tactics.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Non-Blunt and Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing and slashing damage from all weapons (magical or not), and from blunt damage from non-magical weapons. Unaffected by Most Spells. Clay golems are not affected by spells other than move earth (6d6 damage), disintegrate (1d12 damage and slows the golem permanently as per the spell) and earthquake (5d10 damage). Immune to Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more. Immune to Most Spells. Cold- and fire-based spells do not damage the golem, but slow it to 50% speed for 2d6 combat rounds. Electrical attacks heal damage the golem has sustained, at a rate of 1 hit point restored per die of damage that would have been inflicted (example: an 8 hit dice lightning bolt will restore 8 hit points of damage). Other spells have no effect at all. Immune to Mundane, +1, and +2 Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +3 or more. Immune to Most Spells. Only electrical magical attacks can affect it; such spells will slow the golem to one-half speed for 3 combat rounds. Fire attacks repair damage to the golem at a rate of one hit point per die of spell damage (example: a 6 hit die fireball repairs 6 hp of damage). Other spells have no effect at all. Immune to Mundane and +1 Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +2 or more. Immune to Most Spells. A stone golem is invulnerable to most magic. The only exceptions are rock to mud (halves the golem’s attack and movement speed for 2d6 rounds), stone to flesh (makes the golem susceptible to normal weapons for one round), and mud to rock (acts as a heal spell on the monster).
sections.Special Features: Loss of Control. A clay golem is under the direct command of its creator. It stands a 1% cumulative chance of possession by a spirit of chaotic evil alignment for each round the golem is in combat. The creator can never regain control if the golem is possessed. Once possessed, the golem will kill any nearby living thing starting with the closest creature and will haste itself if it has not already done so. Healing-Resistant Damage. Damage inflicted by a clay golem can only be healed by a cleric of 17th level or greater, although it will heal naturally at the normal rate. Loss of Control. For each melee round spent in combat, the flesh golem stands a 1% cumulative chance of going berserk and attacking all targets in sight. The golem’s creator can attempt to reassert control at a chance of 10% per round (non-cumulative). IRON GOLEM An iron golem is created through use of a magical tome or by an 18th level or higher magic-user using the following spells: cloud kill, wish, geas, and polymorph object. Creation time is three months and material cost is 1,000 gp per hit point of the golem. The magic-user can give the construct simple commands, and it can be ordered (if serving as a guard) to wait until a specific event takes place before undertaking a series of commands. Slow. A stone golem can cast a slow spell every other melee round on all opponents within 10ft of its front side.
sections.Special Attacks: The clay golem attacks as an 11 hit dice monster. Haste. Once per day, provided it has been in combat for one or more rounds, a clay golem can act as if hasted (duration: 3 combat rounds). This allows the golem to move and attack at twice normal speed. A golem that loses control will immediately haste itself if possible. FLESH GOLEM Flesh golems are constructs built from human body parts … basically, Frankenstein’s monster. A flesh golem follows simple commands by its creator, and can be ordered (if serving as a guard) to wait until a specific event takes place before undertaking a series of commands. A flesh golem is extremely strong and can break down doors and other wooden structures. A flesh golem is created with a magical tome written for such a process or by a magic-user (of at least 14th level) using the following spells: wish, polymorph object, geas, strength, and protection from normal missiles. One thousand gold pieces per hit point of the golem must be spent on material components, and the entire creation process takes one month. Breath Weapon. In addition to its normal attacks, once every 7 combat rounds an iron golem may breathe poison gas directly before it in a cloud of 10 cubicft. Anyone in the cloud must make a saving throw vs. poison or die. STONE GOLEM A stone golem is created through use of a magical text or by a 16th or higher level magic-user using the following spells: geas, slow, wish and polymorph object. Creation time is two months and cost is 1,000 gp per hit point of the golem. The magic-user can give the construct simple commands, and it can be ordered (if serving as a guard) to wait until a specific event takes place before undertaking a series of commands.

STONE GOLEM A stone golem is created through use of a magical text or by a 16th or higher level magic-user using the following spells: geas, slow, wish and polymorph object. Creation time is two months and cost is 1,000 gp per hit point of the golem. The magic-user can give the construct simple commands, and it can be ordered (if serving as a guard) to wait until a specific event takes place before undertaking a series of commands.

monsters.name: Gorgon
monsters.description: Gorgons are magical creatures resembling giant bulls, but with thick metal scales instead of hide.

sections.Special Attacks: Petrifying Breath (3/day). Gorgons can breathe a cloud of petrifying gas in a cone 60ft long and 10ft in radius at the base up to 3 times per day. Anyone in the cloud must make a saving throw vs. petrifaction or be turned to stone. Unarmed Combat. Gorgons cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use such tactics.

monsters.name: Grey ooze
monsters.description: Grey ooze is indistinguishable from wet stone until it attacks. It will form tentacles that lash out at any who pass. Grey ooze also takes full damage from normal weapons, but if the weapon is made of metal it too will begin to dissolve. As it matures grey ooze gets larger. Specimens over 20 HP can be as large as 36 square feet. While they cover a huge area, they are never more than a few inches deep. At larger sizes they begin to form a kind of consciousness.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Ooze Senses. This creature cannot be knocked prone, and is not affected by lack of light, invisible opponents, gases, or other circumstances that would not affect an ooze. Immunities. Grey ooze is not affected by fire or cold damage.
sections.Special Features: Corrosive Properties. Any metal weapon that hits a grey ooze must make a saving throw (target number: 7) or be destroyed by the ooze’s acidic properties. Magical weapons have a bonus to the saving throw of one higher than the weapon’s to-hit bonus (see PG Section 6.4, Item Saving Throws).
sections.Special Attacks: Corrosive Pseudopods. Grey ooze is corrosive. If the ooze hits an opponent wearing metal armour, the armour will come apart and become useless unless it makes a saving throw vs. acid (target number: 7). The acid will eat through chain mail in 1 round, and requires 2 rounds to eat through plate. See Player Guide Section 1.6.4, Item Saving Throws. The acid does not damage wood, leather, or stone. Unarmed Combat. Grey oozes cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use such tactics.

monsters.name: Griffon
monsters.description: Griffons build nests on cliff faces and rocky outcrops. Where possible they even have been known to build nests inside shallow caves. Horses are their favourite meal and being the fearsome hunters they are, griffons will usually attack their prey on sight. Hatchlings are particularly valuable as they can be trained as mounts. This takes time, effort, and money. The training takes years and must begin early in a griffon’s life. Once the griffon reaches maturity there is no chance of training it. When ridden by a creature weighing more than 100 lbs, a griffon’s aerial agility decreases to III. Unarmed Combat. Griffons cannot be attacked or targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks although they may occasionally overbear as the end of an aerial attack. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/ DEF +10/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +3/na. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF na/na.

monsters.name: Grimlock
monsters.description: Grimlocks are a fierce species of humanoid that dwells in the dark and hidden places of the earth, periodically issuing forth to the surface in search of prey, preferably human. Whilst somewhat resembling men in shape, they have a thick, almost scaly, hide that is a dusky grey in colour, a head of wild and matted black hair, a mouthful of vicious pointed teeth and two white featureless orbs for eyes. (The original inspiration for this monster was probably the morlocks). Though it is unknown whether grimlocks speak a language, it is certain that they are entirely blind. They instead rely on their other senses, which are highly developed and allow them to perceive the environment around them within a 20ft radius with astounding accuracy. Grimlocks show very little grasp of tactics or strategy, preferring to attack directly and all at once. However, they do seem to prefer to fight under cover of darkness, which often yields to them a distinct advantage. Although they are capable of inflicting 1d6 damage with their filthy claws, most prefer to use axes or swords. For every 30 grimlocks encountered there will be one with 3 HD and AC 4 [16]; for every 40 grimlocks encountered there will be one with 4 HD and AC 3 [17]. These act as leaders, being generally more ferocious than their fellows and even capable of developing and employing elementary stratagems. For every one of these leaders present, their morale is increased by 5%. It is rare for them to be found in conjunction with any other monsters.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Grimlocks surprise on a die roll of 1-3 on a d6 if the encounter is underground.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Native Blindness. Grimlocks are immune to the effects of bright light or other visual stimuli that might otherwise adversely affect them, including magical effects, such as invisibility, darkness and any visual illusions. However, grimlocks are also known to be particularly vulnerable to effects that obscure their other senses, such as overpowering scents or overloud noises that have a significant duration. When exposed to such hindrances, their perception is reduced to a 10ft radius and they suffer a -2 penalty to hit. Improved Saving Throw. Regardless of hit dice, grimlocks always make saving throws as 6th level fighters. Unarmed Combat. Grimlocks can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.

monsters.name: Halfling
monsters.description: Halflings as an ancestry value hard work and simple living. Their settlements are as likely to contain small cottages as they are to have underground dwellings. They tend to keep to themselves. When encountered in groups there will likely be a leader, usually a 2nd level fighter, for every 30 individuals. In groups containing over 90 individuals there will likely be a 3rd level fighter as well. In groups containing more than 150 halflings there will usually be a 4th level fighter in addition to the 3rd and 2nd level fighters. There is a 10% chance per level that higher level halflings may have magic armour and/or weapons. If the halflings are encountered in their homes (lair) they will have 1d4 dogs acting as guards. Their lifespan averages about 150 years.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Halflings are very quiet and unobtrusive, surprising enemies on a roll of 1–4 on a d6. Immunities and Resistances Magic and Poison Save. Halfling NPCs make saving throws with a +4 against magic and poison.
sections.Special Attacks: Ranged Attack Bonus. Halflings are +3 “to hit” with bow or sling, and almost all halflings are equipped with some sort of missile weapon. Unarmed Combat. Halflings can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with an 8+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-4. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2.
sections.Language: Halflings speak their own language and will also be able to speak common, gnome, goblin, and orc.

monsters.name: Harpy
monsters.description: These creatures are part vulture (wings and lower body) and part woman (head and torso). Harpies use their charm ability to bind prey, after which the harpies will torture, kill, and consume the victims. In combat a harpy attacks with her clawed feet and, usually, some kind of club as a melee weapon.

sections.Special Features: Singing. Anyone hearing the song of a harpy must make a saving throw vs spells or move toward the source of the song.
sections.Special Attacks: Charm. If the harpy hits with either of its claw attacks, the victim must make a saving throw vs. spells or be charmed (as per the magic-user spell). Unarmed Combat. Harpies cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use such tactics.
sections.Language: Most harpies speak only their own language and the alignment tongue of chaotic evil.

monsters.name: Hell hound
monsters.description: 7 HD: 225 +8/hp Hell hounds are not native to the material plane; they are brought here by others to serve as guard dogs. These fiendish dogs are dark reddish in colour with glowing red eyes and black mouths.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Stealthy Surprise. Because hell hounds can move so quietly, they surprise on a roll of 1–4 on 1d6. Keen Senses. Hell hounds can only be surprised on a roll of 1 due to their own sharp senses.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Eyes of the Underworld. The vision of Hell Hounds is unnaturally sharp: 50% of the time they can spot hidden or invisible creatures.
sections.Special Attacks: Breathe Fire. Hell hounds breath fire up to a 10ft range. Anyone caught in the area (roughly a line 10ft long and 5-6ft wide) must make a saving throw vs. breath weapons or take fire damage equal to the hound’s hit dice. If the saving throw succeeds, the victim takes only half damage. Example: a 6 hit dice hell hound breathes fire for 6hp damage, unless the opponent saves vs breath weapons and thus takes only 3 hit points. The hell hound can attack and breathe fire in the same round. Unarmed Combat. Hell hounds cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, but they may overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +3/na. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF na/na.

monsters.name: Hippogriff
monsters.description: Hippogriffs have the body of a horse, but the head, wings, and foreclaws of an eagle. They are only found in remote locations, far from civilisation, nesting on rocky outcrops. Hippogriffs do not mix well other winged beasts, and will try to eat pegasi. If encountered near its nest, a hippogriff will fight ferociously to defend itself and its young. Eggs and hatchlings bring a high price from those wishing to train them as mounts. When ridden by a creature weighing more than 100 lbs, a hippogriff’s aerial agility rating decreases to III. Unarmed Combat. Hippogriffs cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, but they may overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +4/na. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF na/na.

monsters.name: Hobgoblin
monsters.loot: Individual 1 and 4 each; in lair, Hoard 4 and Cache 3 (x5)
monsters.description: Hobgoblins are bigger cousins of goblins, and form their own society. In general, they have red or orange skin, and are hairier than normal goblins. Their organisation is usually into warbands, which may fight each other over territory if they are not restrained by strong leadership. Although hobgoblins are not affected by sunlight as goblins are, they are still essentially a subterranean species. They typically lair underground, and will sometimes (50%) keep carnivorous apes as guards. Hobgoblin raiding parties are led by a sergeant and 2 assistants, each with 9 hp. Hobgoblin war parties are led by a captain (AC 3 [17], 16 hp, fights as a 3 HD monster, doing 1d8+2 damage). In their lair, hobgoblins are led by a chief (AC 2 [18], 22 hp, fights as a 4 HD monster, doing 1d10+1 damage) and 5d4 personal guards (AC 3 [17], 16 hp, fights as a 3 HD monster, doing 1d8+2 damage). Hobgoblins hate elves, and will attack them on sight.

sections.Special Features: Hobgoblins are very skilled miners and cavers, and can detect new construction, sloping passages and shifting walls with a 40% chance.
sections.Special Attacks: Ranged Attack: One in five hobgoblins will carry a bow or other ranged weapon as well as a sword or spear. Unarmed Combat. Hobgoblins can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 12+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-2. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.
sections.Language: Hobgoblins speak goblin, orcish, their own brutish tongue and the very limited language of carnivorous apes. Some can speak common as well.

monsters.name: Homunculus
monsters.description: A homunculus is a small construct that is vaguely humanoid in form, stands about 18 inches tall, and has bat-like wings with a 24-in wingspan. homunculi have greenish reptilian skin, a batlike head and ears, and a mouth full of needle-sharp teeth. Its alignment is the same as its creator. The homunculus is completely under control of its creator, who need not concentrate on control to maintain it. This means the homunculus can be given a specific goal, which it will then plan to achieve, carrying out its orders without further attention from its creator. Homunculi are created in a process involving both the spell caster and the services of an alchemist. The alchemist will require 1d4×500 (500–2,000) gold pieces, a pint of the magic-user’s blood, and 1d4 weeks to prepare the base mixture of fluids which will form the creature. Within 24 hours of the alchemist completing the mixture process the magic-user must cast the following spells upon the fluid, in order: mending, mirror image, and wizard eye. The spells must be cast by the person who gave the blood for the basic mixture (though scrolls may be used). Failure to cast the spells within 24 hours or casting the required spells out of order ruins that mixture and the whole process and all costs must be repeated. Upon completion of the wizard eye spell, the fluid coalesces into a ready-to-use homunculus. Homunculi make excellent messengers, scouts, or spies. Since they are constructs and not natural creatures, they are never encountered in the wild.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Per Creator. A homunculus is a reflection of its magic-user creator, and therefore rolls saves at whatever level its owner makes their saving throws. Magical defences in effect upon the owner, resist fire or bless for example, also protect the homunculus.
sections.Special Features: Climber. This creature can move on walls and ceilings as if they were floors. Connection to Creator. Killing a homunculus deals an immediate 2d10 points of damage to its master. If the owner of the homunculus dies, the homunculus immediately disappears in a puff of smoke.
sections.Special Attacks: Soporific Bite. The bite of a homunculus is venomous and causes a comatose state for 1d6×5 (5–30) minutes unless the victim saves vs magic to negate. Unarmed Combat. Homunculi can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, although they do not use these tactics. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF -4/+4. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -3/+3.
sections.Language: A homunculus cannot speak, but knows what its creator knows, and can communicate what it sees and hears to its creator via a limited form of telepathy up to 500ft away. A homunculus will never willingly exceed the maximum communication range.

monsters.name: Horse, draft
monsters.description: One of the most common domesticated animals, horses are almost ubiquitous in most human societies. They are insufficiently sure-footed to take into most dungeon environments (this requires a mule). “Heavy”, “Medium” and “Light” refer to warhorses. Only about 10% of horses can be trained as warhorses, even by an expert, and warhorse training requires very specialised knowledge on the part of the trainer. Unarmed Combat. Horses cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use such tactics. A warhorse might be trained to overbear.

monsters.name: Hippocampus
monsters.description: The hippocampus (plural “hippocampi”) is a mer-horse with the forequarters of a horse and a fish-like tail instead of rear legs. They are used as steeds by some underwater species, most notably the tritons. Hippocampi are entirely aquatic, and cannot venture out of the water.

monsters.name: Hippopotamus
monsters.description: Hippopotami, or “hippos”, are large semi-aquatic mammals that spend most of their time in the water. They are herbivores but they are quite aggressive in defending their territory and their great size makes them dangerous opponents. This is compounded by the fact that, in spite of the bulky appearance, they can run faster than a human on dry land. Hippos can’t float, though they can propel themselves to the surface of the water for a breath of air, and they can stay submerged for 15 minutes at a time. A herd will have one bull for every four hippos present. In combat, a bull bites for 3d6 damage and cows bite for 2d6. A boat passing over a hippo has a 50% of having the animal surface under the craft, tipping it over. Unarmed Combat. Hippopotami cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use such tactics. HUMANS Normal humans (non-adventuring types) will usually have 1d6 hit points. In any encounter with groups of humans, there will always be higher level characters as leaders (the number will be given under each entry). It’s worth noting that these entries are also groups that aren’t unique to humankind. A caravan of dwarf merchants or elven mounted nomads are absolutely possible, and any caravan might be accompanied by a dwarf or elf. You, as the GM, can decide to modify any randomly occurring results on the encounter tables to reflect the campaign. All higher level clerics and fighters will be mounted on medium warhorses. For each level a leader type has, there is a 5% chance of possessing a magic item in each of the categories below. For each “Y” in the following table, roll for an item of that type. If the result is undesirable, one re-roll is allowed.

monsters.name: Bandit (brigand), footman
monsters.description: Base Bandits are found in almost any locale, for wherever there is a civilisation there will be those who prey upon the weak. There will always be higher level fighters found with large groups of bandits. Consult the chart below to determine the exact number and level. Bandits are generally of neutral alignment, and brigands are generally chaotic evil. The base number of bandits in a lair is 20d10. Half of these will be footmen, 20% will be archers, 20% will be light cavalry, and 10% will be medium cavalry, as shown in the stats. FIGHTER MAGIC-USER CLERIC THIEF Armour Y N Y Y Shield Y N Y N Sword Y N N Y Misc. Weapon Y N Y* Y Potion Y N Y Y Scroll N Y Y N Ring N Y N Y Wand/Staff/ N Y N* N Rod Misc. Magic N Y Y Y *If no weapon (or an edged weapon is rolled), roll again on Wand/ Staff/Rod (if not usable by a cleric then there is none present). Leaders are in addition to the base number: • For every 20 bandits: 1 additional 3rd level fighter • For every 30 bandits: 1 additional 4th level fighter • For every 40 bandits: 1 additional 5th level fighter • For every 50 bandits: 1 additional 6th level fighter Commander. Bandits will always be led by a high level fighter (8th to 10th level), 6 guards (2nd level), and a lieutenant (7th level). These members are in addition to those described above. The level of the commander is determined as follows: • Under 100 bandits: 8th level fighter • 100 to 150 bandits: 9th level fighter • Over 150 bandits: 10th level fighter Other Leaders • There is a 25% chance per 50 bandits of a magic-user being present with the group. If there is a magic-user present they will be 7th to 10th level (determined by 1d4 roll). • There is a 15% chance per 50 bandits of a cleric being present with the group, if a cleric is present they will be 5th or 6th level and they will be accompanied by an assistant of 3rd or 4th level. Brigand: Brigands are a chaotic evil lot; otherwise they conform to the rules for bandits above. However they fight more fiercely in battle, and have higher morale (the number in parentheses is for brigands). Unarmed Combat. Bandits can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with an 8+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.

monsters.name: Berserker
monsters.description: Berserkers are roaming bands of fighters. They are always unarmoured, as they see it as a sign of weakness (but have an improved armour class). There will always be higher level fighters found with large groups of berserkers. Consult the chart below to determine the exact number and level. • For every 10 berserkers: 1 additional 1st level fighter • For every 20 berserkers: 1 additional 2nd level fighter • For every 30 berserkers: 1 additional 3rd level fighter • For every 40 berserkers: 1 additional 4th level fighter • For every 50 berserkers: 1 additional 5th level fighter Berserkers will always be led by a war chief of 9th or 10th level and a sub-chief of 6th or 7th level, as follows. • If less than 60: 9th level chief & 6th level sub-chief • If more than 60: 10th level chief & 7th level sub-chief Other Leaders: There is a 50% chance per every 10 berserkers, that a cleric will be present. The cleric will be of 7th level and will have 1d4 assistant clerics of 3rd or 4th level.

sections.Special Attacks: Frenzy. Berserkers fight with a fierce battle-lust, and as a result they may either strike twice in a round or make one attack at +2. Unarmed Combat. Berserkers can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with an 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8 (with additional +2 on attack). Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.

monsters.name: Buccaneer (pirate)
monsters.description: One out of every 3 buccaneers (or pirates) is armed with a light crossbow as well as an axe or sword. Buccaneers are found on all large bodies of water, their lair is most always the ship they use for raiding. They are always led by high level fighters as follows: • For every 50 buccaneers: 1 additional 3rd level fighter • For every 100 buccaneers: 1 additional 5th level fighter The overall captain will be a fighter of 8th to 10th level as follows: • If there are less than 200 buccaneers: 8th level fighter with a lieutenant of 6th level • If there are 200 buccaneers or more: 10th level fighter with a lieutenant of 7th level. The captain will also have 4 mates (4th level fighters) in addition to a lieutenant. There is a 15% chance of a cleric being present per every 50 buccaneers. The cleric will be between 12th and 15th level (1d4+11). There is a 10% chance of a magic-user being present for every 50 buccaneers; the magic-user will be between 6th and 8th level (1d3+5). Pirate: Pirates are chaotic evil, but otherwise conform to buccaneers above.

monsters.name: Caveman
monsters.description: Cavemen are humans living beyond the reach of normal civilisation, with stone-age technology. Hunting parties of cavemen (10 or more) are led by a 3rd level fighter. In their lair, in addition to the number of cavemen determined there will be a chief (5th level fighter) and 1d4 guards (4th level fighters). There is always a 10% chance (per every 10 cavemen) that a 3rd level cleric will be present. Cavemen typically dwell in caves and cavern systems. Their treasure will consist of ivory tusks, gold nuggets, or uncut gems (5% chance per 10 cavemen present). If one is present, it will be the only treasure there. The value of each is 1,000 gp per ivory tusk (2d6 tusks), 5 gp gold nuggets (2d4×10), and 10 gp gems (1d100).

sections.Special Attacks: Strength Bonus. Cavemen add +1 to damage rolls due to their great strength. Unarmed Combat. Cavemen can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with an 6+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.

monsters.name: Tribal warriors
monsters.description: Tribal warriors are usually at a bronze-age level of technology, although they may have steel weapons obtained from elsewhere. This entry allows for anything from Roman-era Germanic tribes to isolated island settlements, to post-catastrophic areas that have lost even a feudal level of civilisation. In their lair, there will be a chief (5th level fighter) and 1d4 guards (4th level fighters). There is always a 10% chance (per every 10 tribal warriors) that a 3rd level cleric will be present. Additional Leaders. • One 4th level fighter per 10 • One 6th level fighter per 30 • One 8th level cleric/druid. They are usually armed with spears, shields, short bows, and short swords (longswords, if there is better access to steel, or spears if metal is scarce in the area). Their treasure will consist of furs, gold nuggets, or uncut gems (5% chance per 10 tribal warriors present). If one is present, it will be the only treasure there. The value of each is 1,000 gp per bale of furs (2d6), 5 gp gold nuggets (2d4×10), and 10 gp gems (1d100). Unarmed Combat. Tribal warriors can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with an 8+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.

monsters.name: Mystic nomad
monsters.description: Previous editions used the term “dervish”, which isn’t accurate to the broader concept. Mystic nomads are highly-religious warrior-bands, of any lawful alignment. They will always be led by higher level fighters and clerics as follows. Fighters • For every 30 mystic nomads: 1 additional 3rd level fighter • For every 40 mystic nomads: 1 additional 4th level fighter • For every 50 mystic nomads: 1 additional 5th level fighter Clerics • If under 125 mystic nomads: (1) 10th level cleric and 2 assistants (4th & 5th level clerics) • If under 250 mystic nomads: (1) 11th level cleric and 2 assistants (6th & 7th level clerics) • If more than 250: (1) 12th level cleric and 2 assistants (both 8th level clerics) There is a 15% chance per 50 mystic nomads that a magic-user will be present. The magic-user will be of 7th or 8th level (if more than 200 mystic nomads are present) with two assistants of 3rd or 4th level. Mystic nomads are always mounted on light or medium warhorses.

sections.Special Attacks: Mystic nomads are disciplined and fearless, attacking with +1 on to-hit and damage rolls. Unarmed Combat. Mystic nomads can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with an 8+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.

monsters.name: Mounted nomads
monsters.description: Nomads are mounted clans that live on steppes, plains or in desert climes. They live by hunting and gathering and are closely tied to their native climate. Nomads will always be led by higher level fighters as follows: • If under 150 nomads: (1) 8th level fighter, (1) 6th level fighter, and 12 guards (2nd level fighters) • Between 150–250 nomads: (1) 9th level fighter, (1) 7th level fighter, and guards (2nd level fighters) • Over 250 nomads: (1) 10th level fighter, (1) 8th level fighter, and guards (2nd level fighters) There is a 15% chance per 50 nomads that a cleric will be present. The cleric will be of 4th to 7th level (determined by 1d4). There is also a 15% chance per 50 nomads that a magic-user (of 5th to 8th level, also determined by 1d4) will be present. In addition to the above, there will always be (2) 3rd level clerics and (1) 4th level magic-user present. Nomads will always be mounted on either light or medium warhorses.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Mounted nomads surprise on 1–4 on a d6.
sections.Special Attacks: Unarmed Combat. Mounted nomads can make grappling or overbearing attacks but only if unmounted. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with an 8+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/ DEF +8/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.

monsters.name: Pilgrim
monsters.description: Pilgrims are groups of religious followers making their way to some holy site. They can be encountered almost anywhere. There will always be higher level character types with groups of pilgrims: these higher-level types are the actual threat and carry the lion’s share of the treasure. The “pilgrim” described in the stats above is almost a noncombatant, but the higher-level defenders can make attacking a pilgrimage quite dangerous! Clerics: There will always be clerics with pilgrims, but if the group is neutral these clerics will be druids. • 1d6 2nd level clerics • 1d4 4th level clerics • 1d2 6th level clerics • 1 8th level cleric with 2 assistants (3rd and 5th level)

monsters.name: Merchant, merchants and
monsters.description: Base Fighters: There is a 10% chance per every 10 pilgrims that there will be 1d10 fighters present (roll 1d8 to determine the levels of the fighters). If the group is lawful good, some of these fighters may be replaced by paladins. If the group is chaotic good, some of these fighters may be replaced by rangers. Thieves: There is a 10% chance per every 10 pilgrim that there will be 1d6 thieves present (roll 1d6+1 to determine the levels of the thieves). If the group is evil, some of these thieves may be replaced by assassins. Magic-Users: There is a 5% chance per every 10 pilgrims that there will be a magic-user present (level 1d4+5). Alignment is determined for the entire group (with little variation) by rolling d100 with the likelihood of each alignment as follows: D100 ALIGNMENT 01–34 Lawful good 35–55 Chaotic good 56–66 Neutral 65–80 Chaotic evil 81–00 Lawful evil Most of the time (75%) pilgrims will be travel without mounts. However if they are mounted, all members of the group will be mounted. There is a chance (5%) that a holy item will be with the pilgrims. If so, it will be hidden and carefully guarded. Unarmed Combat. Pilgrims can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with an 6+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0. Merchant encounters are actually caravans of merchants, drovers, and guards. The caravan will also contain pack animals, carts, and horses. The guards will always be led by a higher-level fighter of 6th to 11th level (1d6+5), a lieutenant (1 level lower than the captain), and 12 guards (2nd level fighters). • There is a 10% chance per 50 persons that a magic-user of 6th to 8th level is present (1d3+5). • There is a 5% chance per 50 persons that a cleric of 5th to 7th level (1d3+4) is present. • There is also a 15% chance per 50 persons that a thief of 8th to 10th level will be present (along with 1d4 lower level thieves of 3rd to 7th level). All of the above leader or special character types are in addition to the number of merchants generated. Treasure: The treasure for a caravan will be as follows:

monsters.name: Hydra, 5-6 headed
monsters.description: If A hydra is a multi-headed reptilian monster that lives in damp, dark places like swamps, bogs, or marshes. Sometimes they are found underground if the lair is sufficiently dank and wet. Hydras have reptilian bodies, four legs, a tail and 1d8+4 heads. Each head counts as 1 hit die and has 8 full hit points, so a 10 headed hydra will have 10 hit dice and 80 hp. Each head can attack independently or up to four heads can attack a single target. The damage a hydra does is based on the number of heads. The colouration of a hydra ranges from light brown to an almost blackish brown with a yellow or tan underbelly. Their eyes range from yellow to orange. • Individual Merchants: 3d12 cp, 3d6 sp, 2d6 ep, 2d4 gp, 1d6 pp, 2d4 gp (40%), 1d6x10 pp (50%), 4d8 gems (55%), 1d12 pieces of jewellery (45%). • Individual Mercenaries: 3d6 sp. Individual Leaders: 2d4 gp. • Mercenary Pay Box (Hidden in Caravan): 2,000–4,000 gold (1d3+1), 100–400 pp (1d4), and 4d4 gems). • Caravan Goods: The caravan will be carrying goods and merchandise worth 10,000 to 60,000 gp. This requires either 10 pack animals or 1 cart per 5,000 gp worth of goods.

monsters.name: Hyena, normal
monsters.description: Normal hyenas are medium-sized mammals, 4–5ft long and weighing to around 100 lbs. They are muzzle-snouted, fur-covered, four-legged long-tailed predators and scavengers that hunt in packs and live sub-tropical grasslands, woodlands and waste-lands. Many find their ing, laugh-like bark unnerving and their tendency to raid shallow sometimes earned them an evil reputation. The jaws of a hyena are very powerful for their size. Unarmed Combat (Normal and Big): Normal and Big Hyenas cannot geted with grappling or overbearing attacks, but they may overbear. fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. If not fended off, they unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/na. Overbear Mods: ATK/DEF +4/na.

monsters.name: Invisible stalker
monsters.description: up and in dens in A denizen of the Elemental Plane of Air, an invishauntible stalker encountered on the Prime Material graves has Plane has been conjured and bound to service by a magic-user. The summoning magic-user retains command of the creature until it either fulfils the be tar- mission which it was summoned to perform or it If not is killed. ATK/DEF Invisible stalkers are useful, if dangerous, ser- Mods: ATK/ vants. Once given a mission they will relentlessly pursue their goal, motivated more by a dislike of or forced service and a desire to return to their home score an plane than by any sense of devotion to their sum- Results moner. Invisible stalkers are faultless trackers across any surface or distance and, if ordered to kill their prey, will attack without checking morale until either they or their target is dead. As implied above, invisible stalkers are not willing servants but will not normally begrudge performing a simple task of short duration for the summoner. More complicated tasks or tasks of duration longer than a week will anger the invisible stalker and may lead it to attempt to pervert the wording of its commands without directly violating them. If ordered to guard the summoner’s treasure in perpetuity, for instance, the invisible stalker might remove every last copper piece of the summoner’s treasure to a secret vault located within the invisible stalker’s lair on the Elemental Plane of Air, where the ‘stalker could easily keep watch over it. If the GM feels the invisible stalker’s service too onerous or complicated, assign a cumulative 1% per day chance of the ‘stalker wearying of its task and attempting to twist the meaning of its orders. A clever summoner might be able to word their orders in such a way make its meaning airtight and clear. In this case the ‘stalker must continue to serve until its duties are discharged.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Invisible stalkers surprise on a 1–5 on 1d6.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (30%). Any magic spell or effect has a 30% chance er level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the takes full effect.
sections.Special Features: Invisibility. While on the Prime Material Plane invisible stalkers can viewed by magical means (e.g. gem of seeing, true seeing, detect ity); otherwise anyone attacking an invisible stalker suffers a -2 “to hit”. An invisible stalker cannot be killed on this plane. Reducing zero hit points merely banishes it back to its home plane for a period 1 year plus 1 day. Unarmed Combat. Invisible stalkers cannot be targeted with grappling overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.
sections.Language: Invisible stalkers can understand the common tongue of the Prime terial Plane, the language of the Elemental Plane of Air, and their language. They will speak no tongue but their own.

monsters.name: Jackal, normal
monsters.description: Jackals are small mammals, 2ft to 3ft long and weighing about 25 lbs. are muzzle-snouted, fur-covered, four-legged and long-tailed nocturnal scavengers and occasional predators. They generally hunt and as to singly or in mated pairs, but occasionally gather in small packs to bring down difficult prey. Jackals can be found in subtropical grasslands, woodlands and wastelands, and occasionally in more mountainous terrain. They are most active at dawn and dusk, which has occasionally led to them being revered by death cults.
