monsters.name: Jackalwere
monsters.description: A jackalwere is a malevolent beast that can assume human form (and hence is not a lycanthrope, since lycanthropes are humans who can assume animal form). They will mingle with people, choosing easy targets to victimise. Living for the thrill of murder, many times they will consume the remains of their prey. Of- They ten they steal their victims’ possessions, assume their identities, and go on to the next town. In human form forage a jackalwere will most often attack with a weapon. Jackalweres sometimes prefer the company of normal jackals and can be found living among them from time to time.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Non-Iron Mundane Weapons. The jackalwere is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more, or is made of unsmelted cold iron (most metal weapons are steel rather than unsmelted iron).
sections.Special Features: Shapeshifter. A jackalwere can shift at will into the form of a human or back into its jackal form. Shifting does not affect the creature’s hit points or armour class, or cure the creature of any damage.
sections.Special Attacks: Sleep Gaze. Any creature meeting the gaze of a jackalwere must successfully save vs spells or fall into a magical sleep (save each time the gaze is met). This applies to anyone who is generally in front of the creature and not using an indirect method of sight such as a mirror. Attacking the creature by looking at a reflection incurs a to-hit penalty of -2. Attacking blindly incurs a to-hit penalty of -4. Unarmed Combat. In human form a jackalwere can make grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.

monsters.name: Kobold
monsters.loot: Individual 1 each; in lair Cache 1 and 3
monsters.description: Kobolds stand 3ft tall and are vaguely reptilian in appearance, with scaly skin, small horns, short, snaky tails and red eyes. The weakest of humanoids, physically, kobolds live in a hierarchical society of tribes and clans. They tend to make their lairs in dark places such as caves or deep forests. Kobold raiding parties are led by a sergeant and 2 assistants, who fight as goblins. Lairs are ruled by a chief and 5d4 bodyguards (all fight as goblins). Kobolds often (75%) use wild boars or giant weasels (the smallsized variety) to guard their lairs.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Vulnerability to Sunlight. Kobolds detest direct sunlight and fight at -1 if they are exposed to it.
sections.Special Attacks: Ranged Attack (Slings). Kobolds often employ slings as missile weapons (1d4 blunt damage), 35ft range increment (-2 at 36ft, -4 at 71ft). Unarmed Combat. Kobolds can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with an 8+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-2. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2.
sections.Language: These creatures speak lawful evil and their own tongue. Some also speak goblin.

monsters.name: Kraken
monsters.description: It is rumoured that the krakens once lived in shallower coastal waters and had armies of slaves who worshipped them. For some reason they were forced to retreat to the deepest depths of the oceans. In the darkness they grew larger and more powerful. They excavated huge labyrinths in the sea floor. Now they prey on ships for food and slaves which they drag down to their watery dungeons.

sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. 1/day: create a sphere of airy water 240ft across, faerie fire (8 hours), control temperature (40ft), control winds, and weather summoning. 3/day: animal (fish) summoning III which gives them the ability to summon the fish but not control them. Segmented Armour Class. A kraken’s body is protected by a tough shell with AC 0 [20], but its tentacles and head are more vulnerable, with AC 5 [15].
sections.Special Attacks: Attacking Ships. A kraken will attack a ship in the same way a giant squid does, by anchoring itself with 2 arms and attacking with the other 6. If the kraken wraps 6 tentacles around a ship and squeezes for 3 consecutive rounds, it will cause enough damage to sink the ship. If the kraken loses more than 3 arms it will release the ship, squirt ink, and flee. Tentacle. With each successful hit the kraken grabs its victim and holds it (see below). Each round after the hit, the tentacle does automatic damage without a to-hit roll, inflicting normal damage plus an additional 3d4 blunt damage from crushing. The only way to get free is to sever the tentacle by causing 16 hp damage to it (which does not damage the monster itself). Those within the tentacle’s grasp are 25% likely to have both arms held, and as such they cannot attack. Most of the time (50%) they will have one limb held and may attack with a -3 penalty. The other 25% of the time the victim will have both arms free and can attack the kraken with only a -1 penalty. Ink. When fleeing, a kraken releases ink in the water, leaving a cloud 80ft deep by 80ft wide by 120ft long. A kraken’s ink is poisonous and will cause 1d4 points of damage per round until the ink dissipates. The ink lasts for about 5 rounds.

monsters.name: Lamia
monsters.description: Lamiai like to live in deserted towns, ruins, and other desolate places. These creatures have the upper body of a woman and the lower half of an animal (usually a lion or tiger, but sometimes a serpent). Typically a lamia is armed with a dagger, but these are really just tools. They use spells to lure their victims close, and then drain their wisdom by touch.

sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. 1/day: charm person, mirror image, suggestion, and illusion (like the wand).
sections.Special Attacks: Wisdom-Draining Touch. The touch of a lamia permanently drains a single point of wisdom. The lamia does not need to roll to hit against a charmed victim, but must attack normally to touch a resisting opponent. Once a victim’s wisdom falls below 3, they become permanent slaves of the lamia (although they are likely to just be eaten). Unarmed Combat. Lamiai cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.
sections.Language: Lamiai speak the common tongue as well as the alignment language of Chaotic evil.

monsters.name: Lammasu
monsters.description: Champions of all that is good and just, lammasu have quadrupedal bodies the size and shape of the largest of lions, fully-functional feathered wings, and a human head bearing the kindly visage of a bearded wise man. Lammasu are the guardians and protectors of all lawful good persons and have a friendly disposition to all good-aligned creatures they encounter. Lammasu tend to lair in warm climates but travel widely and can thus be encountered anywhere. Lammasu prefer to advise and support the forces of good if at all possible, but are formidable opponents in battle. In fact, it is almost impossible to press a lammasu into combat against its will due to its ability to dimension door and become invisible at will.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (30%). Any magic spell or effect has a 30% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Protection from Evil. Lammasu are constantly surrounded by an extra strength protection from evil, 10ft radius (-2 to attack, +2 on saving throws from attacking evil creatures).
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: dimension door and become invisible. 20% of these creatures can also speak a holy word at will. Spells. Lammasu can cast cleric spells of up to 4th level as an 8th level cleric does. Spell list: 4—1st level, 3—2nd level, 2—3rd level, 1—4th level. They cast cure light wounds and cure serious wounds at double normal efficacy (2d8 hp and 4d8+2 hp respectively). Unarmed Combat. Lammasu cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.
sections.Language: Lammasu can communicate in their own tongue, the alignment language of lawful good creatures, and also through telepathy.

monsters.name: Larval fiend
monsters.description: Larval fiends, sometimes called soul worms, are the extraplanar form of evil souls. Their appearance is similar to a putrescent maggot with a leering humanoid face. They live in great squirming masses and are tended by night hags, who trade them to demons and devils for the creation of quasits and imps. Liches also make use of soul worms to help preserve their essence throughout the centuries. They are not usually found on the prime material plane unless they have somehow been intercepted by a night hag or lich. Unarmed Combat. Larval fiends cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Leech, giant
monsters.attacks: 1 bite. Damage: 1d4 (1 HD), 1d6 (2–3 HD) or 1d8 (4 HD)
monsters.description: Giant leeches inhabit warmer, fresh water.

sections.Special Attacks: Blood Drain. If a giant leech successfully hits a character, it drains hp equal to its hit dice each round automatically thereafter (so a 4 HD leech drains 4hp per round). Disease. A character bitten by a giant leech must save vs poison or suffer a disease that will be fatal in 1d6 weeks. Unarmed Combat. Giant leeches cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Leprechaun
monsters.description: Leprechauns are a type of fey that love to torment those they encounter with practical jokes, general mischief, and swindles. They normally live in green fields or rolling hills on the outskirts of civilisation. Because of their sharp senses they are never surprised. One of the leprechaun’s favourite tricks is to grab some valuable object, turn invisible and flee with it. If they are chased too closely, they will drop the item rather than be tracked back to their lair. If they are caught or tracked back to their lair, the leprechaun will do or say just about anything to win their freedom back. Be warned: leprechauns are magical, and they take great pride in their confidence games. Nothing they say should be considered the truth. A leprechaun will always be playing some kind of scam.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Leprechauns cannot be surprised.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (80%). Any magic spell or effect has an 80% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect.
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: A leprechaun can turn invisible, polymorph inanimate objects, make illusions, and perform ventriloquism at will. Unarmed Combat. Leprechauns can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with an 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/- 10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF -4/+4. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -4/+4.

monsters.name: Lich
monsters.description: Liches are the remains of powerful wizard-priests who, through fell magics and sinister grimoires, have cheated death and live on beyond the grave in a decaying shell that still revels in awesome magical energies. Unholy magics and an unwavering devotion are not the only things keeping them on the prime material plane. Their souls are already traded to dark gods, but a spark of their essence remains that must be encased in a talisman of sorts. This trinket is a requirement of their Unlife, but no scholar knows how or why this is. The lair of a lich will often be a complex underworld maze or a wickedly diseased stretch of thick wilderness, at whose black heart resides a tower riddled with magic traps and deadly guardians. Liches do not suffer the fools who would tread upon their mysteries. Often dressed in rich decaying rags that were exquisite in life, liches are now horrors to behold. They are cadaverous in appearance, with unholy pin-points of green light emanating from the otherwise empty pits that are the eye-sockets of its fleshless skull. Diseased and leprous tatters of meat cling feebly to ancient bones, reeking with the rot of the grave. Liches are believed to feast on larval fiends as part of the regimen that maintains their unlife.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Turned as Undead. Liches are turned as type 12 Undead. Immune to Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more. Undeath. This creature is immune to all mind control (including charm) and hold spells. It cannot be affected by sleep, gases, poison, or disease. Other Immunities. Liches are immune to cold, electrical, paralysation, polymorph, and death magic. Spells that drain attributes or statistics also have no effect.
sections.Special Features: Spell Use. All liches are powerful spellcasters. 40% of liches cast spells as a magic-user, 40% as a cleric, and 20% as both, at 18th level of ability. Those with magic-user abilities will have multiple copies of powerful spell tomes.

monsters.name: Lion
monsters.description: LION These prefer warm climates and thrive in any such locale be it jungle or savannah. Lions organise themselves into family units called prides. Males are aggressive fighters, defending the territory and the other members of the pride. The female, referred to as a lioness, does all the hunting. A pride will have 1d2 males and 2d4+1 females. If encountered in their lair, there will be 1d10 cubs in various stages of growth but too immature to fight. All adult pride members will fight to the death to protect the young. Lions cannot climb trees and will only swim under duress. COUGAR Popularly known as mountain lions, these great cats are not true lions but are similar in most respects. Cougars are more solitary than lions and tend to range more widely while hunting. They are also more prone to attack if approached than are true lions. Though they share habitat preferences with lions they also inhabit mountains as well, giving rise to their popular name. Mountain lions can leap 20ft to attack or spring upwards 15ft. Aura of Fear. Anything below 6th level beholding a lich (even in a reflection or a projected image) must save vs magic or flee, never to return to the area again.

sections.Special Attacks: Paralysing Touch. The mere touch of a lich will inflict 2d6 cold damage upon the victim, and they must save vs paralysation or be held frozen to the spot for 3d8 turns. Unarmed Combat. Liches can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with an 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0. PREHISTORIC LION Also known as “cave lions” or “spotted lions,” with the exception of their larger size these cats are very similar to regular lions. Cave lions tend to be found in “lost world” type settings but have been encountered in the same areas as ordinary lions. Rake. All lions gain an extra two rear leg raking claw attacks (for the same damage as their forepaws) if they successfully hit with both clawing attacks in melee. Unarmed Combat (Lions and Prehistoric Lions): Lions cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, but they may overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +5/na. Unarmed Combat (Cougars): Cougars cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, but they may overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +3/na. LYCANTHROPE A lycanthrope is a human with the ability to change their shape to some animal form, or a hybrid human-animal form, during the night hours. A full moon is 90% likely to trigger the transition to animal form automatically. Any humanoid bitten by a lycanthrope and damaged for 50% or more of its total hp who survives will contract the lycanthropic disease of its attacker. A cure disease from a cleric of 12th level or higher will remove the disease if performed within three days of the attack. If the victim ingests belladonna within one hour after the attack there is a 25% chance the disease will be cured. However, swallowing belladonna in such a manner will incapacitate the victim for 1d4 days; there is also a 1% chance of the herb killing the victim. A lycanthrope’s “size” stat shows its shape-changed size. In human form they are obviously always medium-sized. Each type of lycanthrope has its own language. The five most common types are listed below.
sections.Surprise and Initiative: Alert. Lions (all types) are only surprised on a 1 in 1d6.

monsters.name: Lycanthrope, werebear
monsters.description: WEREBEAR A werebear appears in human form as a large hairy human with a solitary disposition. In ursine form, they are 50% likely to be accompanied by 1d6 brown bears.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Non-Silver Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more, or is made of silver. Robust Health. Werebears are immune to disease and heal at 3x the normal rate. Immune to Non-Silver Mundane Weapons. monsters.name: Lizard, giant, fire
monsters.description: FIRE LIZARDS Fire lizards are also known as “false dragons” and are thought to be an evolutionary dead-end of the dragon family tree. These giant lizards have a tough scaled hide very similar to a dragon but lacking the long life, wings, and horns of their fire-breathing cousins. Colouration tends to be a rather neutral grey with patches of a dark brownish red on the dorsal surface, and a lighter red on the ventral surface. Fire lizards darken in colour as they age. Curiously, red dragons avoid confrontation with fire lizards and will not even lair in the same area fire lizards frequent. False dragons are normally slow-moving creatures and spend 50% their time sleeping in their subterranean lairs. When they emerge every two weeks or so to feed, however, they are aggressive foes. Fire lizards have an affinity for shiny objects and their lairs tend be littered with coins and gems. A lair also has a 15% chance of containing 1d6 eggs, but the fire lizard is largely indifferent as to their fate. The first hatchling will generally eat the others as they emerge. A fire lizard egg can fetch as much as 5,000gp from an interested party.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Fire. Fire lizards are immune to fire damage.
sections.Special Attacks: Breath Weapon. Fire lizards can exhale a cone-shaped blast of flame 10ft wide at the terminus with a range of 150ft, causing 2d6 points of fire damage. A saving throw vs breath weapons is allowed for half damage. Breathing fire takes up the lizard’s action for that round, but the breath weapon can be used as often as the lizard chooses. Unarmed Combat. Fire Lizards cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks; they may, occasionally, overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +10/ na. GIANT LIZARDS Giant Lizards dwell in marshy or swampy areas, but can also be found underground. Other than their size, they are unremarkable beasts. Powerful Bite. On a to-hit roll of 20+ (including a modified 20), a giant lizard has grabbed its opponent firmly in its powerful jaws and will cause double damage that round. MONITOR LIZARDS Monitor Lizards are aggressive carnivores found in warm regions. Their colouration tends toward dark grey and black and they have longer snouts and longer, sharper teeth than other types of giant lizards. Bite. On a to-hit roll of 20+ (including a modified 20), in addition to ordinary damage, the monitor has seized its opponent in its toothy maw and the unfortunate victim is subjected to an automatic hit in the following round. Unarmed Combat. Giant monitor lizards cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics. CAVE LIZARDS Cave Lizards dwell in underground settings such as caverns and dungeons. Powerful Bite. On a natural to-hit roll of 20, the cave lizard’s jaws have clamped onto its prey, causing double damage on that attack. Unarmed Combat. Giant cave lizards cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.
sections.Surprise and Initiative: Monitor lizards move slowly, but can lunge suddenly, surprising their prey on a 1-4 on 1d6.
sections.Special Features: Climber. This creature can move on walls and ceilings as if they were floors.

Unarmed Combat. Fire Lizards cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks; they may, occasionally, overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +10/ na. GIANT LIZARDS Giant Lizards dwell in marshy or swampy areas, but can also be found underground. Other than their size, they are unremarkable beasts. Powerful Bite. On a to-hit roll of 20+ (including a modified 20), a giant lizard has grabbed its opponent firmly in its powerful jaws and will cause double damage that round. MONITOR LIZARDS Monitor Lizards are aggressive carnivores found in warm regions. Their colouration tends toward dark grey and black and they have longer snouts and longer, sharper teeth than other types of giant lizards. Bite. On a to-hit roll of 20+ (including a modified 20), in addition to ordinary damage, the monitor has seized its opponent in its toothy maw and the unfortunate victim is subjected to an automatic hit in the following round. Unarmed Combat. Giant monitor lizards cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics. CAVE LIZARDS Cave Lizards dwell in underground settings such as caverns and dungeons. Powerful Bite. On a natural to-hit roll of 20, the cave lizard’s jaws have clamped onto its prey, causing double damage on that attack. Unarmed Combat. Giant cave lizards cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.
sections.Surprise and Initiative: Monitor lizards move slowly, but can lunge suddenly, surprising their prey on a 1-4 on 1d6.
sections.Special Features: Climber. This creature can move on walls and ceilings as if they were floors.

monsters.name: Lizard man
monsters.attacks: 2 claws (1d2) and 1 bite (1d8) or by weapon
monsters.description: Lizardmen are bipedal reptile-people. Their hides are tough and leathery, and are coloured in many different shades of green. They have cold black eyes, and hard nails on their fingers. Some have a bony ridge along their backs. Lizard men often make their homes in underwater caves that contain air. They are semi-aquatic and require air to breathe. They are excellent swimmers, and will eat most anything, though they prefer human meat to all others. Some communities of lizardmen are more civilized than others. These make their homes in crude villages and use shields for protection. These lizard men tribes also make use of barbed darts and javelins as missile weapons. For the most part, these lizardmen still hunt and eat humans.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Hold Breath. This creature can go for up to an hour between breaths.
sections.Special Attacks: Ranged Attack. Advanced lizardmen can use missile weapons as humans do. Unarmed Combat. Lizardmen can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.
sections.Language: Lizard men speak their own tongue, and a few (10%) can also speak common.

monsters.name: Locathah
monsters.description: Locathah are bipedal fish-people, covered in scales. They have large, black eyes and large fan-shaped finned ears. Locathah can leave the water for short periods (2d10 minutes) of time but are loath to do so. For the most part, locathah make their home in the warm, shallow, salt waters of seas and oceans. They roam the area around their lair, hunting and gathering food. They are rather distrustful of strangers, even strangers of their own species. Lairs are built in undersea rock formations, very much like human fortifications, and they often alter the rock face to a distinctive fortress-like appearance. The locathah will hollow the rock into rooms, chambers, and passages as needed and doors are typically quite sturdy and well-guarded either by moray eels or trapped air bubbles containing Portuguese man-o-wars. Locathah troops are organised into companies of 40 warriors, each led by a war-chief with 22 hit points who fights as a 5th level fighter. The war-chief is assisted by 4 sub-chiefs with 15 hp who fight as 3rd level fighters. Any group of 3 or more companies (120 warriors) will be led by a full chief with 30 hp who fights as a 6th level fighter. The chief will be protected by an honour guard of 12 warriors who fight as sub-chiefs. There is a 5% chance a sub-chief or war-chief will be carrying a magic weapon of the appropriate type and a 10% a full chief will have one. Locathah troops ride giant eels (q.v.) into battle and these mounts will also fight. • One-fourth of locathah troops are armed with lances (2d4+1 piercing). • One-fourth of locathah troops are armed with tridents (1d6+1 piercing). • One-fourth of locathah troops are armed with light crossbow (1d4+1 piercing) and dagger. The light crossbows have a 20ft range underwater. • One-fourth of locathah troops are armed with net and dagger.

sections.Special Attacks: Ranged or Melee Attack (Net). Some locathah are armed with nets. These have a range of 20ft (and can be thrown while in melee combat). If the attack hits, the target is automatically (no saving throw) entangled for 1d4 rounds, unable to attack or move. Unarmed Combat. Locathah can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks and may use these tactics. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.

monsters.name: Lurker above
monsters.description: Lurkers are dangerous creatures that wait in high places for prey to pass beneath them. In shape they resemble manta rays, but have such colouration and form that they can become almost indistinguishable from the stone of the caverns in which they dwell.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Lurkers surprise on a 1-5 in 1d6, even if they wait to drop (this is a measure of how difficult they are to see).
sections.Special Attacks: Drop and Smother. Lurkers attack by dropping onto a creature and enfolding it. Lurkers that successfully engulf their victim (on a successful to-hit roll) automatically cause 1d6 points of damage from constriction every round thereafter and will cause suffocation within 1d4+1 rounds. Those engulfed may only use short weapons (short sword or smaller) against their attacker and are not in a position to change weapons. Lurkers continue to attack until slain. Fortunately for adventurers, lurkers have such a tough body that attacking a lurker that has enfolded someone does not damage the enfolded victim. Unarmed Combat. Lurkers above cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Lynx, giant
monsters.description: Rare and magical, giant lynxes live in the icy wastes and in deep forests, where they use their intelligence to advantage against competing predators.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Owing to their camouflaged pelts, giant lynxes surprise opponents on a 1–5 on 1d6.
sections.Special Features: Thief Abilities. Giant lynxes have the thief skills Hide, Move Quietly and Climb at 90% and Traps at 75%.
sections.Special Attacks: Rake. If a giant lynx hits with both claw attacks, it gains an additional 2 attacks with the rear claws (1d3 slashing). Unarmed Combat. Giant lynxes cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, but may choose to overbear a lone opponent. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +2/na.
sections.Language: Giant lynxes speak their own language and that of the fey.

monsters.name: Manticore
monsters.description: A manticore has a lion’s body with a human head and bat-like wings. Its tail is thick and club-like at the end, and bristles with iron spikes. They make their lairs in dark, dank caves or desolate underground caverns, flying out by night to hunt sheep, cattle, and (if available) humans.

sections.Special Attacks: Tail Spikes. The manticore can launch 6 tail spikes (1d6 piercing) at a range of up to 60ft (120ft at -2, 180ft at -4). A manticore has 24 spikes total, which regrow fully after as little as 2 days. Unarmed Combat. Manticores cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, but may choose to overbear a lone opponent. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +4/na.
sections.Language: Manticores are monsters, and despite the humanlike head they only speak the alignment tongue of lawful evil.

monsters.name: Medusa
monsters.description: Medusae resemble the monster from Greek myth: women with snakes for hair, whose gaze turns people to stone. One of the most effective weapons against a medusa is a mirror, for a medusa that sees her own reflection may be turned to stone herself if she fails her save.

monsters.name: Mephit, fire
monsters.description: Mephits are the varlets, lackeys, messengers, errand runners, and fetchers of the Lower Planes. They can be found in any of the evilly-aligned lower planes and will be serving the various demons, devils, evil elemental gods, or any extra-planar creature of dark purpose and evil intent. Their exact origins and home plane are not known; even the mephits themselves do not know for certain. This entry lists the known types of mephits, but dark rumours persist of other types more dangerous than these.

sections.Special Attacks: Poison Snakebite. The medusa attacks by drawing near to the victim, allowing her snakes to lash out and bite. In addition to the 1d6 piercing damage, anyone bitten must make a saving throw vs. poison or die. Petrifying Gaze. Any creature meeting the gaze of a medusa must successfully save vs petrifaction or instantly be turned to stone (save each time the gaze is met). The gaze effects extend into both the astral and ethereal planes. This applies to anyone who is generally in front of the medusa, and not using an indirect method of sight such as a mirror. Attacking the creature by looking at a reflection incurs a to-hit penalty of -2. Attacking blindly incurs a to-hit penalty of -4. Unarmed Combat. Medusae can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0. Breath Weapon. The fire mephit’s breath weapon has two modes: a jet of flame 15ft long and 1 inch wide, or a blanket of flame 5ft square. The jet is directed against a single target and always hits, causing 1d8+1 fire damage; a saving throw vs breath weapons is allowed for half damage. The blanket of flame causes 4 points of damage to each victim in the area of effect, no saving throw allowed. LAVA MEPHIT These mephits are red in colour and sweat droplets of molten lava. As a result, the lava mephit is so hot it can be sensed up to 30ft away. Touching one without protection results in 1d8 points of damage. The touch of a lava mephit dissolves metal rather quickly, destroying plate mail armour in 3 melee rounds. Wood dissolves a little more slowly, about an inch per hour of contact. The lava mephit can shape-change into a pool of lava but doing so will not recharge the mephit’s breath weapon or allow it to regenerate. Spit Lava. In addition to its attack, every 3 rounds a lava mephit can spit a blob of molten lava, up to 8 times before recharging (see below). The projectile has a 10ft range, always hits the mephit’s target, and inflicts 1d6 fire damage with no saving throw. Contact with lava also allows the mephit to recharge its breath weapon. SMOKE MEPHIT This type of mephit is charcoal black, and constantly emits smoke. When encountered on the Prime Material Plane, smoke mephits rarely stray from dark or smoky areas except in great need. Smoke mephits attack with two claws, and may employ their breath weapon while in combat. Smokeball (every other round). The smoke mephit’s breath weapon is a ball of oily smoke that automatically strikes its target, with a range of 20ft, dealing 1d4 hp, no save allowed. In addition to the hit point damage, the victim is blinded for 1d2 rounds. There is no limit to the number of times a smoke mephit may use its breath weapon. STEAM MEPHIT These mephits constantly sweat hot water in profuse amounts, leaving puddles of hot water behind them as they travel. Touching a steam mephit causes 1 point of damage to unprotected skin and has a 50% chance to stun the victim for 1 melee round. Spit Scalding Water (every other round). The steam mephit can spit a stream of scalding water that will automatically hit any single target within 20ft. The stream inflicts 1d3 points of damage and has a 50% chance to stun the target (no saving throw allowed).
sections.Language: Medusae speak the common tongue. Mephits share various common characteristics. They are all about 5ft tall, bat-winged, with sharp fangs. Mephits speak their own language shared by all the different types of mephits, their alignment tongue, and usually speak the common tongue of whatever lower plane they happen to call home. Mephits are mischievous and have a malignant sense of humour, finding joy in the pain of others. Unarmed Combat. Mephits cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics. FIRE MEPHITS Fire mephits are wreathed with tiny wisps of flame, and touching one bare-handed will cause 1 point of damage. In combat mephits attack with two claws and a breath weapon.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Fire. Fire mephitis are immune to fire damage. Immune to Fire. Lava mephitis are immune to fire damage. Immune to Fire. Smoke mephits are immune to fire damage. Immune to Fire. Steam mephits are immune to fire damage.
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. 1/Hour: attempt to gate in another mephit, type determined randomly, (33% chance of success). 1/day: magic missile (two missiles) and heat metal. Limited Regeneration. When in contact with molten lava, the lava mephit can regenerate 2 hp per round, but if killed it cannot regenerate back to life as a troll does. Spell-Like Abilities. 1/Hour: gate in 1d2 mephits (25% chance of success). The type is random, but if two appear, they will be the same type. Burning Touch. Although it has no effect in combat, a lava mephit can melt metal and burn wood by prolonged contact, destroying doors or other impediments. Death Flash. If slain, the smoke mephit emits a burst of flashfire which inflicts 1 point of damage to everyone with 10ft, no saving throw allowed. Spell-Like Abilities. 1/Hour: gate in 1d2 mephits (25% chance of success). The type is random, but if two appear, they are the same type. 1/day: invisibility and dancing lights. Spell-Like Abilities. 1/Hour: gate in 1d2 mephits (30% chance of success). The type is random, but if two appear, they are the same type. Also, the steam mephit can contaminate water (as the reverse of the purify water spell). 1/day: rain boiling water in a 40×40ft square area of effect for 2d6 hp to all in the affected area (no saving throw).

SMOKE MEPHIT This type of mephit is charcoal black, and constantly emits smoke. When encountered on the Prime Material Plane, smoke mephits rarely stray from dark or smoky areas except in great need. Smoke mephits attack with two claws, and may employ their breath weapon while in combat. Smokeball (every other round). The smoke mephit’s breath weapon is a ball of oily smoke that automatically strikes its target, with a range of 20ft, dealing 1d4 hp, no save allowed. In addition to the hit point damage, the victim is blinded for 1d2 rounds. There is no limit to the number of times a smoke mephit may use its breath weapon. STEAM MEPHIT These mephits constantly sweat hot water in profuse amounts, leaving puddles of hot water behind them as they travel. Touching a steam mephit causes 1 point of damage to unprotected skin and has a 50% chance to stun the victim for 1 melee round. Spit Scalding Water (every other round). The steam mephit can spit a stream of scalding water that will automatically hit any single target within 20ft. The stream inflicts 1d3 points of damage and has a 50% chance to stun the target (no saving throw allowed).
sections.Language: Medusae speak the common tongue. Mephits share various common characteristics. They are all about 5ft tall, bat-winged, with sharp fangs. Mephits speak their own language shared by all the different types of mephits, their alignment tongue, and usually speak the common tongue of whatever lower plane they happen to call home. Mephits are mischievous and have a malignant sense of humour, finding joy in the pain of others. Unarmed Combat. Mephits cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics. FIRE MEPHITS Fire mephits are wreathed with tiny wisps of flame, and touching one bare-handed will cause 1 point of damage. In combat mephits attack with two claws and a breath weapon.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Fire. Fire mephitis are immune to fire damage. Immune to Fire. Lava mephitis are immune to fire damage. Immune to Fire. Smoke mephits are immune to fire damage. Immune to Fire. Steam mephits are immune to fire damage.
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. 1/Hour: attempt to gate in another mephit, type determined randomly, (33% chance of success). 1/day: magic missile (two missiles) and heat metal. Limited Regeneration. When in contact with molten lava, the lava mephit can regenerate 2 hp per round, but if killed it cannot regenerate back to life as a troll does. Spell-Like Abilities. 1/Hour: gate in 1d2 mephits (25% chance of success). The type is random, but if two appear, they will be the same type. Burning Touch. Although it has no effect in combat, a lava mephit can melt metal and burn wood by prolonged contact, destroying doors or other impediments. Death Flash. If slain, the smoke mephit emits a burst of flashfire which inflicts 1 point of damage to everyone with 10ft, no saving throw allowed. Spell-Like Abilities. 1/Hour: gate in 1d2 mephits (25% chance of success). The type is random, but if two appear, they are the same type. 1/day: invisibility and dancing lights. Spell-Like Abilities. 1/Hour: gate in 1d2 mephits (30% chance of success). The type is random, but if two appear, they are the same type. Also, the steam mephit can contaminate water (as the reverse of the purify water spell). 1/day: rain boiling water in a 40×40ft square area of effect for 2d6 hp to all in the affected area (no saving throw).

monsters.name: Merman
monsters.description: Mermen (also called “merfolk”) appear as normal humans from the waist up, but as human-sized fish or dolphins from the waist down. They disdain clothing, though they will often adorn themselves with plundered jewellery and use any enchanted weapons and protective magic rings or bracers they may gain in their raids. Merfolk are the inhabitants of oceans and seas in the warmer areas of the world, being particularly fond of tropical seas. Mermen are much like rural humans, farming and harvesting vegetation on the ocean floor and hunting in the area around their settlements; they hunt for fish and other sea–going creatures. Merfolk have been known to herd certain fish, keeping them corralled in large, spherical netted seaweed pens in much the same way their human counterparts will herd cattle. Merfolk tend to congregate in small communities, establishing their dwellings in reefs or underwater cliffs and tunnelling many rooms and passages into these natural structures. Rarely, mermen will construct dwellings of natural materials such as seashells, coral, rocks, and materials scavenged from sunken sailing vessels. These communities, no matter the location, will correspond to a human agricultural type community in many respects: there will be workshops, residences, pens for the food fish, and storage areas for the harvested sea vegetation. Merfolk rarely venture from the ocean but can sometimes be spotted sunning themselves on coastal rocks in isolated areas. Merfolk communities are guarded by 3d6 giant gar (see Fish, Giant), bred and trained by the mermen for this purpose. In battle, merfolk troops encountered will be armed as follows: • 50% trident • 25% crossbow (1d4+1 piercing) and dagger. The light crossbows have a 20ft range underwater. • 25% net (see below), javelin, and dagger. Though mermen tend to avoid humans under most circumstances, they have been known to attack and sink surface vessels to plunder them. Grappling hook-equipped mermen will surface and hurl their grapples up to 30ft as the other mermen attack exposed crewman on the ship with crossbows and thrown javelins. The merfolk are quite proficient with grapples and will successfully score a hit on a roll of 1–9 on a 1d10. If a grapple hits it will be grabbed and held by 10 mermen, causing the ship to lose 30ft per round of top speed for each successful grapple attack. If the crew of the ship manages to cut a grapple line it will take the 10 mermen holding the line a round to regroup and return to the fight. Any merman grappling the ship or laying down cover fire is exposed to ranged attack from the ship. Further, fire-based attacks will cause double damage but only for a single round. If the grappled ship is successfully rendered motionless it will be pulled underwater in 4d4 rounds. Any crewmen abandoning ship at this time will be ignored as the ship and mermen sink beneath the waves. Mermen do not take surface dwellers prisoner, but will not normally harm any crewmen in the water—unless the crew of the ship foolishly try to continue the battle.

sections.Special Attacks: Ranged or Melee Attack (Net). Some mermen are armed with nets. These have a range of 20ft (and can be thrown while in melee combat). If the attack hits, the target is automatically (no saving throw) entangled for 1d4 rounds, unable to attack or move.
sections.Language: Merfolk speak their own language, 50% speak locathah, and if the merfolk dwell near any other intelligent aquatic creatures at least 10% of the community will be able to speak that tongue as well.

monsters.name: Minotaur
monsters.attacks: 1 gore (2d4) or 1 bite (1d4), or by weapon
monsters.description: Minotaurs usually like to inhabit vast mazes whether they be underground or outdoors. They are excellent trackers (50% chance to track) and will always give chase if they can see their prey. These beasts are man–eaters and will attack savagely anything they think they can kill and eat. They are stupid and can be tricked. Minotaurs can attack with their horns only if their opponent is medium-sized or larger. They have to bite smaller foes or attack with a weapon.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Minotaurs are surprised only on a 1 in 1d6. Unarmed Combat. Minotaurs can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +3/-3. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2.
sections.Language: Minotaurs can speak their own language and sometimes (25%) can speak common.

monsters.name: Mould, brown
monsters.description: BROWN MOULD Brown mould can be found in places where it escapes the effects of ultraviolet light. It feeds on most other sources of energy, and absorbs the body heat of any creature that comes within 5ft.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Almost Unkillable. Brown Mould cannot be killed without the use of a wish spell. The only thing that really affects it is magical cold. An ice storm or wall of ice will make the brown mould go into a dormant state for 5d6 turns. Immune to All but Fire. Yellow mould is extremely susceptible to fire and fire attacks, but cannot be killed by any other means. A continual light spell will force the mould to go dormant for 2d6 turns until it covers the light source. If it is set alight, the mould will die in 1d3+3 rounds.
sections.Special Features: Growth by Fire. Brown mould grows in the presence of heat, so that the presence of high (fiery) temperatures can cause the mould to increase its size by a factor of 2d4 times in the course of a melee round.
sections.Special Attacks: Heat Absorption. Heat absorption from a brown mould deals damage to all creatures within 5ft, at a rate of 4d8 cold damage per combat round (this is approximately 1d8 per 10 degrees Fahrenheit of body heat over 50 degrees). Creatures that are colder (undead, in particular) will take less damage or potentially none at all. YELLOW MOULD Yellow mould is a growth found only in dark places, more of a hazard than a monster. Spores. When touched, yellow mould releases spores in a 10ft (cube) cloud. Any creature within this area will die unless it successfully saves vs poison. A dead character will require a cure disease in addition to raise dead or resurrection, or they will remain infected and die again. If any surface covered in yellow mould is handled roughly, there is a 50% chance spores will be released in such a cloud.

monsters.name: Mule
monsters.description: Mules are a sterile cross-breed of horses and donkeys, and are sure-footed enough to be taken into dungeons. Their stubbornness is legendary. The stats given for mules can also be used for asses and donkeys, although these should have their hit points rolled on d6s rather than d8s to reflect their smaller size.

monsters.name: Mummy
monsters.description: The mummy is an undead creature. Normally found in tombs or other burial places, they hate life and attempt to destroy any living creature they encounter. A raise dead spell will transform the monster into a 7th-level fighter unless the mummy makes a successful save vs spells.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Turned as Undead. Mummies are turned as type 8 Undead. Immune to Mundane Weapons and Resistant to All Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more. Even a magic weapon inflicts only half damage on a mummy (drop fractions). Undeath. This creature is immune to all mind control (including charm) and hold spells. It cannot be affected by sleep, gases, poison, or disease. Vulnerable to Fire. A mummy is susceptible to fire. A hit from a torch will deal 1d3 hp damage, a flask of burning oil causes 1d8 hp on the first round and 2d8 hp on the second round, and magical fires deal +1 for each die of damage.
sections.Special Features: Fear. All creatures within 60ft of a mummy, upon sight, will suffer the effects of fear and revulsion unless a successful saving throw vs spells is made. If the save fails, the victim will be paralysed for 1d4 rounds. Groups of creatures gain a bonus of +1 for their save at a ratio of six creatures for each mummy (for example: 12 creatures in sight of 1 mummy gain a +2 to save; 12 creatures in sight of 2 mummies gain a +1, and 12 creatures within sight of 3 or more mummies gain no bonus). If humans confront a mummy, then each human will gain a +2 to their saves.
sections.Special Attacks: Mummy Rot. A successful hit by a mummy causes a wasting and rotting disease which will cause death within 1d6 months. For each month of affliction, the victim permanently loses 2 points of charisma, and while diseased no cure wound spells will have any effect and any wounds will naturally heal at a 10% rate. The mummy rot can only be cured by a cure disease spell. A character killed by a mummy cannot be raised (due to the amount of damage caused by the rotting waste) unless a cure disease and raise dead are both cast on the victim within one hour of death. Unarmed Combat. Mummies cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Naga, guardian
monsters.description: Unarmed Combat. Nagas cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics. GUARDIAN NAGA A guardian naga appears as a long, snake-like creature with a human head, golden eyes, and green-gold scales. The scales along its spine are triangular and silvery. Guardian naga are mostly found in holy places. They serve as sentinels over some ancient evil or treasure belonging to the cause of good.

sections.Special Features: Spells. The guardian naga casts clerical spells as a 6th level caster: • 1st level: 3 • 2nd Level: 3 • 3rd level: 2 Spells. A spirit naga can use divine and arcane spells to 4th and 5th levels respectively: DIVINE ARCANE 1st level: 3 1st level: 4 2nd level: 2 2nd level: 2 3rd level: 1 Spells. The water naga casts arcane spells as a 5th level magic-user: • 1st level: 4 • 2nd level: 2 • 3rd level: 1
sections.Special Attacks: Poison Bite. In addition to piercing damage, the naga’s bite is poisonous. Anyone hit by the naga’s bite must make a saving throw vs. poison or die. Spit Poison. The naga can spit poison up to 30ft at any single target (to-hit roll required), and the target must save vs poison or die. SPIRIT NAGA The evil and corrupt spirit naga dwells in deep ruins and other subterranean places. Its scales are black with blood red bands, and its human-like head is large and misshapen. Poison Bite. In addition to piercing damage, the naga’s bite is poisonous. Anyone hit by the naga’s bite must make a saving throw vs. poison or die. Gaze Attack (Charm). Any creature meeting the naga’s gaze must successfully save vs paralysation or be charmed (as per a charm person spell). A saving throw is required each time the gaze is met. This applies to anyone who is generally in front of the naga, and not using an indirect method of sight such as a mirror. Attacking the creature by looking at a reflection incurs a to-hit penalty of -2. Attacking blindly incurs a to-hit penalty of -4. WATER NAGA The water naga’s scales range from deep green to turquoise and its eye colour varies from light green to brilliant amber. It dwells deep below the surface of fresh water lakes ponds and rivers. The water naga is typically quite curious and harmless unless provoked. Poison Bite. In addition to piercing damage, the naga’s bite is poisonous. Anyone hit by the naga’s bite must make a saving throw vs. poison or die.

monsters.name: Necrophidius
monsters.description: Referred to in forbidden books of necromancy as the “death worm”, the necrophidius is a skeletal giant snake with the fanged skull of an adult human for a head. The necrophidius is a necromantic construct but is not an undead creature and cannot be turned by a cleric. There are several ways to go about creating a necrophidius. First, the basic materials must be assembled: the skull of a cold-blooded murderer who has been killed within 72 hours of the ritual, and the complete skeleton of a giant snake. The process will also require 10 days plus the services and laboratory of an alchemist, who will charge the full monthly fee plus 500 gp per hp of the completed necrophidius. At the end of 10 days, the potential owner has 24 hours to complete the ritual by one of the methods detailed hereafter. First, a magical book can be used. These work the same way as a manual of the golems (q.v.) can be used to create a golem. Second, a high-level magic-user can cast the following spells in this order upon the pre-necrophidius alchemical mixture: limited wish, geas, and charm person. Upon completion of the charm person spell the death worm magically assembles from the various parts, absorbing the fluids of the mixture. Lastly, a cleric can cast the following divine spells upon the pre-necrophidius alchemical mixture in this precise order: quest, neutralise poison, prayer, silence 15ft radius, and snake charm. As with the magic-user, when the last spell is completed the necrophidius magically assembles from the various parts, absorbing the fluids of the mixture. Because of the artificial nature of the necrophidius, they are never encountered in a lair or as a wandering monster. Instead, they are created for a specific purpose, usually as an assassin or guard. They are perfect for this role because they never sleep, they never check morale, and they never give up.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Death worms move completely silently, and surprise prey on a 1-3 on 1d6.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Necromantic Construct. This creature is necromantic but not “undead,” so cannot be turned by a cleric. Creature of Necromancy. This creature is immune to all illusions, mind control (including charm) and hold spells. It cannot be affected by sleep, gases, poison, or disease.
sections.Special Attacks: Dance of Death. This attack is a swaying, hypnotic dance that dominates the attention of anyone who fails a saving throw vs petrifaction. An individual so dominated will stand completely motionless and unresisting as the necrophidius advances and attacks. The victim does not defend (no shield or dex bonus) but is not considered fully paralysed for purposes of immediate killing. Paralytic Bite. A successful bite attack inflicts a magical paralysis upon the victim for 1d4 turns, unless the target makes a saving throw vs. paralysis. Unarmed Combat. Necrophidius cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Nereid
monsters.description: Nereids are transparent and invisible in water. On land these fey creatures appear as young, slim humans. They are playful and capricious, but a few (10%) are actually evil. An equally small number are good. A nereid will always have a diaphanous shawl containing the creature’s spirit essence. Anyone holding the shawl can control the nereid by threatening the shawl, but the nereid will use any means possible to recover it.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (50%). Any magic spell or effect has a 50% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect.
sections.Special Features: Control Water. As fey creatures, neireids can control the water of their homes, speeding or slowing swimming movement through it (up to double normal speed, or down to 25% of it), causing crashing waves that deafen, prevent conversation and interrupt spell-casting, or forming miniature waterspouts that attack as 4 HD monsters (inflicting 1d4hp damage—no more than one such waterspout per nereid per round).
sections.Special Attacks: Kiss. The kiss of a nereid can cause the recipient to drown in air and also in water. This requires a to-hit roll unless the kiss is voluntarily received. If it hits, a saving throw vs spells is required, and if the saving throw fails, the victim will drown in 1d4 rounds unless the magic is dispelled. Spit. In extremis, a nereid can attack with their spittle (range 20ft) that blinds its target for 1d12 rounds. This requires a tohit roll but no saving throw is allowed. Unarmed Combat. Nereids can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks if out of the water (this is a terrible idea since the kiss can be used while grappling). If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/ DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

monsters.name: Night hag
monsters.description: Night hags are not creatures of the material plane of existence (and are thus affected by protection from evil), being native to the neutral evil plane of Hades. They resemble hideous women with clawed hands and feet. Night hags hunt in the material planes. This “hunt” is to slay evil people, whose souls are carried back to Hades by the hag, where the soul will form into a larval fiend—a valuable commodity in the demonic and diabolical planes. If success seems likely, they will also attack any good-aligned creature. A night hag carries a special periapt forged in Hades, allowing her to astrally project her body at will. Upon losing the periapt, she can still depart the plane she is in at the time. This periapt gives the possessor +2 on all saving throws, and cures diseases the possessor contracts. With each use by a good creature, the periapt decays; after ten uses, it vanishes.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (65%). Any magic spell or effect has a 65% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immunities. Night hags are immune to charm, fear, sleep, and cold- or fire-based spells. Immune to Non-Silver Mundane, +1, and +2 Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +3 or more, or is made of silver.
sections.Special Features: Know Alignment. A night hag knows the alignment of any creature it sees. Gate. A night hag can try to gate in an ally (50% chance of success), summoning a barbed devil or class A demon (equal chance of one or the other). The expected reward is one of the hag’s larval fiends, so hags tend not to gate in allies unless they are in dire danger. Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: polymorph self, enter/exit ethereal plane (see Section 1.6.10.6: Ethereal in the Player Guide). 3/day: magic missile (2d8 damage), ray of enfeeblement
sections.Special Attacks: Sleep and Dream-Ride. Finding a victim, a night hag casts a sleep spell that affects humans (up to 12th level) who fail a saving throw vs magic, then strangles the sleeper. If the spell fails, she returns nightly while ethereal and enters the victim’s dreams, making them ethereal. Each ride until dawn by the hag (who cannot be unseated from the unfortunate’s back) permanently drains a point of constitution. When all points are drained, the victim dies and the night hag carries the soul to Hades. Unarmed Combat. Night hags can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

monsters.name: Nightmare
monsters.description: Nightmares serve as mounts for powerful evil beings. Whilst in shape they resemble large warhorses, they are unmistakably otherworldly, having blood red eyes, fiery nostrils, powerful fangs, a midnight black coat, a mane of shadow and hooves that appear to leap aflame when they run. Although most nightmares do not possess wings, they can fly through the air considerably faster than they can run along the ground. Their capacity for such swift flight is greatly valued by those they serve, as is their ferocity in combat. Nightmares hate living creatures and, being given to viciousness, will generally attack any non-evil entity they encounter. Nightmares have a strong sense of purpose and this can make them difficult to control; it takes an iron will or powerful magic for a rider to perpetually retain mastery. It is thought that their services can also be bargained for, but exactly what evil such an agreement might entail is unknown. If ridden by a creature weighing more than 100 lbs, the nightmare’s aerial agility level is reduced to III.

sections.Special Features: Smoke Aura. Nightmares give off wisps of noxious smoke, causing anyone within ten feet to make a saving throw vs paralysis or suffer a -2 penalty on “to hit” and damage rolls while in the radius of effect.
sections.Special Attacks: Flaming Hooves. A hit by a nightmare’s hooves may set flammable objects on fire. Unarmed Combat. Nightmares cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.
sections.Language: Though it is known that nightmares can understand what their riders ask of them, they are not thought to be able to speak themselves; but they seem to be able to communicate with one another well enough.

monsters.name: Nixie
monsters.description: Nixies are fey creatures, related to sprites, that make their homes in freshwater lakes. They appear as strangely beautiful humanoids with lightly scaled greenish skin and webbed hands and feet. Their eyes are silver and their hair is dark green, and they garb themselves in clothes of seaweed. Being fey, nixies take great delight in enslaving humans. Nixies are weak in combat but make up for this weakness by attacking en masse and overwhelming their enemies. They favour fighting with daggers (1d4 damage) and short spears (1d6 damage) which can be thrown. Nixies fear bright light and fire; their aquatic nature makes these things foreign to them and a strong presentation of either will drive them away. A strong light source presented underwater will be obscured by schools of summoned fish surrounding the spell effect. Nixies lair at the bottom of lakes, where they weave living seaweed into dwellings. These dwellings blend in with the underwater growth so well they are 90% unlikely to be noted until within 20ft of them. These underwater villages are guarded by either 1d4 giant gar (25%) or 2d4 giant pike (75%) which will obey commands from the nixies (see: Fish, Giant). Nixies can venture onto dry land but do so only with great reluctance.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (25%). Any magic spell or effect has a 25% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect.
sections.Special Features: Confer Water-Breathing (1/day). Nixies can confer the ability to breathe water on another being, with duration of 24 hours. Summon Fish (3/day). Nixies can summon 20d4 small fish to obstruct both an invader’s vision and movement by massing upon them. Vision is reduced to 10ft, and underwater movement is reduced by half.
sections.Special Attacks: Group Charm. If a human or demi-human approaches within 30ft of a group of nixies they will attempt to charm him or her with a special group charm spell. This charm requires a minimum of 10 nixies to join hands and chant, and any person hearing this fey chanting must save vs spells at -2 or enter the water to serve the nixies for a period of a year and a day. It should be noted: a side effect of this charm grants the ability to breathe water for the duration of the spell. There is a brief opportunity to break the charm; if a dispel magic is cast upon the enthralled person before they enter the water there is a 75% the spell will be broken, but once the victim has begun breathing water the chances of breaking the charm drop to only 10%. Unarmed Combat. Out of water, nixies can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +4/- 4. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF -2/+2.
sections.Language: Nixies speak their own language and the common tongue. They also appear to be able to communicate, at least on a rudimentary level, with freshwater fish of all types.

monsters.name: Nymph
monsters.description: Nymphs are nature spirits of almost indescribable beauty, and are always female; it is said that even the mere glimpse of one is enough to rob a mortal of their sight, or perhaps even cause death. They typically inhabit natural places of particular loveliness, such as high mountain lakes or deep forest glades. The key thing about being damaged by seeing a nymph isn’t about gender (as described in the original rules), it is about the Ancient Greek concept of disrespect to the gods. Thus, an elf (being fey) might be immune to the effect of laying eyes on a nymph. Any human—not just males—are affected by the sight, because nymphs are creatures not meant by the gods to be looked upon. Nymphs abhor evil and will occasionally aid someone in distress. A lock of nymph’s hair woven into a cloak or other item of clothing will magically increase the charisma of those who wear it by one point. Alternatively, the lock of hair may be used to create a powerful potion of sleep. Nymph tears are sometimes used in the creation of a philtre of love and any person who bathes in a nymph’s pool will have their charisma increased by two points until sundown.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (50%). Any magic spell or effect has a 50% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect.
sections.Special Features: Dimension Door (1/day). Nymphs can cast dimension door once per day. Spells. A nymph casts spells as a 7th level druid. Not to be Looked Upon. Any character that chances to look upon a clothed nymph must make a saving throw vs spells or be permanently blinded. Should a nymph be seen unclothed, then the consequence of a failed saving throw is death. The nymph can “turn off” this effect if she wishes to communicate or be seen safely. As with medusas, a mirror can provide protection from the sight of a nymph. Unarmed Combat. Nymphs can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/+0.
sections.Language: Nymphs typically speak common in addition to the language of the fey (dryads, etc.).

monsters.name: Octopus, giant
monsters.description: Occasionally a giant octopus will surface to attack a passing ship. They will attach themselves with two tentacles to the ship, leaving the other 6 tentacles free to go after the crew. When the squid has picked the ship clean it will crush the hull and drag the wreckage to its lair. If the octopus loses more than 3 arms it will release the ship and flee. As it does, the monster will release ink in the water leaving a cloud 60ft deep by 80ft wide.

sections.Special Attacks: Grab and Constrict. With a successful hit, the octopus grabs its victim and holds it. The tentacle does an automatic 2d4 points of blunt damage each round after a successful grab (only 1d4 on the initial hit). It takes one round to eat a dead victim, then the tentacle is free to attack a new target. The only way to escape is to sever the tentacle (inflict 10 hp damage to it, which doesn’t affect the creature’s total hp). When the tentacle hits, roll 1d100 to determine how well it is holding the victim. • 01-25: Both arms are held and the victim cannot attack. • 26-75: One limb is held and the victim can attack with a -3 penalty. • 76-00: Both arms are free and the victim can attack with only a -1 penalty.

monsters.name: Ogre, common
monsters.loot: Individual 4 each; in lair Hoard 2, Cache 3 (x10), Cache 5
monsters.description: Ogres are hulking creatures, nine feet tall, although they are not true giants. Their faces are more feral and less human-like than a giant’s. Ogres live in all environments, whether above or below ground. They have affinity with hill giants and trolls, and often can be found with them. Ogres love wealth, and will hire themselves out to other creatures toward this end—although ogre mercenaries tend to get badly out of hand unless tightly controlled. Left to themselves, ogres are quite primitive, but if an ogre mage or another dominant non-ogre leader (such as a necromancer or giant) is in charge, they can be quite wellequipped. In a group of 11 or more ogres, one is a leader and is slightly more powerful (attack capability equal to a 7 HD monster, 33 hit points, AC 3 [17], and damage of 2d6). Groups of 16 or greater ogres will have two of these leaders, as well as an ogre chief. The chief also attacks as a 7 HD monster, but inflicts 1d10+4 hit points of damage and has an AC of 4 [16]. When encountering ogres in their lair, the lair will contain slaves or prisoners 30% of the time. Anyone captured by ogres has a 75% chance to be eaten within a few days of captivity.

sections.Special Attacks: Weapon Damage Bonus. When attacking with a weapon, ogres inflict +2 to damage, leader-types add +3 and a chief adds +4. Unarmed Combat. Ogres can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 12+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-2. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2.
sections.Language: Despite their low intelligence, ogres are social creatures and speak orc, troll, and the language of hill giants in addition to their own language and alignment tongue. OGRE MAGE Ogre Magi are fearsome evil creatures, well versed in magic and of unnatural size and strength. They are clearly related to ordinary ogres, standing around nine or ten feet tall, with the feral face and thick muscles of a normal ogre. Unlike normal ogres, their skin colour is usually bright yellow, blue, or red. Most have two or more yellow horns, and short tusks. Though ogre magi are physically powerful, it is their command of magic that makes them truly dangerous adversaries. Ogre magi are not numerous and tend towards small groups living in castles or well-guarded and luxurious caves. Groups of 5 or 6 are led by particularly powerful individuals with 30–42 hp who fight and save as though they had 9 hit dice. These are leader-type monsters who almost always have underlings: their lairs are generally defended and often guarded by lesser beings (including normal ogres). Ogre magi speak common and ogrish, amongst other languages.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Regeneration. Ogre magi regenerate 1 hp per combat round until they are killed, at which point the regeneration stops.
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: fly (12 turn duration), invisibility, darkness, 10ft radius and polymorph self (limited to humanoid forms 4ft to 12ft in size). 1/day: charm person, sleep, gaseous form, and cone of cold as a 12th level spell caster. Unarmed Combat. Ogre magi can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 14+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-2. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2.

monsters.loot: chance of 4 magic items (any) plus a

monsters.name: Orc
monsters.loot: Individual 3 each; in lair Hoard 3, Cache 1, 3 (x10), and 5
monsters.description: Orcs are subterranean humanoid creatures, with a snout and small tusks like a wild boar. Virtually all orcs are of lawful evil alignment (see Group Alignment for Monsters). This is a reincarnating-spirit species whose form attracts lawful evil spirits for reincarnation just as the elvish form attracts chaotic good spirits. Despite the predilection for evil-aligned spirits to inhabit orcs, there are a few orcs who are not of evil alignment, because the life-activating spirit changed alignment before or after rebirth into an orcish body. These are never found with other orcs, however, because if detected they are usually immediately killed in the lawful and evil society of orcs—the inability to communicate in the group’s alignment tongue makes detection almost inevitable. The ”lawful” aspect of orcish alignment is fairly specific. First, orcs are fanatically loyal to a particular horde, “horde” being a concept which is abstract enough to gain the “lawful” descriptor. Second, they consider a strong leadership hierarchy to be absolutely necessary. Third, they consider orcs (as a species and more specifically their own horde) to be the supreme natural rulers of everything they survey. If it were not for these three points, orcs could easily be seen as chaotic. They do not form wider nations even among orcs, they have no respect for learning or non-warrior technology, and they destroy civilisations they conquer rather than assimilating them. They are “lawful” only within the framework of orcish species-superiority. Powerful non-orcish creatures (such as an ogre mage or dragon) can easily take control of orcs as long as they keep an orcish horde-chieftain in place as a puppet. Orcs love to follow tyrannical leaders as long as they are promised plunder, and as long as they seem to have authority themselves (every orc needs someone to bully). The moment they lose fear of a non-orcish supreme leader, though, they will riot or depart seeking plunder, often replacing whatever horde leader allowed them to be “deceived” by the deal they were offered. Orcs are fiercely loyal to a single horde, and these hordes are in fierce, often-violent competition. They will only unite with other hordes if there is an external force strong enough to be able to control the horde chieftains. Orcs are skilled miners and cavers. They have the ability to note new or unusual constructions underground 35% of the time, and to spot sloping passages 25% of the time. Most orcish lairs will be found underground, and those found above ground will consist of simple huts, typically with some kind of defence (ditch, moat, crude walls, etc.). Above-ground orcs prefer to sleep during the day and roam by night. Leaders Wandering orcish war–parties are led by a captain and the captain’s personal guards (3d6). These orcs fight as 2 HD creatures. They have AC 4 [16], 11 hp, and inflict +1 damage. Orc chiefs will always be encountered in a lair. The chief and the chief’s personal guards (of which there are 5d6) fight as 3 HD monsters. They have AC 4 [16], 15 hp, and inflict 2d4 damage.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Vulnerability to Sunlight. Orcs fight at -1 to hit when they are in direct sunlight.
sections.Special Attacks: Ranged Weapons. Orcs can use ranged weapons. Usually 25% of an orcish group will have short bows or crossbows. Unarmed Combat. Orcs can engage in grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 10+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/-4. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.
sections.Language: Orcs speak goblin and hobgoblin in addition to their own foul tongue.

monsters.name: Owlbear
monsters.description: These nightmarish creatures have the body of a large bear with the head of an owl. They are voracious eaters and possessed of a foul temper, fighting to the death. They are typically found in temperate forests.

sections.Special Attacks: Hug. If an owlbear scores a natural 18 or better on a hit with either of its paws, it has grabbed the victim in a crushing hug. The victim takes an additional 2d8 points of blunt damage that round and the owlbear inflicts an automatic 2d8 points every following round until the owlbear is slain. Unarmed Combat. Owlbears cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Otyugh, lesser
monsters.description: 8 HD: 650 +10/hp 12 HD: 2,300 +17/hp Otyughs are repulsive beasts that feed off the refuse and waste habitually discarded by other creatures. They are generally found in large rubbish pits and cisterns. Not always content with discards, they sometimes wait beneath the surface for anyone foolish enough to stray too close. Otyughs have no discernible head, the bulk of their form consisting of a great horn-plated torso supported by three stocky legs, with a powerful, sharptoothed maw. Three long tentacular appendages extend from their bodies, two of which are hard and thorny, being used to attack and grapple prey; the third is actually a sensory organ with three eyes at its end. Whilst Otyughs suffer no ill-effects from bright light, they do not like it, preferring to dwell in dark places that help them to strike with complete surprise, though their eyes, usually protruding above the surface, sometimes give them away.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Otyughs cannot be surprised, and surprise others on a roll of 1-3 on a d6.
sections.Special Features: Limited Telepathy. Lesser Otyughs are capable of limited telepathy at a range of up to 30ft, and Greater Otyughs up to 60 ft. Such communication is limited to simple thoughts and ideas.
sections.Special Attacks: Disease. Any character unfortunate enough to be bitten by an Otyugh may catch a disease (saving throw vs. poison negates). If contracted, the disease has a 20% chance to be fatal within 1d8 days; if it is not fatal, the patient recovers fully. Grab. Otyughs can use their tentacles for normal attacks, but may also use them to grab opponents. Grabbing an opponent only requires a successful to-hit roll, and normal damage is inflicted in that round. In later rounds, the otyugh inflicts damage automatically, but less than it might inflict by making an attack roll. Grabbed opponents suffer 1d3+1 points of blunt damage per round, and bite attacks against them are made with +2 to hit. A character with 18 strength can break free after one round of struggling, but other characters must make a successful Minor Test of Strength die roll to do the same. Grabbed characters cannot attack until freed. Greater Otyughs may also use grabbed creatures as a shield; in doing so, they gain a +1 bonus to armour class. Unarmed Combat. Otyughs cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.
