monsters.name: Pegasus
monsters.description: A pegasus is a winged horse who lives in secluded areas far from civilisation. They are intelligent, but very wild and untamed. They do not trust humans and must be approached very carefully. If they can be caught and tamed, they become very devoted mounts. They will, however, only serve a good-aligned master. If mounted by a creature weighing more than 100 lbs, the pegasus’ aerial agility level decreases to III. A pegasus is equal in size and strength to a medium warhorse. Unarmed Combat. Pegasi cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, but may choose to overbear a lone opponent. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/ DEF +5/na.

monsters.name: Phase cat (coeurl)
monsters.description: Inspired by the work of A. E. Van Vogt, phase cats (coeurls) are feline predators originating from a place alien in space or time, although probably from the prime material plane since they are not affected by protection from evil. They resemble jaguar-sized black cats with a pair of tentacles that can be used to rip at their foes. The oddest thing about phase cats is that they appear to be in a slightly different place than they actually are, making them difficult to target. Phase cats hate blink dogs, and will hunt them down and kill them if possible.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Improved Saving Throw. Phase cats make all saving throws with a +6 bonus to the die roll.
sections.Special Features: Displacement. Phase cats are out of phase with reality, and their visual appearance is slightly off from their actual location. This is already taken into account with the armour class and saving throw. Unarmed Combat. Phase cats cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.
sections.Language: Phase cats can communicate telepathically, though they use this to coordinate with each other. They seldom bother to communicate with beings other than phase cats.

monsters.name: Piercer
monsters.description: 4 HD: 80 +4/hp A piercer looks exactly like a stalactite, but it is a living creature encased in a stone covering. Piercers are sensitive to noise and heat; when they detect a source of either passing beneath them they drop, seeking to kill and devour their target. A piercer has a single attack, seeking to impale the unlucky victim with its sharp point. After killing and feasting the piercer will move via tiny cilia in its base back up to the ceiling. Any grouping of piercers will include a mix of the various HD, roll 1d4 with 1 = 1 HD, 2 = 2 HD, 3 = 3 HD, and 4 = 4 HD. A piercer will do 1d6 of damage for each of its HD. The 1 HD piercer is 3ft long and weighs about 200 lbs. With each additional HD the piercer adds another foot of length and another 100 lbs of weight. Piercers devour even the bones of their victims and any intelligent cave or dungeon dwelling denizens living nearby will often (carefully) scavenge any armour, weapons, money, magic, or anything else remaining of even the least value.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Piercers cannot be surprised, and have a 95% chance to attack with 1 segment of surprise whenever someone walks underneath them.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Cannot be Prone. Piercers are unaffected by being prone.

monsters.name: Pixie
monsters.description: Pixies are a type of troublesome fey creatures who enjoy playing tricks and generally annoying anyone who passes through their territory. They like to dwell in secluded forests. Unlike many fey, pixies to not capture humans, but they put intruders to sleep, remove their memory, and move them away. Repeat trespassers may be killed.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (25%). Any magic spell or effect has a 25% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect.
sections.Special Features: Invisibility. Pixies are normally invisible and can stay invisible even when they attack. Unless the pixie turns visible, or they are otherwise detected, opponents roll “to hit” at -4. Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: Pixies can make themselves visible or polymorph themselves at will. They are also able to create illusions with both sight and sound that do not have to be controlled. The illusion lasts until it is touched or dispelled, but they do not cause damage. 1/day: Dispel magic (as 8th level caster), dancing lights, and ESP.
sections.Special Attacks: Ranged Attack (Magic Arrows). Their bows shoot three different kinds of arrows at +4 to hit. The first type of arrow is a standard type that causes 1d4+1 points of damage. The second type of arrow causes sleep for 1d6 hours unless the target saves vs magic. The third type of arrow causes total amnesia if the target fails their save vs magic. The only way to regain memory is to receive an exorcism. A pixie’s touch causes confusion in anyone who fails their save vs magic. The confusion will last until they receive a remove curse. Unarmed Combat. Pixies cannot meaningfully be attacked in this way, and they don’t use this sort of tactic.
sections.Language: Pixies speak their own language, the language of the fey, and common.

monsters.name: Poltergeist
monsters.description: Poltergeists are undead creatures: non-corporeal, invisible spirits of humans who died a tragic death or were murdered in cold blood. So far as is known, all poltergeists were formerly human or at least half-human. They are only rarely encountered as a wandering monster but in such a case can be treated as a type 1 undead for purposes of turning or disrupting. More often, however, the poltergeist is in the area where it met its untimely end. The poltergeist’s bond to this area is strong and turning is much more difficult, treat the poltergeist as a turning a type 3 undead in this case.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Turned as Undead. Poltergeists are turned as type 1 or 3 Undead. Immune to Non-Silver Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more or is silver. Unusual Undeath. A poltergeist will not cross over sprinkled holy water, but holy water does not cause actual harm to them. Undeath. This creature is immune to all mind control (including charm) and hold spells. It cannot be affected by sleep, gases, poison, or disease.
sections.Special Features: Invisibility. Poltergeists are naturally invisible and can stay invisible even when they attack. Unless affected by a detection spell, opponents make to-hit rolls at -4.
sections.Special Attacks: Telekinesis and Fear. Poltergeists cannot physically attack. Instead, they hurl objects with a telekinetic power at their opponents (lamps, books, etc.), attacking as a 5 HD monster. Anyone struck takes no damage, but must make a saving throw vs spells or flee at top movement speed for 2d12 rounds. A fleeing victim has a 50% chance to drop whatever they were holding in their hands. Once an opponent has made a successful saving throw, they are immune to further fear from that individual poltergeist, and only for the duration of the encounter. Unarmed Combat. Poltergeists cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Portuguese man o’ war, giant
monsters.description: 4 HD: 150 +4/hp The giant Portuguese man o’war is a translucent jellyfish found in warm salt water, where it floats on the surface, trailing its poisonous tentacles below. The size is determined by hit dice: the body will be 2-1/2ft in diameter for every HD. The 1 and 2HD varieties are size small, the 3HD variety is size medium, and the 4HD variety is size large.

sections.Special Features: Transparent. Roll d100 for anyone fighting the jellyfish; if the result is 01-89, the jellyfish is treated as being invisible to that person.
sections.Special Attacks: Paralysing Sting. In addition to the base 1d10 poison damage from the sting, anyone hit by the jellyfish must make a saving throw vs. paralysis or be paralysed for 3d6 turns. Only a person immune to poison can avoid the base 1d10 points of poison damage. Paralysed creatures are drawn up to the body of the jellyfish and consumed in 3d4 turns.

monsters.name: Pseudo-dragon
monsters.description: Pseudo-dragons are tiny dragons, dark red in colour, lacking the breath weapon of their large cousins but carrying a deadly sting in their tails. They are not generally counted among the true dragons. Pseudo-dragons can be be found in almost every climate save the very hottest and coldest, and prefer snug lairs such as small caves or hollow trees. Pseudo-dragons are highly-prized familiars, and in some cases they will use their abilities on behalf of an ordinary companion of good alignment.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (35%). Any magic spell or effect has a 35% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. This magic resistance may also be extended to any ally in physical contact with the pseudo dragon, if the pseudo dragon desires. See Invisible. Pseudo dragons can see invisible creatures and objects.
sections.Special Features: Chameleon. Pseudo-dragons can change their normal dark red colouration to match their surroundings. Any person not able to see invisible creatures must roll 1d100, and on a roll of 01- 80, the pseudo dragon is treated as being invisible to that person. Limited telepathy. Pseudo-dragons are also able to communicate everything they see and hear to a companion, via a limited form of telepathy at distances of up to 240ft.
sections.Special Attacks: Poison Sting. The pseudo-dragon has a poison sting on its tail. Tail attacks have a +4 to-hit bonus but do not inflict damage. Any creature stung must save vs poison or fall into a death-like trance for 1d6 days. On the last day of the trance there is a 25% chance the victim will actually die, but if they survive, they awaken normally. Unarmed Combat. Pseudo-dragons cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Purple worm
monsters.attacks: 1 bite (2d12 piercing) and 1 tail sting (2d4 piercing+poison)
monsters.description: Purple worms are huge, almost 10ft around and 40ft to 50ft long. They live deep underground where they are constantly on the search for food. They are attracted to vibrations up to 60ft away. These creatures always return to their lair to rest. During this time, they will pass their waste consisting of metals and gems they could not digest.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Prone. This creature cannot be knocked prone.
sections.Special Attacks: Swallow Whole. On a bite attack that rolls a natural 20, the purple worm swallows the victim. If the victim is not rescued, they will die at the end of 6 rounds spent in the creature’s stomach. It is possible for the victim to cut their way out (the inside of the worm is armour class 10 [10]). For each round the victim is inside, subtract 1 from their damage that they inflict. This penalty is cumulative for each round, so after four rounds the damage inflicted is at -4. Poison Stinger. Any creature hit by the worm’s tail takes 2d4 damage and must save vs poison or die.

monsters.name: Rakshasa
monsters.description: Rakshasas are evil spirits embodied in flesh. Their main diet is humans, although they do not need to eat often. They hunt by deception: when first encountered, a rakshasa will use its ESP to gain an image of someone the victim trusts, then use illusion to assume that form. Once the victim lets their guard down the rakshasa will reveal its true self and attack.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Level-Based Magic Resistance. Rakshasas are only affected by 8th level spells and higher. Immune to Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from mundane weapons. Resistant to +1 and +2 Weapons. The rakshasa takes only half damage from magic weapons unless the weapon is +3 or better. Vulnerability. A crossbow bolt blessed by a cleric kills a rakshasa instantly if it hits.
sections.Special Features: ESP. A rakshasa can use ESP (as per the spell) at will. Spells. Rakshasas have the spellcasting abilities of a level 5 magic-user and a 1st level cleric. Unarmed Combat. Rakshasas cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks (immune to mundane weapons), and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Rat, giant, big
monsters.description: Giant rats of both size categories are vicious, opportunistic omnivores often found in ruins and upper dungeon levels.

sections.Special Attacks: Disease. Each successful bite from a giant rat has a 5% chance of causing a disease (as the cleric spell cause disease) unless the victim passes a saving throw vs poison.

monsters.name: Rat, giant, bigger
monsters.description: Giant rats of both size categories are vicious, opportunistic omnivores often found in ruins and upper dungeon levels.

sections.Special Attacks: Disease. Each successful bite from a giant rat has a 5% chance of causing a disease (as the cleric spell cause disease) unless the victim passes a saving throw vs poison.

monsters.name: Remorhaz
monsters.description: 12 HD: 3,000 +16/hp 13 HD: 3,500 +17/hp 14 HD: 4,200 +18/hp These great dragon-like creatures are found only in arctic areas. The remorhaz attacks on sight, and if encountered in its lair there is a 1 in 4 chance it has a mate and 1d3 eggs; the eggs can be sold on some markets for 5,000 gp each. The HD of the remorhaz determines its length: starting at 21ft, each hit die above 7 adds 3ft, so that a 14 HD specimen will be roughly 42ft long. The remorhaz is ice-blue in colour, with vestigial wings and odd, spiny protrusions along its back.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (75%). Any magic spell or effect has a 75% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect.
sections.Special Features: Heat-Spines. When in combat, the internal heat of the remorhaz seeps up into the spiny protrusions along the creature’s back. Non-magical weapons that strike the back will melt (although they will cause damage first), and any physical touch deals 10d10 hp damage. Sectioned Armour Class. The head of a remorhaz is AC 2 [18] and its underside is AC 4 [16]. It exposes its belly in front while attacking. Anyone not in front of the remorhaz in combat will have to attack the armoured body, which is AC 0 [20].
sections.Special Attacks: Swallow Whole. The remorhaz can swallow its prey whole on a natural to-hit roll of 20. All remorhaz generate an intense internal heat that instantly destroys any swallowed opponent unless the opponent is immune to fire damage. Unarmed Combat. Remorhaz cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Rhinoceros, common
monsters.description: Rhinoceroses are aggressive herbivores that will charge any creature they can detect. Rhinos have poor eyesight but have a very good sense of smell and excellent hearing. There are 2 common types of rhinos, single horn and double horned. Double horned rhinos are larger, having 9 HD and doing 2d6 damage. The single horn variety has 8 HD and does 2d4 damage. A woolly rhinoceros is a larger version of the rhino that roams Arctic areas of “lost world” settings, though they can also be encountered in the wild.

sections.Special Attacks: Charge. In combat a rhino will charge, doing double damage on a successful attack. Trample. Any opponent on the ground (prone) may be trampled. Roll to hit for 2 foreleg attacks (2d4 blunt damage). Unarmed Combat. Rhinoceroses cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Rhinoceros, woolly

monsters.name: Roc
monsters.description: Rocs are enormous birds of prey living in high elevations, usually in warmer environments. They will sometimes be found with giants, who keep them as pets. The immense size of a roc is accompanied by an equally immense appetite: rocs hunt for large mammals including horses, cattle, and even elephants. Any treasure found in the gigantic nest of a roc is there purely by coincidence, since rocs have no concept of wealth. The belongings of past victims will be found woven into the intricate nest.

sections.Special Attacks: Grab. If a roc hits with either of its talons, it can pick up any prey smaller than huge size, and fly off toward its nest to feed its young or devour the victim at leisure.

monsters.name: Roper, normal
monsters.description: Unarmed Combat. Ropers cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics. ROPERS Ropers are cavern-dwelling monsters and are frequently mistaken for stalagmites. These monsters are grey-green in colour, standing around 8ft to 12ft tall, with a hide that mimics the smooth limestone formations of a natural cavern. Ropers are about 3ft to 4ft at the base and approximately 1ft wide at the apex. These monsters are almost always encountered in their stalagmite shape but can alter their appearance to some degree. A roper can assume the shape of a pillar, a boulder, or flatten themselves and lie flat to appear as no more than an irregularity on the walking surface of the cavern floor. It can also cling to a cavern ceiling (or wall) and appear as a stalactite. Through means of tiny adhesive cilia on its underside, the roper can move slowly and these cilia are what allow it to cling upside down to the ceiling. Ropers are predators and attack by means of the 6 rope-like appendages that give these monsters their name. Ropers do not hoard treasure, but their acidic bile cannot dissolve platinum or gemstones. Cutting open the gizzard of a roper has a 40% chance of yielding 3d6 (3–18) platinum pieces and 30% chance of 4d6 (4–24) gems.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (80%). Any magic spell or effect has an 80% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Damage Resistance. Ropers take only half damage from electricity and cold, even if such an attack gets past the creature’s magic resistance. Vulnerability to Fire. Ropers are vulnerable to fire, although magical fire must still overcome the creature’s magic resistance to inflict damage. The roper’s saving throw against fire is at -4. Immune to Missile Weapons. Due to its stone-like skin, the creature takes no damage from missile weapons (including magical ones). Magic missile and other spells affect the creature normally.
sections.Special Attacks: Adhesive Tentacles. The tentacles of a roper are 50ft long and secrete a powerful and poisonous adhesive. A successful “to hit” roll grabs and weakens the target (no saving throw), decreasing its strength ability score by 50% (rounded down) within 1d3 rounds and lasting 2d4 turns. Multiple hits have a cumulative strength drain effect. • The victim is not prevented from attacking (arms are not pinioned), but is dragged closer to the roper by 10ft per round. • An ensnared victim can break the strand by performing a Minor Test of Strength (using the reduced strength score). • A strand can be sliced with an edged weapon but the attack must do a minimum of 6 points of damage in a single attack to the AC 0 [20] tentacle to sever it. • Creatures within 10ft of the roper are close enough for the roper to bite. The bite attack automatically hits any victim held by the strands of the roper. QUARTZ ROPERS To adventurers familiar with ropers, a quartz roper appears as a 5ft tall and 2ft wide (at the base) statue of a roper, hewn from some brownish or smoky grey crystalline mineral. The quartz roper is actually a monster with a rocky hide composed of living quartz. Quartz ropers are very sensitive to motion and are able to sense movement up to 225ft away. They do not have the magic or damage resistances of normal ropers. In combat, quartz ropers fight in the same way as normal ropers, although the quartz roper can inject a venom and the tentacles are not as strong. Treasure: A quartz roper’s gizzard has the same percentage chance of containing platinum pieces and gemstones as the standard variety of roper. Charm-Venom Injection (2/day). If the quartz roper hits with a tentacle, it can inject a strange venom twice per day. This venom allows no saving throw and causes the victim to freeze in place, looking as if they have been turned to stone. One round after this apparent petrifaction, the victim recovers, but is under the delusion the quartz roper is a close friend and valued ally. These influenced adventurers will fight to protect the monster to the utmost of their abilities for the duration of effect of the venom (10 turns). If the quartz roper is killed before the venom expires, the deluded defenders will cease attacking and wander about aimlessly until the venom expires. Adhesive Tentacles. The quartz roper attacks with adhesive tentacles as a roper does. The only difference is the ability to inject charm venom (see above) and that the tentacles are not quite as strong as a normal roper’s. An ensnared victim can break the strand by performing a Minor Test of Strength (with the reduced score) but the chance of success is doubled. Thus, if the target number for a Minor Test of Strength is 1-2, the attempt succeeds on a 1-4. If the target number is 1-3, the attempt succeeds on a 1-6 (automatically). The tentacle’s hit points for severing are the same as for a normal roper.

monsters.name: Rot grub
monsters.description: Although rot grubs can be found in animal waste and other foul refuse, they prefer to consume tissue that is still alive.

sections.Special Attacks: Burrow. Upon contact with a living being, rot grubs attempt a tohit roll, and if successful will begin to vigorously burrow deep into the body. Fire must be applied to the site of contact at once (within 3 rounds) in order to prevent the rot grub from burrowing further. This application of flame inflicts 1d6 hit points of damage per rot grub burrow. If not stopped immediately, within 1 to 3 turns the rot grub will find the heart and kill the victim.

monsters.name: Rust monster
monsters.description: Rust monsters are creatures vaguely resembling a 5ft long and 3ft tall giant, bug-like, armadillo that weighs about 200 lbs. Rust monsters have rust-red colouration on their dorsal hides and two prehensile antennae on their heads. Rust monsters are only found in underground type environments, which they prowl constantly in search of food. Rust monsters consume metal of any kind, especially ferrous metals and ferrous metal alloys. The antennae of a rust monster can “smell” metal 90ft away, and the creature will dart toward such a source of food with blinding speed, attacking the largest piece of metal it can sense. Rust monsters are motivated by blind hunger, and can be easily distracted from pursuit by dropping metal objects and fleeing; some iron spikes or a heavy mace will cause the attacking rust monster to stop for 1 round to devour the treat. Otherwise, rust monsters will relentlessly pursue the PCs until slain or all metal items have been consumed.

sections.Special Attacks: Rust. A successful antennae attack causes up to 10 cubicft of metal instantly to crumble into easily-digestible rust. The creature will immediately cease attacking in such a case and begin devouring its newly-created meal. Metal with magical bonuses gains a 10% chance per plus of not being affected by the rust monster’s attack. For instance a +3 shield would have a 30% of resisting the rusting effect. A successful “to hit” roll against a rust monster with a metal weapon automatically subjects that weapon to a rust attack. Unarmed Combat. Rust monsters cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Sahuagin, normal
monsters.loot: Individual 5 each; in lair, Hoard 9, Cache 1, 2, 3 (x10), 10, 11
monsters.description: Sahuagin are humanoid fish-people of evil alignment, much more shark-like in their appearance than the locathah. They dwell in shallow, warmer salt waters and raid villages and communities on land for loot and sport. Sahuagin have been known to tame sharks and keep them as pets. Each sahuagin realm has a King and is divided into nine provinces, each ruled by a Prince. Each Prince will have a number of Barons under his command, and each Baron controls a warband. The “Number Encountered” listing for this creature is for the lair of a typical war-band; the lair of a Prince would be much larger. If encountered outside their lair, there will be only normal sahuagin and guards. The band will be led by a warchief. Sahuagin are typically armed as follows: • Dagger and spear: 25% of the band • Dagger, trident and net: 50% of the band • Dagger and heavy crossbow: 25% of the band All these weapons are fully usable both above and below the water, which makes them quite highly prized. Priestesses The sahuagin clergy will always be led by a priestess with 6 HD and the spell casting powers of an 8th level cleric. The remaining priestesses will be trainees of 2nd to 7th level (1d6+1). Their HD are equal to their spell casting level minus 2 (minimum 2). Sahuagin priestesses will typically be attended by zombie or skeleton servants, as they are fond of the animate dead spell.

sections.Special Attacks: Ranged or Melee Attack (Net). Some sahuagin are armed with nets. These have a range of 20ft (and can be thrown while in melee combat). If the attack hits, the target is automatically (no saving throw) entangled for 1d4 rounds, unable to attack or move. Unarmed Combat. Sahuagin can engage in grappling or overbearing attacks when out of water. For a normal sahuagin, if not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

Sahuagin are typically armed as follows: • Dagger and spear: 25% of the band • Dagger, trident and net: 50% of the band • Dagger and heavy crossbow: 25% of the band All these weapons are fully usable both above and below the water, which makes them quite highly prized. Priestesses The sahuagin clergy will always be led by a priestess with 6 HD and the spell casting powers of an 8th level cleric. The remaining priestesses will be trainees of 2nd to 7th level (1d6+1). Their HD are equal to their spell casting level minus 2 (minimum 2). Sahuagin priestesses will typically be attended by zombie or skeleton servants, as they are fond of the animate dead spell.

sections.Special Attacks: Ranged or Melee Attack (Net). Some sahuagin are armed with nets. These have a range of 20ft (and can be thrown while in melee combat). If the attack hits, the target is automatically (no saving throw) entangled for 1d4 rounds, unable to attack or move. Unarmed Combat. Sahuagin can engage in grappling or overbearing attacks when out of water. For a normal sahuagin, if not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

monsters.name: Sahuagin, king
monsters.description: Sahuagin are humanoid fish-people of evil alignment, much more shark-like in their appearance than the locathah. They dwell in shallow, warmer salt waters and raid villages and communities on land for loot and sport. Sahuagin have been known to tame sharks and keep them as pets. Each sahuagin realm has a King and is divided into nine provinces, each ruled by a Prince. Each Prince will have a number of Barons under his command, and each Baron controls a warband. The “Number Encountered” listing for this creature is for the lair of a typical war-band; the lair of a Prince would be much larger. If encountered outside their lair, there will be only normal sahuagin and guards. The band will be led by a warchief. Sahuagin are typically armed as follows: • Dagger and spear: 25% of the band • Dagger, trident and net: 50% of the band • Dagger and heavy crossbow: 25% of the band All these weapons are fully usable both above and below the water, which makes them quite highly prized. Priestesses The sahuagin clergy will always be led by a priestess with 6 HD and the spell casting powers of an 8th level cleric. The remaining priestesses will be trainees of 2nd to 7th level (1d6+1). Their HD are equal to their spell casting level minus 2 (minimum 2). Sahuagin priestesses will typically be attended by zombie or skeleton servants, as they are fond of the animate dead spell.

sections.Special Attacks: Ranged or Melee Attack (Net). Some sahuagin are armed with nets. These have a range of 20ft (and can be thrown while in melee combat). If the attack hits, the target is automatically (no saving throw) entangled for 1d4 rounds, unable to attack or move. Unarmed Combat. Sahuagin can engage in grappling or overbearing attacks when out of water. For a normal sahuagin, if not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

monsters.name: Satyr (faun)
monsters.description: A satyr looks like a man with goat legs, and their heads have small goat-horns as well. These creatures are invariably male. As they are fey creatures, they are probably capable of breeding with humans and with other types of fey. Satyrs live in remote forests or meadows far away from civilisation. They are a frisky sort of fey creature, occupying most of their time with playing, flirting, and drinking. They value their privacy and will try to drive away any intruders from their domain. Satyrs have been known to ignore intruders from time to time, if given enough premium food and or wine. Satyrs will not attack physically unless they themselves are threatened. Sometimes (20%) a satyr will carry a magic weapon.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Hard to Surprise. Being nature spirits, fauns are very tuned into their surroundings and are surprised only on a roll of 1 on a d6. (See also “Invisibility in Foliage,” below).
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (50%). Any magic spell or effect has a 50% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect.
sections.Special Features: Magic Pipes. A faun’s primary defence is its magic pipes that only it can play. With it the faun can cast charm, sleep, or fear. All spells have a 60ft radius and those within range must save vs magic or suffer the effects. Invisibility in Foliage. Satyrs magically blend in with their surroundings, and each one has a 90% chance to be treated as invisible when hiding in foliage. This can be used for an ambush, but once the satyr is moving, it becomes visible unless it hides again. Unarmed Combat. Satyrs can engage in grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +1/-1. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.
sections.Language: Satyrs can speak their own language and that of the fey, as well as elven and common.

monsters.name: Scorpion, giant, big
monsters.description: Giant scorpions are vicious, fearless predators found almost anywhere. Their usual tactic is to attack anything smaller than themselves. The scorpion can use its attacks independently on 3 different targets. Anything that the scorpion kills is taken back to its lair and consumed.

sections.Special Attacks: Poison Sting. Anyone hit by the stinger of a giant scorpion must make a saving throw vs. poison or die. Giant scorpions are not immune to poison, so if one stings another it can be lethal. Unarmed Combat. Giant scorpions cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Scorpion, giant, bigger
monsters.description: Giant scorpions are vicious, fearless predators found almost anywhere. Their usual tactic is to attack anything smaller than themselves. monsters.name: Sea hag
monsters.description: Sea hags typically make their lairs beneath the ocean depths, but they are occasionally found in large lakes or other significant bodies of water. Their true form is that of a decrepit old woman, ravaged by time and repellent beyond reason, but they generally use their magic to assume a much more pleasant visage. They have sharp claws and teeth, as well as an insatiable appetite for flesh. Most sea hags are thought to be capable of speaking a number of languages.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (50%). Any magic spell or effect has a 50% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immune to Non-Silver Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more, or is a silver weapon. Cold iron weapons also affect this creature. Immunities. Sea hags are immune to charm, fear, sleep and fire- or cold-based spells.
sections.Special Features: Change Self (At Will). A sea hag can change self at will, with unlimited duration. Evil Gaze. A sea hag can employ an evil gaze up to three times per day that subjects one creature within thirty feet to a saving throw vs poison; failure results in immediate collapse and paralysis for three days, though for 1 in 4 victims the effect is stronger and causes instant death.
sections.Special Attacks: Horrific Appearance. Should a sea hag’s true appearance ever be revealed, then the horror causes anyone within thirty feet to be subject to a saving throw versus spells to avoid losing half their strength score for 1d6 turns. Unarmed Combat. Sea hags can engage in grappling or overbearing attacks if not in the water. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +6/- 6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

monsters.name: Sea lion
monsters.description: Sea lions are not to be confused with the seal-like sealion. These are fantastical aquatic beasts that could be described as a mer-lion. They have the head and front legs of a lion, but a fish-like tail instead of rear legs, and they are entirely aquatic.

sections.Special Features: Sectioned Armour Class. The sea lion’s head is AC 5 [15], but its scales protect the rest of the body better, having an AC of 3[17]. Unarmed Combat. Sea lions cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Sea serpent
monsters.description: Descriptions of sea serpents vary with the region in which they are found. Sometimes they appear as giant sea snakes and other times as dragon-like serpentine creatures with legs or flippers. What is known for certain is that a sea serpent can be encountered in any ocean, sea, or large body of fresh water. Sea serpents are very territorial but are not otherwise aggressive, only attacking when hungry. Sea serpents are capable of diving to great depths and staying underwater for long periods of time. They only lair in caves in very deep water, and tend to be solitary or, at most, a mated pair.

sections.Special Attacks: Poison Bite. The sea serpent has a poisonous bite, causing death in 1d4 rounds (save vs poison to negate). Constrict. After a successful to-hit roll, the coils of a sea serpent do automatic damage to the captured person or vessel. Creatures take an automatic 3d6 blunt damage per round. Ships are crushed in 1d6+4 rounds.

monsters.name: Seahorse, giant
monsters.description: Giant Seahorses are giant versions of the regular seahorse, not mer-horses (that’s the hippocampus). They are often trained as steeds by underwater species such as tritons.

monsters.name: Shadow
monsters.description: Shadows flitter about old ruins and dusty dungeons, seeking to feed upon the living. Due to their partial immaterialness, they can only be hit by magic weapons. Infravision does not detect them as they do not radiate heat, but magical light is sufficient to reveal these horrors for what they are. Some shadows attack victims in their sleep, giving them nightmares from which they never wake, as their physical forms are drained of life by the shadows’ horrid ties to worlds beyond mundane reckoning.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Turned as Undead. Shadows are turned as type 4 Undead. Immune to Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more. Immunities. Shadows are immune to cold damage. As undead creatures they are also immune to all mind control (including charm) and hold spells. They cannot be affected by sleep, gases, poison, or disease.
sections.Special Features: Hard to See. Shadows are nearly undetectable in their normal conditions. In any given round, a shadow has a 90% chance to be treated as invisible unless the lighting is full daylight or is magical (such as a light spell).
sections.Special Attacks: Drain Attributes. Any successful hit by a shadow causes the victim to lose a point of strength for a period of 6 turns (no saving throw). If a victim’s strength score or hit point total is reduced to zero, they become a shadow under control of the shadow that drained the last point. A character dying in this way cannot be raised from the dead. Unarmed Combat. Shadows cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Shambling mound
monsters.description: Shambling mounds are intelligent plants that appear to be walking piles of rotting vegetation. They dwell deep underground and in swamps, wherever there is ample moisture and decay. Shambling mounds will eat anything organic. They feed by wrapping their roots around prey they have killed, absorbing the nutrients as the material rots.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Resistant to Weapons. Weapons inflict only half damage to a shambling mound. Electricity Causes Growth. If a shambling mound is “damaged” by electricity, it gains a hit die. Immune to Fire. Shambling mounds are perpetually damp and immune to fire damage. Resistant to Cold. Cold-based attacks do no damage if the creature makes a saving throw, half if it fails the save. Vulnerability to Plant-Attacking Spells. Shambling mounds are considered plants for all spells that affect plants (such as plant control or charm plant).

monsters.name: Shark, 3 hd
monsters.description: Sharks are scavengers of the seas who viciously attack anything that seems wounded or dying. They are attracted to splashing, kicking, or any other sound that can be mistaken for a fish in distress. The smell of blood in the water can attract sharks from miles away. When sharks have targeted their prey, they will enter a feeding frenzy and attack everything in sight, sometimes even each other.

sections.Special Attacks: Suffocation. If both arms strike the same target within the same round, that target has become tangled up inside the creature. The victim will be smothered in 2d4 rounds unless the monster can be killed. Anyone entangled can continue to attack, but at -4 to hit and damage. Unarmed Combat. Shambling mounds cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Shedu
monsters.description: Shedu are winged bulls with human heads. They wander endlessly, battling evil and chaos. They will aid anyone of good alignment who is in need. Shedu not only travel the material plane but the ethereal and astral planes as well.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (25%). Any magic spell or effect has a 25% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect.
sections.Special Features: Spells. All shedu cast spells as a 9th level magic-user. Ethereality (at will). Shedu can become ethereal at will. Unarmed Combat. Shedus cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.
sections.Language: Shedu speak their own language, using their telepathy to communicate with others.

monsters.name: Shrieker
monsters.description: Shriekers are mobile fungi that wander around quietly underground soaking up moisture. They are the favourite food of purple worms and shambling mounds.

sections.Special Features: Shriek. Shriekers give off an ear-piercing shriek whenever they detect light within 30ft, or movement within 10ft. Shriekers will continue to shriek for 1d3 rounds, with a 50% chance to attract a wandering monster each round.

monsters.name: Skeleton
monsters.description: Skeletons are the animated bones of humans and the like, essentially mindless undead creatures. They are created by an evil (or neutral at best) magic-user or cleric, only obeying the simple commands of their animator, which is often limited by the spell itself to a score of words. Some sages warn, though, that mere proximity to great evil can animate the dead, resulting in armies of these horrors springing to unlife in forgotten catacombs and foul dungeons. Though given no commands, they seek out the living and attempt to force them into the ranks of the dead. No matter how a skeleton attacks, whether with a rusty blade, a stone, or its own former femur, it always deals 1d6 damage.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Turned as Undead. Skeletons are turned as type 1 Undead. Undeath. This creature is immune to cold, and to all mind control (including charm) and hold spells. It cannot be affected by sleep, gases, poison, or disease. Resistant to Slashing and Piercing Damage. Skeletons take only half damage from slashing and piercing damage. They take full damage from blunt weapons. Unarmed Combat. Skeletons do not engage in grappling or overbearing attacks. They can be targeted this way, but do not suffer any temporary damage inflicted. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

monsters.name: Skeleton warrior
monsters.description: Skeleton warriors are the unfortunate victims of powerful magic; in life they were fighters of great prowess and likely lords in their own right. In death they have become abominations, compelled by evil sorcery to serve any who possess the golden circlets that contain their souls. Skeleton warriors desire above all else to gain possession of their own circlet and to be revenged upon any who have possessed and used it in the past. They are generally armed and armoured with the remains of what they wore in life, or their grave goods. A character in possession of the circlet of a skeleton warrior and within 240ft may attempt to dominate it. The circlet must be worn on the attempting character’s head in order to do this; it cannot be used whilst wearing a helmet or similar headgear. On the first attempt at domination, the character has a chance of success equal to their wisdom score ×5, but they must be able to see their victim and have the freedom to concentrate for one round. If the attempt fails, it may be attempted again on the following round. If concentration is interrupted before domination is achieved, such as by an attack, the character must concentrate for a further three rounds. During this time, the Skeleton Warrior will attempt to kill its would-be master and take possession of the circlet if such is at all possible. In the event of successful domination, the skeleton warrior is rendered inert for as long as the character remains in possession of the circlet. Additionally, whenever they are within 240ft of one another and the character wears the circlet without helmet as described above, the user may take control of the Skeleton Warrior, being able to see through its eyes and direct its actions as they desire; whilst controlling the actions of the skeleton warrior, the user may not take any action. Should the user lose possession of the circlet for any reason, the skeleton warrior will seek them out and slay them, moving at double its usual movement rate. In the event that the skeleton warrior ever regains possession of its circlet, it will place it upon its head and as a result both will turn to dust. The lair of a skeleton warrior is normally a richly adorned tomb filled with considerable treasure. However, because they are usually either seeking the current possessor of their circlet or else in the unwilling service of said possessor, they are rarely found in their lairs.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (90%). Any magic spell or effect has a 90% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immune to Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more. Unusual Form of Undeath. Contrary to appearances, the skeleton warrior is not undead in the conventional sense. It cannot be turned, is unaffected by a scroll of protection from undead, etc.
sections.Special Features: Fear Aura. The appearance of a skeleton warrior is terrifying, and creatures with less than five HD who look upon it will panic and flee from its presence. Unarmed Combat. Skeleton warriors do not engage in grappling or overbearing attacks. They can be targeted this way, but do not suffer any temporary damage inflicted. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with an 18+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/ DEF +4/+1. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

monsters.name: Slithering tracker
monsters.description: Slithering trackers live in dungeons, ruins and dark places. They are transparent and if not in natural sunlight are almost impossible to see. They almost never attack their prey immediately, instead following and waiting until their target is asleep. They can follow through almost anything, being amorphous in shape and capable of seeping through tiny gaps, such as door jambs or cracks in stonework.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Ooze. This creature cannot be knocked prone, and is not affected by lack of light, invisible opponents, gases, or other circumstances that would not affect an ooze. Compressible. This creature can fit through a gap one inch wide. It can’t be restrained and isn’t affected by being prone.
sections.Special Features: Almost Invisible. If not in natural sunlight, a slithering tracker has a 19 in 20 chance to be effectively invisible. Since the tracker tries to follow its prey, this should be determined in one die roll by the GM that covers all the adventurers. Once combat begins, each adventurer may roll separately to determine if they can see the creature.
sections.Special Attacks: Paralyse Sleeping Opponent. If a slithering tracker catches its victim asleep, it will touch it, forcing the victim to roll a saving throw vs paralysation or be totally paralysed for 1d6 hours. The tracker will then feed directly on its victim’s life energy, killing it in 1 hour. Unarmed Combat. These creatures cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Slime, green
monsters.description: Green slime is an occasional dungeon hazard. Sages debate whether it is vegetable or fungoid in nature. It grows over the ceiling of an area until a pendulous bulb of slime is almost ready to drop. The vibrations from passing creatures cause these bulbs to fall. This hazard makes it a good idea for adventurers to carry open flame and cure disease spells.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Only Damaged by Fire, Cold, Cure Disease. Green slime is unharmed by weapons and most spells. It does take damage from cold and fire, and can be instantly killed by a cure disease spell.
sections.Special Attacks: Converts Flesh to Slime. If green slime touches exposed flesh, it will convert the flesh rapidly to green slime. It can also eat through wood (slowly) and metal (quickly—a metal item will be consumed in 1d6 rounds). Only stone can stop it. Failing that, a creature with green slime on it must cut away the affected area, amputate the affected limb, or die in 1d4 rounds (after which it will be converted to green slime and cannot be raised or resurrected).

monsters.name: Slug, giant
monsters.description: Giant slugs live in dungeons and other underground complexes where they can avoid sunlight. Since these creatures are boneless, they can squeeze through narrow openings and navigate around most obstructions.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Non-Magical Blunt Weapons. Because of the slug’s flexible body, non-magical blunt weapons do not inflict damage against them.
sections.Special Features: Compressible. This creature can fit through a gap one foot wide. It isn’t affected by being prone.
sections.Special Attacks: Spit Acid. Giant slugs have a nasty bite, but their most effective weapon is their ability to spit acid up to 100ft away. The first shot is almost always a miss (only 10% chance to hit), but this attack serves to approximate distance. After the first shot the chance hitting is base 100%, going down 10% for every 10ft distance from the giant slug; thus at 20ft away the chance to hit is 80%, at 70ft away 30%, etc. On a successful hit using this percentage, the acid inflicts 4d8 points of corrosion damage on an individual target unless the target makes a saving throw, in which case the damage is halved. Items exposed to the acid must also make an item saving throw on Table 1.6.4a in the Player Guide.

monsters.name: Snake, giant, boa
monsters.description: All giant snakes are carnivorous and can be found in every type of climate except for the coldest. Note: For giant sea snakes see the listing for sea serpent. Unarmed Combat. Giant snakes cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics. GIANT BOA CONSTRICTORS

sections.Special Attacks: Constrict. A boa constrictor will drop on its prey from above, coiling its long body around the chosen target victim and attacking by squeezing for 2d4 points of damage, inflicting automatic damage from the constriction (a to-hit roll is still required for the bite). Attacks against a constricting snake have a 25% chance to also damage the victim in the coils). GIANT ADDERS This is the common name for giant poisonous snakes and they come in a variety of species. Venomous Bite. The default poison for a giant adder is negated by a saving throw, but causes death if the save is failed. Some types of adders have a powerful poison which, even if saved against, causes 3d6 points of damage to the victim. Unarmed Combat. Giant slugs cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics. GIANT COBRAS These are hooded giant snakes with the ability to spit poison at a single target up to 30ft distant. Venomous Bite or Spit Venom. A successful to-hit roll on a bite or spit (range 30ft) requires a saving throw vs. death or the victim dies. AMPHISBAENA These are 6ft long snakes with a head at both ends of the body. Both heads are capable of delivering a poisonous bite. Its method of travel is as bizarre as the creature’s appearance: one head of this unusual snake will grab the neck of the other, and the creature then rolls like a hoop upon the ground. Venomous Bites. A successful to-hit roll on a bite attack requires a saving throw vs. death or the victim dies.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Cold. The amphisbaena is immune to cold damage, though the sages are at a loss as to why this is so.

Its method of travel is as bizarre as the creature’s appearance: one head of this unusual snake will grab the neck of the other, and the creature then rolls like a hoop upon the ground. Venomous Bites. A successful to-hit roll on a bite attack requires a saving throw vs. death or the victim dies.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Cold. The amphisbaena is immune to cold damage, though the sages are at a loss as to why this is so.

monsters.name: Snake, giant, amphisbaena
monsters.description: All giant snakes are carnivorous and can be found in every type of climate except for the coldest. Note: For giant sea snakes see the listing for sea serpent. Unarmed Combat. Giant snakes cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics. GIANT BOA CONSTRICTORS

sections.Special Attacks: Constrict. A boa constrictor will drop on its prey from above, coiling its long body around the chosen target victim and attacking by squeezing for 2d4 points of damage, inflicting automatic damage from the constriction (a to-hit roll is still required for the bite). Attacks against a constricting snake have a 25% chance to also damage the victim in the coils). GIANT ADDERS This is the common name for giant poisonous snakes and they come in a variety of species. Venomous Bite. The default poison for a giant adder is negated by a saving throw, but causes death if the save is failed. Some types of adders have a powerful poison which, even if saved against, causes 3d6 points of damage to the victim. Unarmed Combat. Giant slugs cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics. GIANT COBRAS These are hooded giant snakes with the ability to spit poison at a single target up to 30ft distant. Venomous Bite or Spit Venom. A successful to-hit roll on a bite or spit (range 30ft) requires a saving throw vs. death or the victim dies. AMPHISBAENA These are 6ft long snakes with a head at both ends of the body. Both heads are capable of delivering a poisonous bite. Its method of travel is as bizarre as the creature’s appearance: one head of this unusual snake will grab the neck of the other, and the creature then rolls like a hoop upon the ground. Venomous Bites. A successful to-hit roll on a bite attack requires a saving throw vs. death or the victim dies.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Cold. The amphisbaena is immune to cold damage, though the sages are at a loss as to why this is so.

monsters.name: Spectre
monsters.description: Spectres are similar to ghosts, but unlike the ethereal-dwelling ghost, a spectre is an undead spirit that dwells mostly on the negative material plane with a “shadow” in the prime material plane. If a cleric (good or evil) attempts to restore a spectre back to life via a spell or ritual, the spectre must make a saving throw or it is destroyed. Some sages speculate that spectres have no power in sunlight, but no one has ever proved this theory.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Turned as Undead. Spectres are turned as type 9 Undead. Immune to Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more. Immunities. Spectres are immune to cold damage, paralysation, and elemental spells (any spell relying on fire, water, earth, or air). Undeath. This creature is immune to all mind control (including charm) and hold spells. It cannot be affected by sleep, gases, poison, or disease.
sections.Special Attacks: Level Drain. With a successful hit, a spectre drains two levels of experience from the victim. Those reduced below zero energy levels become half-strength spectres under control of the one that stole their life-force. Unarmed Combat. Spectres cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics. SPHINXES There are four kinds of sphinx. Androsphinxes are always male, while gynosphinxes are always female. It is not clear whether criosphinxes and hieracosphinxes are related to the andro-gyno type of sphinx, or even whether these types are related to each other. Unarmed Combat. Sphinxes cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, but they may overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +6/na. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF na/na.

monsters.name: Sphinx, andro-
monsters.description: The androsphinx is a winged lion with a human head, sometimes with human head and torso (although the front arms are lion-like in this case). Like their female counterparts, the androsphinx love intellectual pursuits and will often grant access to areas they are set to guard or hoards they are watching (providing doing so does not break a prior agreement or endanger the androsphinx in any way). Androsphinxes may be “hired” (if that is the right word) as guardians for a given treasure, place or thing for a while; they are circumspect in their acceptance of such duties and payment must be made in full or they will unleash their wrath on their would-be employers upon completion of the duties set.

sections.Special Features: Spell Use. An androsphynx casts spells as a 6th level cleric.
sections.Special Attacks: Roar. Androsphinx all have the ability to emit a deafening roar that functions as a horn of blasting.

monsters.name: Sphinx, crio–
monsters.description: Less “magical” than their more human-seeming kin, the criosphinx is a winged lion with the head of a ram. These creatures simply collect treasure and hunt much as other intelligent beings.

sections.Special Attacks: On a successful to-hit roll of 20, a head-butted opponent is stunned for a single round.

monsters.name: Sphinx, gyno–
monsters.description: The storied gynosphinx is a winged half-woman, half lion creature that dwells in arid climes, amid abandoned tombs and the like. Like the androsphinx, the gynosphinx is a winged lion with a human head, sometimes with human head and torso (although the front arms are always lion-like). The chief pursuits of the gynosphinx are intellectual; their kind prefers riddles and puzzles and complex games to (almost) any other type of activity. Although basically good in nature, the gynosphinx is capricious and will not hesitate to “corner” a creature and demand some sort of payment for release (usually in the form of a song, story, a game of chess, etc.). Offers of payment in the form of material bribes are always welcome.

sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. 1/day: read magic, read languages, detect invisibility, locate object, dispel magic, clairvoyance, clairaudience, remove curse or legend lore (this last spell she greatly prefers to use as gynosphinxes can be storehouses of knowledge and pride themselves on the ability).

monsters.name: Sphinx, hieraco–
monsters.description: The dreaded hieracosphinx is an eminently evil being. A hawk-headed, winged lion, it prowls desolate places and preys on unsuspecting lone travellers or weak parties of people. Its appetite for warm flesh is nearly insatiable and it is utterly merciless in its pursuit. The creature will often toy with opponents, chasing them for league upon league through the desert under the blazing sun, and when they think they have reached relative safety, the beast will swoop down and attack with its razor-sharp beak and talons.

monsters.name: Spider, giant, big
monsters.description: Unarmed Combat. Giant spiders cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics. BIG GIANT SPIDERS Big giant spiders come in various shapes and colours. These are among the most frequently encountered denizens of dungeons and ruins. Some are jumping spiders and some spin webs, but unlike the larger types, neither characteristic is significant in game terms.

sections.Special Attacks: Venomous Bite. On a successful hit, the target of a big giant spider’s bite must make a saving throw vs. death or die, but the saving throw is made with a +2 bonus to the die roll because the venom is relatively weak. BIGGER GIANT SPIDERS The bigger variety of giant spiders resemble tarantulas. They do not spin webs because they are jumping predators. Leap. The bigger type of giant spider can leap 30ft to attack and attack in the same round. This is considered a charge. Venomous Bite. On a successful hit, the target of a bigger giant spider’s bite must make a saving throw vs. death or die, but the saving throw is made with a +1 bonus to the die roll because the venom is slightly weaker than normal poison. BIGGEST GIANT SPIDERS These creatures build webs to ensnare prey. Usually, adventurers will encounter the webs first. Venomous Bite. On a successful hit, the target of a biggest giant spider’s bite must make a saving throw vs. death or die.
sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. As hunting spiders, the bigger giant spider surprises prey on a roll of 1-5 on a d6.
sections.Special Features: Webs. It takes 2 combat rounds to break free from their webs (+1 additional round for each point of strength below 17).
sections.Language: In some fantasy worlds, giant spiders can speak Common; in others, they are voiceless.

monsters.name: Spider, giant water
monsters.description: These are like their giant land-based cousins in most respects. They differ in that they do not build webs; rather they build underwater lairs and carefully transfer air trapped in web-sacs to the lairs (they do spin silk for this purpose and to cocoon their prey). They can hide within and wait for unwary swimmers, whereupon they will scuttle out and drag their prey down, poisoning them, cocooning them, and removing them to their lair to consume. As their lairs are air-filled, if the creature is slain, these places may be used for one hour for creatures that require air to breathe.

sections.Special Attacks: Venomous Bite. On a successful hit, the target of a giant water spider’s bite must make a saving throw vs. death or die. Unarmed Combat. Giant spiders cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Spider, phase
monsters.description: The phase spider is so named because it is able to shift itself subtly in and out of reality during combat. If struck by a phase door spell, the phase spider must remain in phase for eight rounds. Becoming ethereal through magic or other means puts attackers in phase with the creature and they may strike at it with no disadvantage. The webs of this creature are highly sought after for the construction of bags of holding, etc.

sections.Special Features: Shift Phase. A phase spider can shift in phase or out of phase, at will on its initiative segment, without using an action. Once the spider has changed phase, it cannot change phase again until its next initiative. While out of phase, the spider is considered to be ethereal.
sections.Special Attacks: Venomous Bite. On a successful hit, the target of a phase spider’s bite must make a saving throw vs. death or die. The saving throw is made with a penalty of -2 to the roll (the venom is exceedingly deadly). Unarmed Combat. Giant spiders cannot effectively be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Sprite
monsters.description: Sprites are fey creatures resembling tiny humans with insect wings. They use daggers in melee, but prefer small bows (treat as a short bow, but half range and 1d3 damage per arrow). They will typically only attack evil creatures or those that blunder through their homes. Evil things will be slain, others removed in their sleep to somewhere far away.

sections.Special Features: Fey Magic. Sprites can (at will) become invisible, detect evil as per the spell, and move in complete silence.
sections.Special Attacks: Arrows. Sprite arrows are coated with sleep poison. A successful hit requires a saving throw vs poison or the victim falls into magical sleep for 1d6 hours. Unarmed Combat. Sprites are too small to be effectively targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Squid, giant
monsters.description: These monsters live deep within the oceans at depths few can reach. Occasionally they will surface to attack a passing ship. When these squid attack, they will attach themselves with two of their ten tentacles to the ship. This leaves the other eight tentacles free to go after the crew. When the squid has picked the ship clean it will crush the hull and drag the wreckage to its lair. If the squid loses more than 3 arms it will release the ship and flee. As it does the monster will release ink in the water leaving a cloud 60ft deep by 80ft wide.

sections.Special Features: Sectioned Armour Class. A giant squid’s body is protected by a tough shell (AC 3 [17]), but its tentacles and head are more vulnerable (AC 7 [13]).
sections.Special Attacks: Tentacle. Each tentacle hits for 1d6 damage. With each successful hit it grabs its victim and holds it. In addition to biting one held victim, with each successive round the tentacle does an additional 2d6 crushing damage until the victim is dead. It takes one round to eat its dead victim, then the tentacle is free to attack a new target. The only way to get a squid to release its victim is to sever the tentacle by causing 10 hp of slashing damage to it (this only damages the tentacle, not the squid). When the tentacle hits, roll 1d100 to determine how well it is holding the victim. 01-25: Both arms are held and the victim cannot attack. 26-75: One limb is held and the victim can attack with a -3 penalty. 76-00: Both arms are free and the victim can attack with only a -1 penalty.

monsters.name: Stirge
monsters.description: Stirges are bat-like flying mammals with a long, bloodsucking snout. They live in dark places and feed on blood.

sections.Special Attacks: Attacks as 4HD. A stirge attacks as a 4 hit dice creature. Suck Blood. Once it has hit, the stirge has latched on to its victim and will continue draining the victim of 1d3 hp worth of blood per round, without needing any further rolls “to hit”, until the stirge has drunk 10–13 (9+1d4) hp worth of blood, at which time its hunger is satisfied and it will attempt to depart. Only death will prevent the stirge feeding once it has latched on.

monsters.name: Stunjelly
monsters.description: Stunjellies appear, at a distance, to be no more than a normal section of wall, but should any individual stray too close, they will turn translucent and attack. Most known examples occupy an area 10ft wide by 10ft high and are 2ft to 5ft thick, but larger versions have occasionally been reported.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Stunjellies surprise on a 1-5 on 1d6 if they have not been detected before the target moves into range.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immunities. Stunjellies are immune to paralysis, as well as polymorph, electrical attacks and mind-influencing spells. They cannot be knocked prone.
sections.Special Attacks: Paralysis. If the stunjelly makes a successful hit, the target must make a saving throw vs paralysis or be paralysed for 5d4 rounds, which the Stunjelly uses to engulf its victim and begin the process of digestion.

monsters.name: Sylph
monsters.description: Sylphs are aerial fey creatures thought to be closely related to nymphs. Because a sylph’s territory is so vast it is unlikely they will be encountered anywhere near their lair.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (50%). Any magic spell or effect has a 50% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect.
sections.Special Features: Spells. Sylphs are able to cast spells as if they are a 7th level magic-user (4—1st level, 3—2nd level, 2—3rd level, 1—4th level). Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: invisibility. 1/Week: conjure air elemental. Unarmed Combat. Sylphs do not engage in grappling or overbearing attacks. They can be targeted this way. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.
sections.Language: Sylphs have their own language, speak the language of the fey, and can also understand common.

monsters.name: Tick, giant
monsters.description: These blood-sucking creatures are giant versions of the normal tick, but are 3-4ft in length. They typically dwell in ruins and upper dungeon levels, though some are found in forests as well. They usually seek to ambush their prey, jumping out from hiding.

sections.Special Attacks: Suck Blood. The initial attack inflicts the damage indicated, and thereafter the giant tick drains 1d6 hp worth of blood automatically per round (no further to-hit rolls needed). Disease. A character bitten by a giant tick must save vs poison or suffer a disease that will be fatal in 1d6 weeks. Unarmed Combat. Giant ticks cannot be effectively targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Tiger
monsters.description: Tigers are large, carnivorous and very cunning cats ranging from tropical climes to subarctic tundra. Tigers are ruthless and efficient predators, often hunting in pairs or family groups, surrounding their prey and attacking as one. Smilodons (sabre-toothed tigers) are dangerous and aggressive. These giant cats are generally found in “lost world” type areas with dinosaurs and cave men, but they are sometimes encountered in more standard (sword & sorcery) settings as well.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Alert. Tigers and smilodons are surprised only on a roll of 1 on 1d6.
sections.Special Features: Movement. Tigers can climb trees as easily as walking on the ground. Tigers and smilodons can leap 40ft to attack from hiding (treat as charge), move quietly at quarter speed in natural settings, and spring upwards a distance of 10ft.
sections.Special Attacks: Rear Claws. If both claw attacks are successful the tiger (or Smilodon) has grabbed its victim and gains two additional attacks at +4 “to hit” from its powerful rear legs (claw damage with a +2 bonus). Smilodon Bite. Smilodons have a +2 to-hit bonus for their bite. Unarmed Combat. Tigers and smilodons cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. They may choose to overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/ DEF +5/na.

monsters.name: Tiger, smilodon
monsters.description: Tigers are large, carnivorous and very cunning cats ranging from tropical climes to subarctic tundra. Tigers are ruthless and efficient predators, often hunting in pairs or family groups, surrounding their prey and attacking as one. Smilodons (sabre-toothed tigers) are dangerous and aggressive. These giant cats are generally found in “lost world” type areas with dinosaurs and cave men, but they are sometimes encountered in more standard (sword & sorcery) settings as well.
