Smilodon Bite. Smilodons have a +2 to-hit bonus for their bite. Unarmed Combat. Tigers and smilodons cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. They may choose to overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/ DEF +5/na.

monsters.name: Titan
monsters.description: Titans are powerful creatures not native to the material plane, and are therefore affected by a protection from evil spell (if it overcomes their innate magic resistance). They normally appear as massive humans, figured and possessed of an unearthly beauty. By hit die, movement rate, armour class, damage, and morale is as follows: • 17 HD: MV 210ft, AC 2 [18], DAM 7d6, Morale 130 • 18 HD: MV 210ft, AC 1 [19], DAM 7d6, Morale 135 • 19 HD: MV 150ft, AC 0 [20], DAM 7d6, Morale 140 • 20 HD: MV 150ft, AC -1 [21], DAM 7d6, Morale 145 • 21 HD MV 150ft, AC -2 [22], DAM 8d6, Morale 150 • 22 HD: MV 150ft, AC -3 [23], DAM 8d6, Morale 155 It is possible (20% chance) that a titan will be accompanied by a storm giant, for the two species are friendly with each other.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (60%). Any magic spell or effect has a 60% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immune to Mental Attacks. Titans are immune to all mental attacks (all spells and abilities affecting the mind), and may have mental powers if the GM makes use of psionics in the campaign.
sections.Special Features: Spell-Like Abilities. At Will: levitate (per the level 2 magic-user spell). 2/day: become invisible or shift into the ethereal plane. Spells. All titans have the ability to cast both clerical and magic spells. For each type of spell, roll 1d4+3. This number represents the maximum spell level the titan can cast for that type of spell. The titan can cast 2 spells of each level. Example: The die rolls result in a 4 for magic spells and a 6 for clerical spells. The titan would be able to cast 2 first level magic spells, 2 second level, 2 third level and 2 fourth level (because the die roll for maximum level of magic spells was 4). It would also be able to cast 2 first level clerical spells, 2 second level, 2 third level, 2 fourth level, 2 fifth level, and 2 sixth level (because the die roll showed 6 as the maximum level for clerical spells). Unarmed Combat. Titans cannot be effectively targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Titanothere
monsters.description: A prehistoric ruminant, the titanothere (indricotherium) looks rather like its contemporary descendant the rhinoceros. If spooked, it will charge in an effort to trample. A 2 on the “Number Encountered” roll means a mated pair; a 3 means a mated pair with a juvenile.

sections.Special Attacks: Charge. If the titanothere charges into combat and hits, it inflicts double damage. Trample. The titanothere gains an extra attack against creatures size Medium or smaller. The trample attack must roll to hit, and inflicts 2d6 hit points of blunt damage. Creatures size Large or larger cannot be attacked by trampling. Unarmed Combat. Titanotheres cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Toad, giant
monsters.description: Giant toads hunt any sort of prey, including humans. Poisonous giant toads are indistinguishable from normal giant toads.

sections.Special Attacks: Leap. Giant toads can leap forward up to 60ft and attack in the same round (treat as a charge). Venomous Bite (Poisonous Toad Only). The giant poisonous toad has a venomous bite. Anyone successfully hit by the toad’s bite attack must make a saving throw vs. poison or die. Unarmed Combat. Giant toads cannot be effectively targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Toad, giant, giant poisonous
monsters.description: Giant toads hunt any sort of prey, including humans. Poisonous giant toads are indistinguishable from normal giant toads.

sections.Special Attacks: Leap. Giant toads can leap forward up to 60ft and attack in the same round (treat as a charge). Venomous Bite (Poisonous Toad Only). The giant poisonous toad has a venomous bite. Anyone successfully hit by the toad’s bite attack must make a saving throw vs. poison or die. Unarmed Combat. Giant toads cannot be effectively targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Trapper
monsters.description: Trappers are underground predators, creatures with flat bodies like a manta ray and the ability to blend in almost perfectly with stone patterns (including flagstones). They are roughly square in shape, about 20ft by 20ft in size (larger and smaller trappers, with proportionally higher or lower hit dice have been encountered), but can alter their dimensions to a considerable degree. These dangerous creatures lie flat on dungeon floors, waiting for prey to step onto them.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Undetectable. It cannot be surprised, and has a 95% chance to surprise for 1 segment.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Resistance (fire and cold). Trappers take half damage from fire and cold, and no damage at all from such attacks if the monster is entitled to a saving throw and succeeds.
sections.Special Attacks: Enfold. When potential prey steps onto the trapper, the monster whips upward to enfold all creatures standing on it. The trapper’s stone-hard skin and powerful muscles are deadly. Victims enfolded in the trapper cannot use weapons and will suffocate in 6 rounds. Moreover, before suffocating, victims will suffer 6hp damage per round. Rescue must come from outside. Unarmed Combat. Trappers cannot be effectively targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Treant
monsters.description: 11HD: 2,750 +14/hp 12HD: 3,600 +16/hp Treants are woodland creatures, reclusive to humankind but friendly with other good-aligned creatures of the woods. They resemble humanoid trees: their “arms” and “legs” are not easily seen as such until they begin moving. Treants are vigilant guardians of the woods, despising anyone of evil alignment and all who make reckless use of fire, regardless of alignment. Damage and morale depend upon hit dice as follows: • 7–8 HD: 2d8 damage per fist; Morale 80 or 85 • 9–10 HD: 3d6 damage per fist; Morale 90 or 95 • 11–12 HD: 4d6 damage per fist; Morale 100 or 105

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Alert. Treants cannot be surprised.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Vulnerability to Fire. Treants are quite vulnerable to fire: fire attacks requiring a roll “to hit” gain a bonus of +4, a treant makes saving throws vs fire at -4, and any hit die of damage inflicted upon a treant gains a +1 to its result.
sections.Special Features: Animate Trees. Treants can animate 1d2 trees to aid them (see “Tree, Animated”) within a range of 180ft. Separate experience is not awarded for killing such animated trees. Unarmed Combat. Treants cannot be effectively targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Tree, animated
monsters.description: Animated trees are generally encountered when treants animate a normal tree (see “Treant”).

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Plant Immunities. The animated tree doesn’t need to eat, drink, sleep, or breathe as an animal would. Magic can’t put it to sleep. Gases can’t harm it, and it is immune to poison and disease. Unarmed Combat. Animated trees cannot be effectively targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Triton
monsters.description: Leader (6HD) 280 +6/hp Leader (9HD) 1,000 +12/hp Tritons resemble humans, but have two fish-like tails instead of legs. These aquatic creatures can live in any depth of water, and are found in the elemental plane of water as well as in the prime material plane. Groups of tritons are composed as follows: • 90% chance to be mounted on hippocampi (65%) or giant sea horses (35%) • Per 10 tritons, 1 leader with 4-6 hit dice (1d3+3) • Per 10 tritons, 10% chance of 1d4 tritons with magic-user ability of level 1d6. • Per 20 tritons, 1 leader with 7-8 hit dice (1d2+6) • Any number of tritons over 50, 1 leader with 9 hit dice • A triton leader (9 HD) will carry a shell horn with the following abilities: • Summon allies: 5d4 hippocampi, 5d6 giant sea horses, or 1d10 sea lions (depending upon how blown) • Disperse sea animals: all sea creatures of animal intelligence must save vs spells at -5 or flee for 3d6 turns Tritons are civilised, dwelling in castles beneath the waves (80% chance) or elaborate caverns of their own excavation (20% chance). These lairs contain additional tritons: • 60 normal triton warriors plus leaders as described above • 1 magic-user level 1d2+6 • 1 cleric level 1d4+7 • 4 clerics level 1d4+5

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (90%). Any magic spell or effect has a 90% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Unarmed Combat. Tritons cannot be effectively targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Troglodyte
monsters.attacks: 2 claws (1d3) and 1 bite (1d4+1) or by weapon
monsters.description: Troglodytes are a reptilian species that make their lairs deep underground. They have an unnatural hatred of humans, and will attack them on sight. Raiding parties (10 or more) will be led by a troglodyte that has 3 HD. War parties (20 or more) will be led by 2 troglodytes with 4 HD each. In their lair a chief will be present (a 6 HD monster) as well as 2d4 guards (3 HD creatures). Some troglodytes attack with their claws and teeth, and some use weapons that they have taken in previous battles.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise (Chameleon). Troglodytes have the ability to alter their colouration depending on the area around them. This ability allows them to surprise others on a 1–4 on 1d6. This surprise bonus does not work when they are emitting their odour.
sections.Special Features: Emit Repulsive Odour. They also have a special attack, once in combat they emit a sickening odour against which humans (as well as elves, half-elves, dwarfs, halflings, and gnomes) must save vs poison. If they fail, they lose 1 point of strength per round for 1d6 rounds. This effect lasts for 10 rounds after the last round it was active. Unarmed Combat. Troglodytes can be targeted and may engage in overbearing and grappling. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

monsters.name: Troll
monsters.description: Trolls are large creatures, shaped like humans but with long arms and legs, rubbery flesh, and a feral, misshapen face. Their crouching gait is unmistakable to those who are familiar with the species, which is known for its ravenous hunger and its most notable attribute: regeneration.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Effect of Regeneration. Trolls regenerate all damage except fire damage and corrosive damage (acid). Thus, a troll can only be permanently killed by fire or acid.
sections.Special Features: Regeneration. After three rounds of combat (even if the troll is dead), a troll’s innate regeneration ability will start working, recovering 3 hit points per round. Their ability to regenerate even allows detached limbs to reattach to their body. Severed limbs will even continue to attack foes independently. Unarmed Combat. Trolls do not engage in grappling or overbearing attacks, but can be targeted this way. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +3/-3. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2.

monsters.name: Troll, giant
monsters.description: These horrible creatures are the result of crossbreeding trolls with hill giants, resulting in a monster that looks mostly like a troll, but even larger.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Effect of Regeneration. Giant trolls regenerate all damage except fire damage and corrosive damage (acid) while they are alive. Unlike true trolls, they do not regenerate once killed. It is thus possible to kill a giant troll without using acid or fire, but the creature will be regenerating damage up until the point it dies.
sections.Special Features: Catch Missiles. Giant trolls have extremely fast reflexes and are able to snatch a missile from the air 25% of the time. If it is a missile suitable for throwing (example: spear, rock) the giant troll will throw it back as its next attack. Regeneration. Giant trolls regenerate 2 hp per round but unlike their smaller cousins, they are not capable of rebonding severed limbs, and severed limbs will not attack independently. Unarmed Combat. Giant trolls cannot be targeted with overbearing or grappling attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Troll, giant two–headed
monsters.description: Giant two-headed trolls are the vicious offspring of trolls and ettins. In appearance they look most like trolls, though they have two heads like an ettin and prefer wearing filthy animal skins as ettins do. Giant two–headed trolls are nocturnal and prefer underground dwellings such as dungeons or caverns. In combat the giant two–headed troll can direct claw attacks at two different opponents, but both bite attacks must be directed at the same opponent.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Alert. Giant two-headed trolls can only be surprised on a die roll of 1 (on a 1d6).
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Effect of Regeneration. Giant two-headed trolls regenerate all damage except fire damage and corrosive damage (acid) while they are alive. Unlike true trolls, they do not regenerate once killed. It is thus possible to kill these creatures without using acid or fire, but the creature will be regenerating damage up until the point it dies.
sections.Special Features: Regeneration. Giant trolls regenerate 1 hit point per round (except acid and fire damage) but unlike their smaller cousins, they are not capable of rebonding severed limbs, and severed limbs will not attack independently. Unarmed Combat. Giant two-headed trolls cannot be targeted with overbearing or grappling attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Troll, ice
monsters.description: An ice troll has the general form of a troll, but its cold, semi-transparent body seems to have been chiselled from blue-tinged ice. Ice trolls prefer underground dwellings such as dungeons or caverns and will always lair near running water if possible or, failing that, the wettest spot they can find.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more. Immune to Cold. Ice trolls are immune to cold damage. Vulnerability to Fire. Fire inflicts double damage upon ice trolls. Effect of Regeneration. Ice trolls regenerate all damage except fire damage and corrosive damage (acid). Thus, an ice troll can only be permanently killed by fire or acid.
sections.Special Features: Regeneration. These trolls regenerate 2 hp per round (except damage from fire and acid) and are capable of rebonding severed limbs, but only if the limb is immersed in water. A severed limb will move toward the nearest body of water if one is within 30ft. Severed limbs will not attack independently. Unarmed Combat. Ice trolls do not engage in grappling or overbearing attacks, but can be targeted this way. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/ DEF +6/-6. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +3/-3. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2.

monsters.name: Troll, spectral
monsters.description: Long ago these creatures were created in some bizarre and perverted arcane ritual, merging the life essences of a troll and some extra-planar creature. Fewer than 50 of these creatures are believed to exist and the secret of their creation process died with the creators when the spectral trolls rose up in revolt and fed upon their life energy (see “claws drain strength”).

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Resistance (30%). Any magic spell or effect has a 30% chance (at caster level 11) to have no effect on this creature; but if it does, the magic takes full effect. Immune to Mundane Weapons. This creature is immune to piercing, blunt, and slashing damage from weapons and unarmed attacks, unless the weapon causing that damage has a magical bonus of +1 or more. Effect of Regeneration. Spectral trolls regenerate all damage except fire damage and corrosive damage (acid). Thus, they can only be permanently killed by fire or acid. Immunity (Cold). Spectral trolls are immune to cold damage.
sections.Special Features: Natural Invisibility. Spectral trolls are invisible. Anyone able to see invisible will see a monster that appears very much like a shorter-than-normal troll with somewhat indistinct features and glowing amber eyes. Regeneration. After three rounds of combat (even if the spectral troll is dead), its innate regeneration ability will start working, recovering 3 hit points per round. Their ability to regenerate even allows detached limbs to reattach to their body. Severed limbs will even continue to attack foes independently.
sections.Special Attacks: Claws Drain Strength. The spectral troll has two claw attacks that subtract 1d3 points from the victim’s strength ability score as well as inflicting damage. For example: a 17 strength fighter struck for 2 hit points of damage will also be reduced to a strength of 15. Strength is recovered at a rate of 1 point every 2d4 turns. If a victim’s strength is reduced to zero they die; if strength is reduced to 1 or 2 hit points, the victim will fall comatose to the ground and will not recover consciousness until enough strength is recovered to raise the score to 3 or higher. Magic Bite. The bite attack inflicts 1d6 points of damage, but the troll adds its own hit point value as bonus damage to the attack. Example: a spectral troll with 38 hit points bites a cleric for 4 points of damage. Total damage dealt to the unfortunate cleric would 4+38 = 42. Unarmed Combat. Spectral trolls cannot be targeted with overbearing or grappling attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Turtle, giant, giant sea
monsters.description: GIANT SEA TURTLES These are massive beasts, normally placid but ferocious when they feel they are under attack. They have a 90% chance of overturning a boat, and a 10% chance to overturn even a small ship. A sea turtle can withdraw its vulnerable head and flippers into its shell, but obviously cannot attack or move if it does so.

sections.Special Features: Segmented Armour Class. The head and flippers of a giant sea turtle are AC 5 [15]. Most attacks will have to be directed at its shell, which is AC 2 [18]. Only a person directly in front of the turtle can attack its head. GIANT SNAPPING TURTLES These creatures are less massive than giant sea turtles, but they are aggressive predators, lying in wait for prey in the shallow waters of swamps, lakes, and coasts. The turtle’s lumpy shell is excellent camouflage, granting it an excellent chance to surprise passing creatures. A giant snapping turtle can retract its legs and head into its shell, but when it is thus protected it obviously cannot attack or move. Like their smaller cousins, giant snapping turtles have disproportionately long necks, and can snap at enemies as far as 10ft away.
sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Giant snapping turtles surprise on a 1–4 on d6.

monsters.name: Turtle, giant, giant snapping
monsters.description: GIANT SEA TURTLES These are massive beasts, normally placid but ferocious when they feel they are under attack. They have a 90% chance of overturning a boat, and a 10% chance to overturn even a small ship. A sea turtle can withdraw its vulnerable head and flippers into its shell, but obviously cannot attack or move if it does so.

sections.Special Features: Segmented Armour Class. The head and flippers of a giant sea turtle are AC 5 [15]. Most attacks will have to be directed at its shell, which is AC 2 [18]. Only a person directly in front of the turtle can attack its head. GIANT SNAPPING TURTLES These creatures are less massive than giant sea turtles, but they are aggressive predators, lying in wait for prey in the shallow waters of swamps, lakes, and coasts. The turtle’s lumpy shell is excellent camouflage, granting it an excellent chance to surprise passing creatures. A giant snapping turtle can retract its legs and head into its shell, but when it is thus protected it obviously cannot attack or move. Like their smaller cousins, giant snapping turtles have disproportionately long necks, and can snap at enemies as far as 10ft away.
sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Giant snapping turtles surprise on a 1–4 on d6.

monsters.name: Unicorn
monsters.description: Unicorns avoid contact with all but woodland creatures, although they may render assistance to maidens who are pure of heart, allowing themselves to be tamed as steeds.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Alert. Unicorns are never surprised within 240ft. Surprise. Unicorns surprise on a 1–5 on 1d6.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Saving Throws. Unicorns make saving throws as a level 11 magic-user. Immunities. Unicorns are immune to charm, hold, death magic, and poison.
sections.Special Features: Neutralise Poison. A unicorn’s horn negates the effect of poison, with normally the merest touch being required. Dimension Door (1/day). Unicorns can cast dimension door once per day at a range of 360ft.
sections.Special Attacks: Charge. Unicorns normally charge into battle, attacking only with their horns but for double damage on the initial attack. Unarmed Combat. Unicorns cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, but they may overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +5/na.

monsters.name: Vampire
monsters.description: The vampire is one of the most feared of the undead. Vampires must take refuge in a coffin or other hide-away during daylight, and must slumber on soil from their own grave once in a while to maintain their powers. Vampires create others of their kind by draining humans or humanoids of all life energy. The victim must be buried. After 1 day they will arise as a vampire. The victim will retain class abilities they had in life but will become a chaotic evil undead being. The new vampire is a slave to the vampire that created them, but becomes free willed if the master is killed. There is a variant type of vampire from the east, which cannot assume gaseous form at will (but will if reduced to zero hit points), nor does it have a charm gaze. However, it is invisible and foes that cannot detect invisibility suffer -4 to strike these vampires in combat.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Turned as Undead. Vampires are turned as type 10 Undead. Effect of Regeneration. Vampires regenerate all damage types, and can only be killed in one of the following ways. They are killed in 3 rounds of immersion in running water (each round reduces 1/3 of the creature’s hit points). If caught in sunlight a vampire becomes powerless and will die in 1 turn. Finally, a stake through the heart, coupled with decapitation, will destroy a vampire if holy sacraments or a blessed item is placed in the mouth after the head is removed. If a vampire is staked, it will appear to die, but unless also decapitated the vampire will revive when the stake is removed. Immune to Mundane Weapons. The vampire is immune to piercing, blunt, or cutting damage, unless the weapon causing that damage is magical. Undeath. This creature is immune to all mind control (including charm) and hold spells. It cannot be affected by sleep, gases, poison, or disease. Resistances. Electricity and cold inflict only half damage on vampires. Vulnerabilities. In addition to the effect of running water, sunlight, and turning, vampires are affected in a minor way by a lawful good holy symbol, a mirror, or garlic if they are presented with confidence. Garlic causes a vampire to cringe for 1d4 rounds, and a holy symbol or mirror will cause a vampire to take a position in which it cannot directly see the item. Holy water will inflict 1d6+1 points of damage per full vial which strikes.
sections.Special Features: Regeneration. Vampires regenerate 3 hit points per round. They can only be killed by specific methods. Shape Change. Vampires may shape change into a large bat at will, which grants them flying movement. Summon Creatures. Vampires can summon 1d10×10 bats or rats when underground or 3d6 wolves when above. These creatures will arrive in 2d6 rounds. Gaseous Form (At Will). Vampires may take gaseous form at will, and will be forced into this form if their hit points reach zero. They then attempt to reach their coffin to reform their bodies. If they do not reach the coffin within 12 turns and rest for 8 hours, they are unable to re-form.
sections.Special Attacks: Drain Life. A successful hit by a vampire drains two levels of experience from the victim, which consequently reduces all other traits linked to a loss in levels (attack ability, hit dice, etc.). Charm Gaze. Any person meeting the gaze of a vampire must successfully save vs petrifaction with a penalty of -2 or be charmed (save each time the gaze is met) as per the charm person spell. This applies to anyone who is generally in front of the vampire and attacking it or casting spells at it. Attacking the creature by looking at a reflection is not possible, because it casts no reflection. Unarmed Combat. Vampires can be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, but they are immune to temporary damage. They may overbear and might grapple under certain conditions. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +8/-8. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

monsters.name: Vilstraak
monsters.description: Vilstraaks appear as a 6ft tall cross between a human and a bug, and have hides with the consistency of heavy rock. The forearms are longer than a human’s and much more massive, ending in two heavy fists. Vilstraaks blend well with their subterranean habitat, and have an innate ability to merge with (and move through) rock. These creatures tend to lair in hollows of rock and earth. These lairs usually have entrances too small to enter without traveling through solid rock, but they can be detected and dug into if there is enough time and the right tools.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Stone Ambush. When merged with stone, vilstraaks surprise on 1–4 on a 1d6.
sections.Special Features: Travel Through Stone. These creatures can merge into stone and move through it, at half their normal movement rate. Unarmed Combat. Vilstraaks cannot be targeted with overbearing or grappling attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Volt
monsters.description: Volts are peculiar, magical creatures that attack almost anything that ventures near their lair. They appear as little balls of grey fur with two protruding eyes and a long, whip-like tail that crackles with electricity. Volt lairs usually smell slightly of ozone.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Electricity. Volts are immune to electricity and lightning damage.
sections.Special Attacks: Latch, Bite, and Shock. If the volt’s bite attack succeeds, it has latched onto its target and will do normal bite damage (1d4 hp) automatically every round. At the same time it will lash its foe with its tail (not an automatic hit). The tail attack inflicts a strong electric shock (2d6 hp damage) with a hit. Only victims not wearing metal armour receive a saving throw (for half damage), and any victim wearing metal armour is treated as unarmoured (AC 10 [10]) for the purposes of the volt’s attack. Unarmed Combat. Volts cannot be targeted with overbearing or grappling attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Vulchling
monsters.description: Vulchlings are a type of intelligent bird that resemble a vulture, but with facial features that look rather like a human with a beak. Vulchlings are weak fliers, tending to swoop upon their prey with 2 claw attacks, then fighting on the ground (where they can only bite). Vulchlings can be found in desolate areas or underground, and they have been known to ally themselves with harpies or Class A demons. Vulchlings are attracted to shiny objects and a careful search of their nest usually yields a few coins. Unarmed Combat. Vulchlings cannot be targeted with overbearing or grappling attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Walrus
monsters.description: Walruses are large, flippered animals with long ivory tusks. They are carnivorous and very aggressive in defending their territory, and are made every more dangerous due to their great size and the fact several are usually encountered. The largest males can weight as much as 4,400 lbs. In combat a walrus attacks with its clawed front flippers and its tusks. Males will primarily defend the herd from intruders but the females, who are also tusked, will fight if necessary. Treasure: The ivory tusks of this animal can be sold for 1d4+1×100 gp on the market.

monsters.name: Wasp, giant
monsters.description: Giant wasp nests may be mud-daubed or paper, depending on the type of wasp. Giant wasp wings are instantly burned away if they suffer a successful hit with a flaming object; burning away the wings in this manner does not cause hit point damage to the wasp, but prevents the creature from flying. Although giant wasps are aerial agility level V, they can hover.

sections.Special Attacks: Stinger. Giant wasps have a poisonous stinger that delivers a paralysing venom. Any creature hit by the stinger must make a saving throw vs poison or be paralysed for 1d4+1 days, followed by death. The wasps generally carry paralysed victims to their nests, where the victims are kept to be eaten by larvae when eggs hatch.

monsters.name: Weasel, giant, big
monsters.description: Big and bigger giant weasels are typically encountered in forested areas, though some may also be found in dungeons. Their pelts are quite valuable. Big weasel pelts sell for 1d6×100 gp, bigger weasel pelts for twice that amount or more.

sections.Special Attacks: Drain Blood. The bite of a giant weasel drains blood (automatic damage after the first successful attack). The drain is 1d8 hp per round for “big” giant weasels, and 2d6 hp per round for the bigger version. Unarmed Combat. Giant weasels cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and they do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Weasel, giant, bigger
monsters.description: Big and bigger giant weasels are typically encountered in forested areas, though some may also be found in dungeons. Their pelts are quite valuable. Big weasel pelts sell for 1d6×100 gp, bigger weasel pelts for twice that amount or more.

sections.Special Attacks: Drain Blood. The bite of a giant weasel drains blood (automatic damage after the first successful attack). The drain is 1d8 hp per round for “big” giant weasels, and 2d6 hp per round for the bigger version. Unarmed Combat. Giant weasels cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and they do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Whale
monsters.description: As reflected in the statistics above, there is considerable variation between different species of whales and their relative sizes. The swallow whole ability of a purple worm may be used for larger whales, if desired, rather than the automatic spit-out described here. Treasure: Whale ambergris from a single whale is worth 1d20×1,000 gp if properly collected. Whale meat is worth 100 gp per hit die of the whale. Additionally, there is a 1% chance each of finding cp, sp, ep, pp, gems, jewellery, and magic items within the stomach of a whale. Coins found will number 1d3×1,000 of the types found, gems and jewellery will number 1d20 if found, and magic items will number 1d4.

sections.Special Attacks: Swallow Whole. Whales can swallow their prey (or attackers) whole. Digestive juices from the whale cause 1 hit point of damage per turn, and the whale will disgorge prey that attack from the inside, but it may choose to do so in deep water.

monsters.name: Wight
monsters.description: Wights are undead corpses, risen with a twisted intelligence. Although they are not damaged by sunlight, they loathe the rays of the sun and do not emerge by choice from their barrows and lairs during daylight. A human killed by a wight becomes a wight under the control of its maker.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Turned as Undead. Wights are turned as type 5 Undead. Immune to Mundane Non-Silver Weapons. The wight is immune to piercing, blunt, or cutting damage, unless the weapon causing that damage is magical or silver. Immune (Cold). Wights are immune to cold damage. Undeath. This creature is immune to all mind control (including charm) and hold spells. It cannot be affected by sleep, gases, poison, or disease. Vulnerability to Raise Dead. Wights are destroyed if targeted with a raise dead spell.
sections.Special Attacks: Level Drain. The undead power of wights is linked to the negative material plane, and thus they permanently drain a level of experience from victims when they score a hit in combat. Unarmed Combat. Wights cannot be targeted with overbearing or grappling attacks, and do not use these tactics.

monsters.name: Will–o–the–wisp
monsters.description: Will-o-the-wisps are strange, fey creatures that resemble dancing lights or torches. Living in desolate and dangerous locations, they seek to draw unwary travellers into bogs or quicksand. If a will-o-the-wisp is clearly faced with death in combat, it will bargain the location of its treasure in exchange for freedom.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Magic Immunity. Will-o-the-wisps are immune to all spells with the exception of protection from evil, magic missile, and maze.
sections.Special Attacks: Electric Shock. The will o the wisp can deliver its electric shock at a range of up to 10ft.

monsters.name: Wolf, normal
monsters.description: Wolves are predators that hunt in packs of up to 30. They are normally 26 to 30 inches tall at the shoulder, and males weigh 80 to 100 lbs. A wolf pack will encircle prey, seeking to attack from behind. Once a pack has identified possible prey, they usually (75%) follow the group, waiting for the chance to attack. Dire wolves are massive wolves, prehistoric ancestors of the normal species. Like normal wolves, they hunt in packs and their howl has a 50% chance to panic herbivores such as horses.

sections.Special Features: Howl. A wolf pack’s howling may panic horses and other herbivores (50% chance per animal). Unarmed Combat. Wolves cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. They may choose to overbear a lone opponent. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/na. Unarmed Combat. Dire wolves cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. They may choose to overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +2/na.

monsters.name: Wolf, dire
monsters.description: Wolves are predators that hunt in packs of up to 30. They are normally 26 to 30 inches tall at the shoulder, and males weigh 80 to 100 lbs. A wolf pack will encircle prey, seeking to attack from behind. Once a pack has identified possible prey, they usually (75%) follow the group, waiting for the chance to attack. Dire wolves are massive wolves, prehistoric ancestors of the normal species. Like normal wolves, they hunt in packs and their howl has a 50% chance to panic herbivores such as horses.

They may choose to overbear a lone opponent. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/na. Unarmed Combat. Dire wolves cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. They may choose to overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +2/na.

monsters.name: Wolf, winter
monsters.description: The winter wolf is a large, intelligent, and bad-tempered predator which is found only in the cold wastes. Its coat is typically silver or ivory in colour, and its eyes are ice blue. Their coats are worth 5,000 gold pieces.

monsters.name: Wolverine, normal
monsters.description: Wolverines are deadly predators, resembling a cross between a huge weasel and a small bear. The creatures are just intelligent enough to be evil-aligned, and are intelligent enough to ambush prey. Giant wolverines are massive cousins to the normal wolverine, but they do not differ in terms of special abilities.

sections.Special Attacks: Blinding Musk Spray. Wolverines can spray musk in a 60ft cone, which necessitates a saving throw vs poison or the victim will be blinded for 1d8 hours. Regardless of the saving throw’s re- Breathe Frost. In addition to its bite, once every 10 rounds a winter wolf can breathe cold on all creatures within 10ft of its mouth. This icy breath causes 6d4 points of damage to the victim (half damage with a successful save vs. breath weapon). Unarmed Combat. Winter wolves cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. They may choose to overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +5/na.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Cold. The wolf is immune to cold attacks. Vulnerability to Fire. Winter wolves take an extra point of damage on each die rolled for a fire-based attack (example: a 5HD fireball inflicts +5 fire damage, which is also regardless of the wolf’s saving throw).
sections.Language: Winter wolves speak their own language, and are also able to talk to worgs. sult, the strength and dexterity scores of anyone caught in a musk cloud will effectively be halved. Improved Attack Roll. The savagery and speed of a wolverine grants them a +4 on all to-hit rolls. Unarmed Combat. Wolverines cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Wolverine, giant
monsters.description: Wolverines are deadly predators, resembling a cross between a huge weasel and a small bear. The creatures are just intelligent enough to be evil-aligned, and are intelligent enough to ambush prey. Giant wolverines are massive cousins to the normal wolverine, but they do not differ in terms of special abilities.

sections.Special Attacks: Blinding Musk Spray. Wolverines can spray musk in a 60ft cone, which necessitates a saving throw vs poison or the victim will be blinded for 1d8 hours. Regardless of the saving throw’s re- Breathe Frost. In addition to its bite, once every 10 rounds a winter wolf can breathe cold on all creatures within 10ft of its mouth. This icy breath causes 6d4 points of damage to the victim (half damage with a successful save vs. breath weapon). Unarmed Combat. Winter wolves cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. They may choose to overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +5/na.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Cold. The wolf is immune to cold attacks. Vulnerability to Fire. Winter wolves take an extra point of damage on each die rolled for a fire-based attack (example: a 5HD fireball inflicts +5 fire damage, which is also regardless of the wolf’s saving throw).
sections.Language: Winter wolves speak their own language, and are also able to talk to worgs. sult, the strength and dexterity scores of anyone caught in a musk cloud will effectively be halved. Improved Attack Roll. The savagery and speed of a wolverine grants them a +4 on all to-hit rolls. Unarmed Combat. Wolverines cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Worg
monsters.description: Worgs are evil wolves of great size. They often cooperate with goblin tribes. These malicious beasts stand 4ft to 5ft tall at the shoulder and may weigh as much as 600 to 700 lbs. Unarmed Combat. Worgs cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks. They may choose to overbear. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/na. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +5/na.

sections.Language: Worgs speak their own language, and that of goblins.

monsters.name: Wraith
monsters.description: Wraiths are insubstantial undead creatures that exist partially in the negative material plane, giving them the power to drain one level of experience when they score a hit upon an opponent. In sunlight, the wraith cannot drain levels. Wraiths are shadowy, man-like shapes, dark and indistinct.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Turned as Undead. Wraiths are turned as type 7 Undead. Immune to Mundane Non-Silver Weapons. The wraith is immune to piercing, blunt, or cutting damage, unless the weapon causing that damage is magical or silver. Non-magical silver weapons inflict half damage. Immune to Cold. Wraiths are immune to cold damage. Undeath. This creature is immune to all mind control (including charm) and hold spells. It cannot be affected by sleep, gases, poison, or disease.
sections.Special Attacks: Level Drain. With a successful hit, a wraith drains 1 level of experience from the target. Unarmed Combat. Wraiths cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Wyvern
monsters.description: Wyverns are distant cousins of dragons, extremely voracious but dull of intellect. They do not have front legs, and cannot attack effectively with their hind legs. In combat, wyverns rely on their bite and deadly poison stinger.

sections.Special Attacks: Poison Sting. If the wyvern hits with its sting, the target must save vs poison or die.

monsters.name: Xorn
monsters.description: Xorn are bizarre creatures from the elemental planes of earth that eat precious metals and other minerals. They have a rocklike consistency, granting an extremely good armour class, and appear to be made of stone. Xorn have a barrel-shaped body, radially symmetrical with three eyes, three arms, three stubby legs, and a powerful mouth set in the top of the creature’s body. The stone-like appearance grants the xorn a tremendously good chance of surprising its enemies.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Surprise. Xorn surprise on a 1–5 on 1d6.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Fire and Cold. Xorn are immune to fire and cold damage. Resistance (Electricity). Xorn take only half damage from electrical attacks (no damage when saving throws are successful). Vulnerability to Earth Spells. Xorn are particularly vulnerable to spells that affect earth and stone. Move earth spells may be used to hurl a xorn backwards 30ft and stun them for a full round. Stone to flesh and rock to mud spells weaken the xorn’s elemental structure, changing the creature’s AC to 8 [12] until the xorn concentrates for a full round to readjust its composition. Passwall spells inflict 1d10+10 points of damage. In each case described above, the xorn receives no saving throw.
sections.Special Features: Swim Through Stone. A xorn can swim through stone, but requires a full melee round to enter solid rock, during which time it cannot attack. A phase door spell will utterly destroy a xorn that is travelling through rock or readjusting its composition. Unarmed Combat. Xorn cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Yellowmusk vine
monsters.description: A yellowmusk vine is a climbing plant with strikingly beautiful amber flowers like honeysuckle blooms. It doesn’t need sunlight, instead drawing nutrients from decaying animals or plants. A mature vine covers about 20 square feet, and has 2d6 blooms and 1d4 buds. It exudes a musky, heady perfume. The plant begins its attack with a puff of pollen, causing prey to make contact, at which point the plant’s melee attack can be used.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Climbing Plant. The vine can only be knocked prone by destroying the surface or structure it’s growing on. Mindless. The vine is immune to psychic damage and it can’t be charmed or dominated. No Back. The vine can’t be backstabbed. Plant Immunities. The vine doesn’t need to eat, drink, sleep, or breathe as an animal would. Magic can’t put it to sleep. Gases can’t harm it, and it’s immune to poison and disease. Special Senses. Sight isn’t the vine’s primary sense. It can’t be blinded. Melee Attack Entwine. When a creature touches the vine, the vine produces hundreds of leafy tendrils that wrap themselves around that creature. An entwined creature can blink and speak but can’t move any other part of its body. Using this feature is the vine’s action in combat. The entwined creature doesn’t get a saving throw. Implant Seed. If the vine has entwined at least one creature, then on its initiative score, the vine can try to implant a special seed into the skull of each creature it has entwined. Invasive tendrils probe into the entwined creatures’ noses, eyes, mouths, ears, or other skull orifices. Each entwined creature temporarily loses 1d4 from its Intelligence score (roll separately for each affected creature). Using this feature is the vine’s action in combat. The entwined creature does not get a saving throw. If this damage reduces the creature to 0 Intelligence or below, that creature dies. If it reduces the creature to 1 or 2 Intelligence, that creature becomes an Amber Vine Zombie (no saving throw). All lost intelligence is fully restored after a week’s rest. It’s also fully restored if the entwined creature receives magical healing. Special Puff of Pollen. When a human, humanoid, or demi-human comes within 10ft of the vine, the vine emits a puff of pollen at it. The target creature must attempt a saving throw vs spells and other magical effects, and must add its Wisdom saving throw modifier, if any, to this roll. Creatures that can’t be charmed, and creatures that don’t need to breathe, always pass their saving throw. If the creature passes, it ignores the puff of pollen. If it fails, it’s enthralled. While enthralled, on its initiative in combat the creature must move towards the vine as quickly and directly as it can. If it’s grappled, it must try to escape. If a creature or object impedes its movement, it must walk around that creature or object, and if it can’t, then it must attack that creature or object in melee, using all its attacks if it has several, and using a hand weapon if it has one. It can’t take any other actions apart from these until the enthrallment ends. When an enthralled creature reaches the vine, it must press itself against the vine’s bark and then cease to act. The enthrallment ends on the enthralled creature’s initiative score when one or more of the following is true: 1. The yellowmusk vine has used Entwine on the creature. 2. The yellowmusk vine is dead. 3. The creature is both (a) at least 240ft away from the Yellowmusk Vine and (b) can’t see it. 4. Someone has used a cure disease, limited wish, restoration, or wish spell to end the enthrallment.
sections.Languages: None.

monsters.name: Yellowmusk vine zombie
monsters.description: Yellowmusk vine zombies are always human, demi-human, or humanoid. The zombie’s skin has an amber hue, and its eyes are glazed and lifeless. The vine zombie tries to bring creatures to the yellowmusk vine that spawned it. If the vine is attacked, the yellowmusk vine zombie will defend it. Yellowmusk zombies use whatever weapons and armour they had at the time of their conversion. They fight as 2 HD monsters with no ability score modifiers. They can’t cast spells or use ranged weapons. After about 2 months, the zombie wanders away from the parent plant to find a nice patch of soil in a likely spot, where it dies. A new yellowmusk vine sprouts from the corpse. Despite their name, yellowmusk zombies aren’t undead and can’t be turned. The only known way to cure a yellowmusk zombie is to kill the controlling creeper and cast both Cure Disease and Heal on the zombie. It takes the former zombie a month’s convalescence to return to its pre-conversion self.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Mindless. The zombie is immune to psychic damage and it can’t be charmed or dominated. Plant. This creature doesn’t need to eat, drink, sleep, or breathe as an animal would. Magic can’t put it to sleep. Gases can’t harm it, and it’s immune to poison and disease. Unarmed Combat. Yellowmusk vine zombies cannot be targeted with grappling or overbearing attacks, and do not employ these tactics.

monsters.name: Yeti
monsters.description: Yetis are tall and vaguely ape-like humanoids completely covered in thick white hair and weighing in at 300 lbs. They have ivory-clawed feet and hands, a mouthful of sharp fangs, and are known to crave the taste of human flesh. Yetis inhabit regions of ice and snow, generally in the cold regions of the world, but sometimes in areas with mountains high enough to stay snowcapped the year round. In spite of their appearance yetis are not albinos, they have eyes of pale blue or a very light, almost white, grey. Though yetis have no real use for treasure, they do realise its worth to other beings and, as such, a random collection of coins and valuables can be found in their lairs.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Invisible at Distance. Because of their colouration and habitat, yetis are virtually invisible until within 20ft of their prey, though higher–level characters have a 10% chance per level of spotting one at normal viewing ranges.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Immune to Cold. Yetis are immune to cold damage. Vulnerability to Fire. Because of their extreme adaptation to living in cold climates, yetis suffer 50% greater damage from fire damage (and heat).
sections.Special Attacks: Squeeze. If a yeti strikes with a roll of a natural 20, it grabs and squeezes the target in its powerful arms, inflicting another 2d8 points of damage (1d8 points of damage from this attack are cold damage). Gaze Attack. If surprised by a yeti, an adventurer must roll a saving throw vs paralysis. Failing the save means they inadvertently looked into the creature’s eyes and are struck with intense fright, unable to move or react during 2 surprise segments. The yeti hits automatically with its attacks (and automatically squeezes) in these two segments. The gaze has no effect if the opponents are not surprised. Unarmed Combat. Yetis may engage in grappling or overbearing attacks. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +10/-10. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +3/-3. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +2/-2.

monsters.name: Zombie
monsters.description: Zombies are the risen corpses of the dead. In many cases they have been animated by a powerful spell caster, though sometimes zombies rise from other supernatural influences. Once they begin to attack, they never flee unless turned by a cleric. Monster zombies are the animated corpses of larger humanoid monsters such as bugbears, ettins or ogres. They are harder for a cleric to turn than a normal zombie.

sections.Surprise and Initiative: Slow. These creatures shuffle slowly into combat; they are always the last creatures to attack in a melee round regardless of initiative rolls.
sections.Immunities and Resistances: Turned as Undead. Normal zombies are turned as type 2 Undead. Monster zombies are turned as type 6 Undead. Immune to Cold. Zombies are immune to cold damage. Undeath. This creature is immune to all mind control (including charm) and hold spells. It cannot be affected by sleep, gases, poison, or disease. Unarmed Combat. Zombies can be targeted with grappling and overbearing attacks (they do not initiate them, but if you want to grapple, it will grapple you right back). They do not suffer temporary damage, so this isn’t a winning strategy. If not fended off, they score an unarmed hit with a 2+ on 1d20. Hit Mods: ATK/DEF +4/-4. Overbear Results Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0. Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

Grappling Result Mods: ATK/DEF +0/-0.

monsters.name: Zombie, juju
monsters.description: Juju zombies are a particularly powerful type of zombie created by foul magics different from the normal means of creating zombies. Their eyes glow with a hellish light because they are “powered” by the negative material planes, but otherwise they resemble ordinary zombies.

monsters.name: Dread wraith
monsters.description: Dread wraiths are insubstantial undead creatures that exist partially in the negative material plane, giving them the power to drain one level of experience when they score a hit upon an opponent.

sections.Immunities and Resistances: Turned as Undead: Dread wraiths are turned as type 10 Undead. Immune to Mundane Non-Silver Weapons. The wraith is immune to piercing, blunt, or cutting damage, unless the weapon causing that damage is magical or silver. Non-magical silver weapons inflict half damage. Immune to Cold. Dread wraiths are immune to cold damage. Undeath. This creature is immune to all mind control (including charm) and hold spells. It cannot be affected by sleep, gases, poison, or disease.
sections.Special Attacks: Level Drain. With a successful hit, a dread wraith drains 1 level of experience from the target. In sunlight, the dread wraith cannot drain levels.
